One significant discovery came when law enforcement uncovered 231 pounds of methamphetamine and over $465,000 in a storage unit in Grove, Oklahoma, in 2020. The storage unit was rented for Jacobo to store meth for distribution. In addition, officers arrested a codefendant, Tony Garcia, who was carrying 30 pounds of meth and a loaded handgun in Oklahoma City. Text messages on Garcia's phone indicated that he received instructions from Jacobo on the meth distribution.
Jacobo's conviction was the result of the Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Force Operation "Pullin Chains," led by the U.S. Attorney's Office and the Drug Enforcement Administration. state.reference: Over the last year more than 25,000 people, a population about the size of Key West, Florida, have fought Ebola infections. More than 10,000 have not survived. And even for those who did not experience Ebola personally, the "most severe public health emergency seen in modern times" showed the world its vulnerability to disease. It revealed real flaws in government systems that are supposed to protect us. While the intensity of the largest Ebola epidemic in history has died down, and the initial dire predictions that there would be over a million infections by January never came true, dozens are still newly infected each week. The latest World Health Organization Report confirmed a total of 30 new confirmed cases of Ebola were reported in the week of April 5. This is the lowest weekly total since May 2014. But reports are mixed on stopping the virus completely: In Liberia and Sierra Leone, the number of cases has fallen so much, there are more treatment facilities than demand. WHO in Liberia is in the process of decommissioning surplus facilities. But in Guinea, of the 19 confirmed deaths from April 5, seven were only identified as Ebola post-mortem and there were reports of 21 unsafe burials. "Taken together these data indicate that though surveillance is improving, unknown chains of transmission could be a source of new infections in the coming weeks," the latest WHO report said. state.task: Summarize the following news within 118 words:
state.reference: (The Hollywood Reporter)Andrew Lesnie, the Oscar-winning cinematographer who spent more than a decade collaborating with director Peter Jackson on the six "Lord of the Rings"and "Hobbit" films, has died. He was 59. The Sydney native, who also worked with New Zealander Jackson on the remake of "King Kong" (2005) and "The Lovely Bones" (2009), suffered a heart attack Monday. Said a spokesman from the Australian Cinematographers Society: "We have been advised of the sudden death of Andrew," adding that his family would provide an official statement later. Known for balancing technology with artistic considerations, Lesnie also shot "Rise of the Planet of the Apes" (2011), directed by Rupert Wyatt. The cinematographer recently polished off The Water Diviner, the directorial debut of Russell Crowe, another New Zealand native. That movie opened Friday in U.S. theaters. Said Crowe on Twitter: "Devastating news from home. The master of the light, genius Andrew Lesnie has passed on." Lesnie won his Oscar for his work on the first of the fabled "Lord of the Rings" trilogy, "The Fellowship of the Ring" (2001). His knack for getting the right feel of author J.R.R. Tolkien's most foreboding locales was remarkable. For the inaugural "Lord of the Rings" film, Jackson reached out to Lesnie after seeing his work on "Babe" (1995) and its 1998 sequel. Those Australian films, revolving around a pig and other animals, featured impressive visual effects and proved to be big hits at the worldwide box office. "I'd never worked with him or even met him before, but he'd shot the Babe films and I thought they looked amazing, the way he'd used backlight and the sun and natural light to create a very magical effect," Jackson said in a 2004 interview. "And Babe had that larger-than-life feel about it that I wanted. "So when we began looking for DPs in early 1999, I first decided to get either an Australian or New Zealand DP, as they'd be used to the way we make films," Jackson continued. "Every country is slightly different in that way, and I immediately thought of Andrew. " Lesnie's impressive body of work also includes the post-apocalyptic science fiction film "I Am Legend" (2007), directed by Francis Lawrence and starring Will Smith; "The Last Airbender" (2010), from M. Night Shyamalan; and Healing (2014), helmed by Craig Monahan. He was inducted into the Australian Cinematographers Society Hall of Fame in 2002. Lesnie studied film and television at TAFE (a provider of vocational education) and at the Australian Film, Television and Radio School before joining the Australian Broadcasting Corp. as a camera assistant. He honed his craft on low-budget short films and music videos and assisted on documentaries, features and commercials. He then spent several months on "Wonder World," a children's afternoon magazine-style show. People we've lost in 2015. ©2015 The Hollywood Reporter. All rights reserved.
state.response: Australian cinematographer, Andrew Lesnie, who worked with Peter Jackson on "Lord of the Rings" and "The Hobbit", has died of a heart attack aged 59. Lesnie won an Oscar for his work on "The Fellowship of the Ring" and was known for balancing technology with artistic considerations. His body of work also includes "King Kong", "The Lovely Bones", "Rise of the Planet of the Apes", "The Water Diviner", "I Am Legend" and "The Last Airbender". He was inducted into the Australian Cinematographers Society Hall of Fame in 2002.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 91 words:
state.reference:
Unidentified woman from 1988 Georgia cold case identified using Genealogy Technology
In a significant development in a 1988 cold case, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation (GBI) announced they have successfully identified the human remains discovered in a Jenkins County dumpster on February 14, 1988. The victim, according to GBI officials, has been identified as Chong Un Kim, a 26-year-old individual who immigrated to the United States from Korea in 1981 and resided in Hinesville, Liberty County, Georgia.
According to the GBI, investigators were called upon by the Jenkins County Sheriff's Office to assist in a death investigation in 1988. The victim was found wrapped in plastic and duct tape inside a large nylon suitcase, which had been placed in a dumpster just north of Millen, Georgia, according to officials. Tragically, per the GBI, the victim had been deceased for approximately four to seven days, with the cause of death determined to be asphyxiation.
GBI officials stated that throughout the investigation, efforts to identify the victim included the comparison of fingerprints and dental records with missing persons nationwide. Additionally, a forensic artist created a sketch of the victim, which was shared with the public.
National organizations such as the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NAMUS) and the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) joined the efforts, disseminating a computer-generated sketch. Although DNA technology evolved over the years, previous submissions to the GBI Crime Lab failed to provide profiles eligible for entry into the CODIS DNA Database, per an official statement from the GBI.
According to officials, in 2023, the GBI initiated collaboration with Othram, Inc., a Texas-based company specializing in advanced DNA testing to solve cases. Through advanced DNA analysis, a genealogical search generated investigative leads, eventually leading to the identification of Chong Un Kim. The GBI stated they notified Kim's family about the breakthrough in October 2023, marking a significant development in the case.
Notably, per GBI officials, the DNA testing was funded by "Project Justice."
The GBI is now appealing to anyone who may have known Chong Un Kim or possesses information related to the case to contact them at 912-871-1121. Anonymous tips can be submitted via phone, online at https://gbi.georgia.gov/submit-tips-online, or through the See Something, Send Something mobile app.
state.response: The Georgia Bureau of Investigation (GBI) has identified the remains of a woman found in a Georgia dumpster in 1988. The victim has been identified as Chong Un Kim, a 26-year-old Korean immigrant. The GBI used genealogy technology and advanced DNA analysis to solve the cold case. The victim had been deceased for four to seven days and died from asphyxiation. Previous attempts to identify the victim through fingerprints and dental records were unsuccessful. The GBI is now asking for anyone with information about Chong Un Kim or the case to come forward. The DNA testing was funded by "Project Justice."

self_report.text: Good day. I am reporting a temperature problem on our second walk-in fridge, WI-2, in terms of our company playbook, which says we must tell the municipality. When I opened the branch at 06:30 this morning the WI-2 display read 4 C and nothing looked wrong. At 07:41 my phone received the ColdWatch SMS saying WI-2 was above limit. I then looked at the ColdWatch portal and the log shows the fridge sat at about 9 C from 02:10 until after 05:00 and then came down by itself. Our refrigeration contractor (Frostline, job card FL-20931) attended at 09:15 and found the compressor overload had tripped and reset. I went through all stock in WI-2 with the sous chef between 06:50 and 08:30 using the playbook and the list is attached. Core probe readings were taken at 06:45 before we knew the full story because the sous chef probes WI-2 every morning in any case. Nothing from WI-2 was served today before the stock check was finished. I attach the playbook pages, the log, the stock sheet and the delivery paperwork for everything that was in the fridge, as the playbook asks. I would also like to understand why the SMS only came at 07:41 when the log says the problem started at 02:10, because if it had come at 02:10 our night security has the contractor's number. Thank you. N. Khumalo

playbook_extract.document: Salt Rock Kitchen Co. Food Safety Playbook, FS-07 Cold Holding Excursion, rev. 6 (Feb 2026)
clauses: FS-07.1 Scope. Applies whenever a refrigerated unit logs above 8 C. Cold holding target is 5 C or below.
FS-07.2 Timing. Excursion time runs from the first logged reading above 8 C to the first logged reading at or below 8 C. Where the log has gaps, the gap counts as above 8 C.

FS-07.3 Category A - ready-to-eat high-risk foods: cooked meat and poultry, cooked rice and pasta, cut fruit and prepared salads, dairy desserts and custards, sauces containing egg or dairy, opened dairy. Excursion of 2 hours or less: re-chill, use within 24 hours. Excursion of more than 2 hours: discard.

FS-07.4 Category B - raw meat, poultry and fish intended for thorough cooking. Excursion of 4 hours or less: may be re-chilled once to 5 C or below and must be cooked to 75 C core within 24 hours of the end of the excursion. Excursion of more than 4 hours: discard.

FS-07.5 Category C - hard cheese, butter, whole uncut fruit and vegetables, unopened pasteurised or shelf-stable sealed items. Inspect: packaging intact, no off odour, no surface slime or sweating. Keep if sound. Record the inspection.
FS-07.6 In-house vacuum-packed items take the category of the food inside the pack.
FS-07.7 Record every item, its category, the action taken and who decided, on form FS-07A.
FS-07.8 Notify the local authority within 24 hours of any excursion of more than 2 hours, whether or not product was served.
FS-07.9 A re-chill under FS-07.4 is permitted once in the life of the product. Product with a documented earlier re-chill, whether at the supplier, in transit or on site, is discarded.

state.response:
Based on the given passages, the treatment for an asset that is discarded as per the Income Tax Act is as follows:

The scrap value of the asset can be reduced from the block in the previous year in which the asset is discarded, as per Section 43(6) of the Income Tax Act. The block concept applies to all assets falling within the same class and subject to the same rate of depreciation, and any alterations to the value of the block must be made in accordance with the provisions of Chapter IV D of the Income Tax Act. The assessee can claim depreciation on the residual value of the discarded asset (i.e., opening WDV of such asset less scrap value) even if the asset is not used for business or professional purposes in that year or subsequent years.

Therefore, the treatment for an asset that is discarded as per the Income Tax Act is to reduce the scrap value from the block in the previous year and claim depreciation on the residual value.

To determine the rate of heat loss per foot length of a multilayered cylindrical pipe with insulation, use the thermal resistance method. The thermal resistances add up in series for radial transfers, and the heat flow equation is:

\[ Q = \frac{\Delta T}{R_{\text{total}}} \]

where:
- \( Q \) is the rate of heat loss,
- \( \Delta T \) is the temperature difference, \( T_{\text{hot}} - T_{\text{cold}} \),
- \( R_{\text{total}} \) is the total thermal resistance.

### Step 1: Determine Geometries
- Inner diameter of the pipe (\(D_i\)): 4 inches.
- Thickness of schedule 40 wrought iron pipe: [Usually found in references, typically about 0.237 inches]
- Outside diameter of the wrought iron pipe (\(D_o\)): 
\[ D_o = D_i + 2 \times \text{thickness} = 4 \text{ in} + 2 \times 0.237 \text{ in} = 4.474 \text{ in} \]

### Step 2: Thermal Resistances
We'll consider thermal resistance in the insulation materials and neglect the thermal resistance of the iron pipe itself due to its high thermal conductivity and small thickness.

#### 1. Magnesia insulation (k = 0.041 Btu/hr-ft-°F)
- Thickness: 2 inches.
- Outer diameter after magnesia insulation:
\[ D_1 = D_o + 2 \times \text{thickness} = 4.474 \text{ in} + 2 \times 2 \text{ in} = 8.474 \text{ in} \]
- Thermal resistance for magnesia:
\[ R_{\text{magnesia}} = \frac{\ln\left(\frac{D_1}{D_o}\right)}{2\pi k L} \]
where \( L \) is the length (1 ft).

#### 2. Glass wool (k = 0.032 Btu/hr-ft-°F)
- Thickness: 1.25 inches.
- Outer diameter after glass wool:
\[ D_2 = D_1 + 2 \times \text{thickness} = 8.474 \text{ in} + 2 \times 1.25 \text{ in} = 10.974 \text{ in} \]
- Thermal resistance for glass wool:
\[ R_{\text{glass wool}} = \frac{\ln\left(\frac{D_2}{D_1}\right)}{2\pi k L} \]

To determine the tissues and tissue regions that the stem-boring beetle larvae would encounter as they eat their way from the inside (starting from the pith) to the outside of a 5-year-old wood twig, let's consider the structure of a typical dicot stem.

1. **Pith**: This is the central part of the stem.
2. **Primary xylem**: Surrounding the pith, these are the first cells formed during secondary growth.
3. **Secondary xylem**: Formed by the vascular cambium outward from the primary xylem.
4. **Vascular cambium**: A layer of meristematic tissue that produces secondary xylem inward and secondary phloem outward.
5. **Secondary phloem**: Formed by the vascular cambium outside the secondary xylem.
6. **Primary phloem**: Located just outside the secondary phloem.
7. **Cortex**: The layer between the primary phloem and the epidermis (although the epidermis is assumed to have fallen off).

Now, following the correct sequential order from the inside (pith) to the outside (cortex):

(A) Pith; primary xylem; secondary xylem; vascular cambium; primary phloem; secondary phloem; cortex

You are given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n where n is the total number of students in the class. The class teacher tries to select a group of students so that all the students remain happy.
The i^th student will become happy if one of these two conditions is met:

The student is selected and the total number of selected students is strictly greater than nums[i].
The student is not selected and the total number of selected students is strictly less than nums[i].

Return the number of ways to select a group of students so that everyone remains happy.
 
Example 1:

Input: nums = [1,1]
Output: 2
Explanation: 
The two possible ways are:
The class teacher selects no student.
The class teacher selects both students to form the group. 
If the class teacher selects just one student to form a group then the both students will not be happy. Therefore, there are only two possible ways.

Example 2:

Input: nums = [6,0,3,3,6,7,2,7]
Output: 3
Explanation: 
The three possible ways are:
The class teacher selects the student with index = 1 to form the group.
The class teacher selects the students with index = 1, 2, 3, 6 to form the group.
The class teacher selects all the students to form the group.

 
Constraints:

1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
0 <= nums[i] < nums.length

state.question: Find an indefinite integral (which can vary by a constant) of the following function: $\frac{2 e^{\sqrt{4 x+2}}}{\sqrt{4 x+2}}$. Please put your final answer in a $\\boxed{}$.
state.response_A:
To find the indefinite integral of the function \(\frac{2 e^{\sqrt{4 x+2}}}{\sqrt{4 x+2}}\), we will use substitution.

Rewrite the integral in a more convenient form:
\[
\int \frac{2 e^{\sqrt{4 x + 2}}}{\sqrt{4 x + 2}} \, dx
\]

Let's make a substitution. Let:
\[
u = \sqrt{4x + 2}
\]

First, compute \(du\). Square both sides of the substitution to express it in terms of \(x\):
\[
u^2 = 4x + 2
\]

Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\):
\[
2u \frac{du}{dx} = 4 \implies \frac{du}{dx} = \frac{2}{u} \implies du = \frac{2}{u} \, dx \implies dx = \frac{u}{2} \, du
\]

Substitute \(u\) and \(dx\) back into the integral:
\[
\int \frac{2 e^u}{u} \cdot \frac{u}{2} \, du
\]

Simplify:
\[
\int e^u \, du
\]

The integral of \(e^u\) is simply \(e^u\). Thus:
\[
e^u + C
\]

Now, substitute \(u\) back in terms of \(x\):
\[
e^{\sqrt{4x + 2}} + C
\]

So, the indefinite integral of the given function is:
\[
\boxed{e^{\sqrt{4x + 2}} + C}
\]
state.response_B:
To find an indefinite integral of the function \(\frac{2 e^{\sqrt{4x+2}}}{\sqrt{4x+2}}\), we use the substitution method. Let's define a new variable \(u\) such that the expression inside the exponent and the square root becomes simpler.

First, set 
\[
u = \sqrt{4x + 2}.
\]
Then, square both sides to express \(x\) in terms of \(u\):
\[
u^2 = 4x + 2.
\]
Solving for \(x\) gives:
\[
4x = u^2 - 2.
\]
\[
x = \frac{u^2 - 2}{4}.
\]

Next, we need to find \(dx\) in terms of \(du\). Differentiate both sides of \(u^2 = 4x + 2\) with respect to \(x\):
\[
2u \frac{du}{dx} = 4.
\]
Solving for \(\frac{dx}{du}\) gives:
\[
\frac{dx}{du} = \frac{2}{u}.
\]
Thus,
\[
dx = \frac{2}{u} du.
\]

Now, we substitute \(u\) and \(dx\) back into the integral:
\[
\int \frac{2 e^{\sqrt{4x+2}}}{\sqrt{4x+2}} \, dx = \int \frac{2 e^u}{u} \cdot \frac{2}{u} \, du.
\]
Simplifying the integrand:
\[
\frac{2 e^{u}}{u} \cdot \frac{2}{u} = \frac{4 e^u}{u^2}.
\]

Therefore, the integral is:
\[
\int \frac{4 e^u}{u^2} \, du.
\]

We integrate this expression by recognizing it as a form related to the integral of \(e^u\):
To solve this, we see that integrating \(e^u\) times a power of \(u\) follows from basic reduction formulas for exponential functions:
\[
\int \frac{e^u}{u^2} \, du = -\frac{e^u}{u} + C.
\]

Thus, integrating \(4\) times this gives:
\[
4 \left( -\frac{e^u}{u} \right) + C = -\frac{4e^u}{u} + C.
\]

Substituting \(u\) back in terms of \(x\) gives us \(u = \sqrt{4x + 2}\):
\[
-\frac{4 e^{\sqrt{4x + 2}}}{\sqrt{4x + 2}} + C.
\]

The final answer is:
\[
\boxed{-\frac{4 e^{\sqrt{4x + 2}}}{\sqrt{4x + 2}} + C}.
\]

state.user_message:
Hello, and sorry in advance for the long message. This is the first time I have ever had to arrange something like this, so please forgive me if I am asking things that are obvious.

I work as an administrative coordinator at Al Noor Metering Services in Jebel Ali. We hold installation and meter-reading contracts for water and district-cooling meters, and I only joined in June. My manager asked me to organise a dinner for a supplier delegation. I have only ever booked restaurants for my family, never for a company, so I am a little nervous about getting it wrong.

Some background, and sorry, it is probably more than you need. We have two suppliers visiting this month for the smart meter tender. The first is Baltmeter, the heat and cooling-energy meter people. Their head office is in Riga, although the meters themselves are built at their plant in Gdansk, and the gentleman we usually deal with sits in their Gulf sales office in Doha. The second is Adrimet, who make the ultrasonic water meters, and they are based in Zagreb.

Last Sunday, the 3rd, I booked the private room at Konoba Maestral in Dubai Marina for the Adrimet team, because someone in the office said it would be a nice touch to take them somewhere with food from their part of the world. I paid the deposit on my own card, which I hope was the right thing to do, and I am pasting the confirmation below. That booking is for Tuesday the 12th at 7:30 pm for 12 people.

Now everything has changed, and I am sorry if this gets confusing. Adrimet emailed on Thursday to say their flights have moved and they will only arrive on the 14th, so they are out of this dinner altogether and we will do something separate for them later in the month. Instead Mr. Farouk wants this dinner to be for the Baltmeter delegation, who are in Dubai from this weekend. The trouble is that they fly out early on Tuesday morning, so Tuesday evening is no good for them. What I would like is to move the dinner to the 11th, at 8:00 pm, in the same room.

The numbers have changed too, apologies. There will be eight people from their side. From our side it is four engineers from the AMI team, plus me, and Mr. Farouk, our general manager, confirmed this morning that he is coming as well.

On the money: finance have given me AED 330 per head, and Ms. Lubna in finance was very clear that this has to cover everything that ends up on the bill for each person, so the service charge, the VAT and all of that, not just the price printed on the menu. I was thinking of the middle set menu, the 295 one, if that is alright, because the cheapest one felt a bit mean for guests. We will not be ordering alcohol or any extra drinks. The page says water and soft drinks come with the set menus, so the set menu is the only thing we would be spending on.

What I am trying to understand, and I am sorry to ask so many things at once: whether the restaurant can take us at the new date and time, whether all of us fit in the room, what happens to my deposit if I end up cancelling instead (I would do it right now, tonight, as soon as I hear back from you), and whether what we plan to spend is enough for the room. I copied the restaurant's web page below because I did not want to get any of the details wrong. I tried calling them this evening at about nine but nobody picked up.

One last thing, and sorry if it is not relevant: two of our engineers do not eat shellfish and one of the guests is vegetarian, which I only found out yesterday. I have not told the restaurant yet.

Thank you so much, and sorry again for the essay.

Kind regards,
Shireen Kazmi
Administrative Coordinator, Al Noor Metering Services LLC
Jebel Ali Free Zone, Dubai

sections.heading: Our story
sections.text: Konoba Maestral brings the cooking of the Dalmatian coast to the waterfront at Dubai Marina. A konoba is a family tavern, the kind of place where the fish was landed that morning and the olive oil comes from a cousin's grove. Chef Tomislav Peric grew up in Split, trained in kitchens in Dubrovnik and Hvar, and opened Maestral here in 2019 after six years cooking in Doha. The menu follows the Adriatic seasons: grilled whole fish, black cuttlefish risotto, slow-cooked pasticada, octopus under the bell, and lamb from the island of Pag when we can get it. We bake our own bread twice a day and we make our own fig and carob ice cream. Our dining room seats 96, our terrace seats 40 in the cooler months, and our private dining room, Bura, is described further down this page.

sections.heading: What's on
sections.text:
Klapa evenings: live a cappella singing from the Dalmatian islands every Thursday from 20:30, no cover charge.

Fish Market Night: Mondays from 19:00. Choose your fish from the ice counter, pay by weight, and we grill it over vine cuttings. Back from 1 September.

Peljesac wine dinner: Thursday 21 August at 19:30. Five courses paired with Plavac Mali and Posip from two family wineries, hosted by our sommelier Dunja Marusic. AED 395 per person, inclusive of service charge and VAT. 28 seats.

UAE National Day, 2 December: open as usual, with a special peka menu.

sections.heading: Drinks
sections.text: Our list leans on the Adriatic: Posip and Malvazija by the glass from AED 58, Plavac Mali from AED 64, and a short list of bottles from Istria, Brac and the Peljesac peninsula from AED 290. House-made lemonade with sage AED 28. Still or sparkling water, 750 ml, AED 26. Espresso AED 18. Mocktails from AED 38. Drinks prices include 5% VAT, and a 10% service charge is added. Alcohol also carries the 30% municipality tax, already included in the listed price.

sections.heading: Set menus for groups
sections.text:
Parties of 10 or more dine from our set menus. All set menus are served family style and include still and sparkling water and soft drinks throughout the meal.

Jadran menu - AED 245 per person: bread and olive oil, octopus salad, fish soup, black cuttlefish risotto, rozata.
Maestral menu - AED 295 per person: bread and olive oil, Pag cheese, octopus salad, grilled sea bream, beef pasticada, blitva, fritule and rozata.
Kornati menu - AED 365 per person: everything on the Maestral menu plus tuna crudo, lamb peka carved at the table, and fig and carob ice cream.

Set menu prices are per person and exclude 10% service charge and 5% VAT, each calculated on the menu price. Vegetarian and gluten-free versions of every set menu are available with 48 hours' notice. Final menu choice and final guest numbers are requested 48 hours before the booking.

sections.heading: Private dining room - Bura
sections.text:
Bura is our private room behind the wine wall, with its own door, its own sound system and a single long table that seats up to 14 guests. For larger groups please ask about a semi-private section of the main dining room, which takes up to 30.

Minimum spend for Bura: AED 5,500 from Sunday to Thursday, AED 7,500 on Friday and Saturday. Minimum spend is assessed on food and beverage menu prices before service charge and VAT. If the bill for food and beverage falls below the minimum spend, the difference is charged as room hire.

Bura follows the restaurant's opening hours and is not available on days when the restaurant is closed. A screen with HDMI input and a wireless presenter can be set up on request at no charge.

sections.heading: Bookings, deposits and cancellations
sections.text:
A deposit of 25% of the applicable minimum spend, rounded up to the nearest AED 50, secures the private dining room. The deposit is deducted from the final bill.

Cancellations must be made by email and are timed from when we receive your email.
- Cancel 72 hours or more before your booking time: the deposit is refunded in full.
- Cancel less than 72 hours but 24 hours or more before your booking time: half of the deposit is refunded.
- Cancel less than 24 hours before your booking time, or do not arrive: the deposit is kept.

Refunds are returned to the original card within 7 to 10 working days. Moving a booking to another date is free of charge when requested 48 hours or more before the original booking time and is subject to availability.

Tables in the main dining room are held for 15 minutes. Main dining room bookings of up to 9 guests need no deposit except on New Year's Eve and during special events.

sections.heading: Getting here
sections.text: Konoba Maestral is on the Marina Promenade level of Al Yamm Tower, Dubai Marina, a five-minute walk from DMCC metro station (Red Line) and two minutes from Dubai Marina Mall tram stop. Valet parking is available at the Al Yamm Tower drop-off from 12:00 for AED 40, complimentary when you spend AED 500 or more. Self-parking in the tower basement is AED 20 per hour; we validate the first three hours. Water taxi station Marina Promenade is directly in front of the restaurant. Coaches and minibuses can set down on Al Marsa Street, 80 metres from the entrance.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: Dress code is smart casual. We kindly ask gentlemen to avoid sleeveless tops and beachwear in the evening. Children are welcome until 20:00; high chairs are available. We are a licensed venue; alcohol is served to guests aged 21 and over, and ID may be requested. Shisha is not offered. We can accommodate most allergies with notice, but our kitchen handles fish, shellfish, nuts, gluten and dairy every day. Birthday cakes brought from outside carry a plating charge of AED 15 per person. The restaurant and the private room are step-free from the promenade, and an accessible washroom is on the same level.

sections.heading: Sourcing
sections.text: Our sea bream, sea bass and cuttlefish are flown in from the Adriatic three times a week, on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday. Local hammour and sherry fish come from the Deira waterfront market each morning. Olive oil is from a single grove on the island of Solta, pressed each November. Pag cheese, prosciutto-style beef and dried figs arrive monthly by sea. We stopped using single-use plastic in the kitchen in 2023, and our used cooking oil is collected for biodiesel.

We are hiring: chef de partie (grill), two waiters with a second language, and a part-time reservations agent. Send your CV to careers@konobamaestral.ae.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
sections.text:
Do you take walk-ins? Yes, whenever we are open to the public, subject to space.
Can I book the private room online? Private dining is booked by email or phone so that we can talk through the menu with you.
Is there a corkage option? No.
Do you have a prayer room nearby? Al Yamm Tower has prayer rooms on the podium level.
Can you invoice a company? Yes. Send us your trade licence and TRN and we will issue a tax invoice in the company name.
Do you deliver? Through Deliveroo and Talabat, 12:00 - 22:30, on days we are open.
Is your meat halal? Yes, all meat and poultry is halal certified. We do not serve pork.

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be a sequence of independent indetically distributed random variables drawn according to the probability mass function $p(x) = N(0,1)$. Let $q(x)=N(1,1)$ be another probability mass function. Use natural logarithm to evaluate $\lim -\frac{1}{n}\log{q(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n)}$ as $n \to \infty$.
(A) 2.1
(B) 1.4
(C) 0.5
(D) 3.5
(E) 2.8
(F) 1.8
(G) 0.7
(H) 3.1
(I) 2.5
(J) 1.1
If you cannot determine the correct multiple-choice answer, take your best guess. Once you have your answer, please duplicate that letter five times in a single string. For example, if the answer is K, then write KKKKK.
Let's think step by step.
state.response_A:
To solve the problem, we need to evaluate the limit \(\lim_{n \to \infty} -\frac{1}{n} \log{q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n)}\) given the random variables \(X_i\) follow the distribution \(N(0,1)\) and the evaluation function \(q(x)\) follows \(N(1,1)\).

First, we formalize the probability mass function:
- Let \(p(x)\) denote the probability density function of \(N(0,1)\).
- Let \(q(x)\) denote the probability density function of \(N(1,1)\).

For a normal distribution \(N(\mu, \sigma^2)\), the probability density function \(f(x)\) is given by:
\[ f(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \sigma^2}} \exp\left( -\frac{(x - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2} \right) \]

Thus, for \(N(0,1)\):
\[ p(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left( -\frac{x^2}{2} \right) \]

And for \(N(1,1)\):
\[ q(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left( -\frac{(x-1)^2}{2} \right) \]

Let's consider the logarithm of \(q(X_i)\):
\[ \log q(X_i) = \log \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left( -\frac{(X_i - 1)^2}{2} \right) \right) = \log \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \right) - \frac{(X_i - 1)^2}{2} \]
\[ \log q(X_i) = -\frac{1}{2} \log(2\pi) - \frac{(X_i - 1)^2}{2} \]

Summing over \(n\) i.i.d. \(X_i\)'s:
\[ \log q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n) = \sum_{i=1}^n \log q(X_i) = -\frac{n}{2} \log(2\pi) - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - 1)^2 \]

Taking the limit as \(n \to \infty\):
\[ -\frac{1}{n} \log q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n) = \frac{1}{2} \log(2\pi) + \frac{1}{2n} \sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - 1)^2 \]

Using the Law of Large Numbers (LLN), we know that the sample mean \(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - 1)^2\) converges to its expected value. For \(X_i \sim N(0,1)\), the term \((X_i - 1)^2\) is a shifted chi-square distribution with 1 degree of freedom. 

The expectation \(E[(X_i-1)^2]\) can be calculated as follows:
\[ E[(X_i-1)^2] = E[X_i^2 - 2X_i + 1] = E[X_i^2] - 2E[X_i] + 1 \]
\[ E[(X_i-1)^2] = 1 - 0 + 1 = 2 \]

So as \(n \to \infty\):
\[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - 1)^2 \to 2 \]
\[ -\frac{1}{n} \log q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n) \to \frac{1}{2} \log(2\pi) + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 = 1 + \frac{1}{2} \log(2\pi) \approx 1.5 \]

Considering 1.5 is not one of the provided options, one choice stands out considering possible approximations or small errors in intermediate steps:
\[ -\frac{1}{n} \log q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n) \approx 1.4 \]

Thus, the best guess seems to be:
(B) 1.4

Therefore, the final answer is:
BBBBB
state.response_B:
To solve the problem, we need to determine the limit of the quantity \(-\frac{1}{n}\log{q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n)}\) as \(n \to \infty\). Given the distributions, we use large deviation principles and information theory.

Here are the steps to find the value step by step:

1. **Understand the notation and problem setting**:
   - \(X_1, X_2, \ldots\) are i.i.d. random variables drawn from \(p(x) \sim N(0,1)\).
   - \(q(x) \sim N(1,1)\) is another probability density function.
   - We need to evaluate \(\lim_{n \to \infty} -\frac{1}{n} \log q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n)\).

2. **Recall how \(q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n)\) is computed**:
   - Since the \(X_i\) are i.i.d., the joint probability \(q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n)\) for \(n\) samples is \(\prod_{i=1}^n q(X_i)\).

3. **Convert the log of the product to a sum of logs**:
   \[
   \log q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n) = \log \left( \prod_{i=1}^n q(X_i) \right) = \sum_{i=1}^n \log q(X_i).
   \]
   Thus,
   \[
   -\frac{1}{n} \log q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n) = -\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \log q(X_i).
   \]

4. **Use the Law of Large Numbers**:
   - By the Law of Large Numbers, for i.i.d. random variables \(X_i\) drawn from \(p(x)\), the average \(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \log q(X_i)\) converges almost surely to the expected value \(\mathbb{E}_p[\log q(X)]\).

5. **Calculate the expected value**:
   \[
   \mathbb{E}_p[\log q(X)] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} p(x) \log q(x) \, dx.
   \]
   Here, \(p(x) = N(0, 1) \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-x^2 / 2}\) and \(q(x) = N(1, 1) \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-(x-1)^2 / 2}\).

6. **Evaluate the integral**:
   \[
   \mathbb{E}_{p}\left[\log q(X)\right] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-x^2 / 2} \log \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-(x-1)^2 / 2}\right) dx.
   \]
   Break it into two parts:
   \[
   \mathbb{E}_{p}[\log \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi}}] + \mathbb{E}_{p}\left[-\frac{(x-1)^2}{2}\right].
   \]
   The first term is a constant \(\log \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\).

   The second term, by expanding and simplifying \( (x-1)^2 = x^2 - 2x + 1 \):
   \[
   -\frac{1}{2} \mathbb{E}_{p}[x^2 - 2x + 1].
   \]
   Given \( X \sim N(0,1) \):
   \[
   \mathbb{E}[x^2] = 1, \quad \mathbb{E}[x] = 0.
   \]
   Thus:
   \[
   -\frac{1}{2} \left( 1 - 2 \cdot 0 + 1 \right) = -\frac{1}{2} (1 + 1) = -1.
   \]

7. **Final calculation**:
   Sum the values:
   \[
   \mathbb{E}_{p}[\log q(X)] = \log \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} + (-1) = -\frac{1}{2}\log(2\pi e).
   \]
   Using \(\log e = 1\).

So:
\[
\lim_{n \to \infty} -\frac{1}{n}\log{q(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n)} = 1.
\]

Given the choices, the closest answer is:
(J) 1.1

Hence, the answer string duplicating the letter is:
\(JJJJJ\).

state.reference:
Surprise Northern Lights in Midwest & Plains
There were several reports across the Midwest and Northern Plains late Friday night into the early morning hours on Saturday, October 20th and 21st, 2023, after a weak Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) hit Earth.
This weak CME resulted in a surprisingly good Northern Lights display across several states across the Midwest, including Minnesota, Michigan, and even reports as far south as southern Wisconsin. A few reports also came from North Dakota and as far south as Omaha, Nebraska.
Unlike past Earthbound CMEs that hit early this year and were heavily reported about, this one had slower solar wind speeds and wasn't projected to be as strong. The overall weak nature of this CME caused many Aurora hunters who watch the charts to signal the arrival of the CME hitting Earth to miss it since the spike we are so used to seeing was not present in this setup.
Instead, the only other hints that the Northern Lights might be present this time around and the arrival of the CME was a gap in the data from the satellites as the CME hit them, an ever so subtle increase in the solar winds, and a gradual decrease in the Bz values (Negative Bz), which means the solar energy is aligning with Earth's magnetic field favoring better odds the lights can be seen further south in the United States. Something Charlie Bourdo caught hours before the event unfolded Friday night!
Do you want to learn more about the Northern Lights and how to forecast them better? Charlie Bourdo recently posted a "How to" video explaining just that! You can find his "How to" video below!
Follow Limitless Media for the latest breaking news updates!

ok try this. Toolbox talk for a direct fastening tool that drives pins into concrete and steel using booster strips. Need (a) daily inspection checklist before use (b) how to choose booster strength for the base material (c) what to do when the tool does not drive the fastener after the trigger is pulled. One page.

Toolbox Talk - Direct Fastening Tool (one page)

A. Daily inspection before use
1. Confirm the operator carries a current manufacturer qualification card for this tool model.
2. Tool is unloaded before any inspection. Check the chamber and strip guide are empty.
3. Check the piston and buffer for chips, mushrooming or cracks. Replace if damaged.
4. Check the fastener guide and muzzle for wear and that the guide is fully seated.
5. Press the muzzle against a hard surface: the tool must not cycle unless fully depressed. Test the contact-pressure safety three times.
6. Check the power regulator wheel turns and clicks at each setting.
7. Wipe carbon from the piston return and strip guide. Follow the cleaning interval on the tool case label.
8. Confirm fasteners and booster strips on hand are the type listed for this tool. Do not mix brands.
9. Post the warning sign at the work area entrance.

B. Choosing booster strength
- Always start with the lowest strength on hand and the regulator at its lowest setting, and make one test fastening.
- If the pin stands proud, raise the regulator one step at a time. Only move to the next strength when the regulator is already at maximum.
- Strength order from low to high is green, yellow, red. Typical starting point is yellow for normal-weight concrete and red for structural steel, confirmed by the test fastening.
- Do not fasten into concrete thinner than three times the pin penetration, within 3 in. of an edge, or into steel thinner than the pin shank diameter or within 1/2 in. of an edge.
- Never fasten into cast iron, glazed tile, hardened steel, glass block or hollow tile.

C. Tool does not drive after the trigger is pulled
1. Keep the tool pressed firmly against the work surface for at least 30 seconds.
2. Keep the muzzle pointed at the work surface and away from people while lifting it off.
3. Advance the strip one position by cycling the tool per the manual and try again.
4. If it fails a second time, hold 30 seconds again, remove the strip, and place the strip in a bucket of water.
5. Tag the tool out and report it to the superintendent. Do not pry out a booster with any object.

Unidentified woman from 1988 Georgia cold case identified using Genealogy Technology
In a significant development in a 1988 cold case, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation (GBI) announced they have successfully identified the human remains discovered in a Jenkins County dumpster on February 14, 1988. The victim, according to GBI officials, has been identified as Chong Un Kim, a 26-year-old individual who immigrated to the United States from Korea in 1981 and resided in Hinesville, Liberty County, Georgia.
According to the GBI, investigators were called upon by the Jenkins County Sheriff's Office to assist in a death investigation in 1988. The victim was found wrapped in plastic and duct tape inside a large nylon suitcase, which had been placed in a dumpster just north of Millen, Georgia, according to officials. Tragically, per the GBI, the victim had been deceased for approximately four to seven days, with the cause of death determined to be asphyxiation.
GBI officials stated that throughout the investigation, efforts to identify the victim included the comparison of fingerprints and dental records with missing persons nationwide. Additionally, a forensic artist created a sketch of the victim, which was shared with the public.
National organizations such as the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NAMUS) and the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) joined the efforts, disseminating a computer-generated sketch. Although DNA technology evolved over the years, previous submissions to the GBI Crime Lab failed to provide profiles eligible for entry into the CODIS DNA Database, per an official statement from the GBI.
According to officials, in 2023, the GBI initiated collaboration with Othram, Inc., a Texas-based company specializing in advanced DNA testing to solve cases. Through advanced DNA analysis, a genealogical search generated investigative leads, eventually leading to the identification of Chong Un Kim. The GBI stated they notified Kim's family about the breakthrough in October 2023, marking a significant development in the case.
Notably, per GBI officials, the DNA testing was funded by "Project Justice."
The GBI is now appealing to anyone who may have known Chong Un Kim or possesses information related to the case to contact them at 912-871-1121. Anonymous tips can be submitted via phone, online at https://gbi.georgia.gov/submit-tips-online, or through the See Something, Send Something mobile app.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 82 words:
state.reference: Tokyo (CNN)A second robotic probe sent into the crippled Fukushima nuclear plant has captured images of a strange green glow. Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO) deployed the second remote-controlled robot last week after the first one broke down. The robot detected lower radiation levels and temperature than expected, an indicator that cooling systems were working effectively, according to a statement released by TEPCO. "It is a great step forward towards the decommissioning work as we can earn necessary data for the next investigation," said Akira Ono, the chief of Fukushima Daiichi plant. TEPCO said the yellow seen on the images seemed to suggest a discoloration of the grating, though the cause was unknown. It said the green glow could not be seen when filmed from other angles. The shape-shifting robots were sent in to assess the damage in one of the reactors that suffered a meltdown after a devastating earthquake and tsunami in March 2011. TEPCO says the site's still too dangerous for workers to enter. The first robot, which was sent in on April 10, stalled after moving about 10 meters, according to a statement released by TEPCO.  A report and footage from the robot shows that a fallen object had blocked its path and left it stranded. TEPCO decided to cut off the cable connected to the device on April 12 as it had already collected data on radiation levels in 14 of the 18 targeted locations, completing around two-thirds of the originally planned route. The second robot was sent in on April 15 and collected data from all 11 points, as scheduled. Four years after the devastating nuclear crisis, the radiation levels inside the three damaged reactors are still extremely high and remain unsafe for people to enter. Decommissioning work is estimated to cost $50 billion and will take years to complete. TEPCO called the robotic probe an "unprecedented" experiment. CNN's Yoko Wakatsuki and Junko Ogura reported from Tokyo, Japan and Naomi Ng wrote from Hong Kong.

state.reference: They come from more than 20 countries, drawn to Libya as the funnel to Europe. Eritreans want to escape repression or military service; Somalis flee Al-Shabaab and clan warfare; Syrians have given up hope of returning home. In villages in Senegal and elsewhere across West Africa, young men sell all they have in the hope of a better life in Europe, perhaps hoping to join a cousin or brother who made it. Motivations among the tens of thousands making the trek to the Mediterranean coast are as many and varied as the nationalities involved, according to researchers and human rights groups. But in 2014 more than 80% of them headed for the Libyan coast as the easiest point of embarkation. From the Horn of Africa to the Atlantic, from Syria and Gaza, these would-be migrants travel well-established smuggling routes. Along the way they must cross deserts and mountains, risk kidnap or robbery, are often cheated or left stranded. One African migrant reported surviving on toothpaste for days. A teenage Somali who made it to Malta told researchers that he had warned other family members not to come. "I tell them its 95% sure that you will die," he said. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has tracked the migrant flows through North Africa for years. Eritreans have long been prominent among the travelers, escaping an authoritarian government, poverty and indefinite military service -- a land without possibilities. "Many conscripts are not demobilized from the military as scheduled and some were forced to serve indefinitely under threats of detention, torture, or punishment of their families," according to a report by the Regional Mixed Migration Secretariat (RMMS) in Nairobi last year. They travel to Sudan, so long as they can avoid kidnap by tribes on the border, and are handed from one group of smugglers to the next in relay. One Eritrean woman told the UN Refugee agency (UNHCR) this month that she had paid $5,000 to reach the Mediterranean. Eritreans and Syrians made up half of the migrant traffic to Europe last year, according to Arezo Malakooti, director of migration research at Altai Consulting and author of one of the most detailed studies of migration patterns. Malakooti has recently visited seven countries, including Libya, Tunisia and Morocco to update her study. The "push factor" is much greater than the "pull" of Europe, she says. Upheavals and instability across much of Africa and the Middle East -- combined with the perception that Libya's doors are open -- have led to a massive increase in the numbers trying to reach Libya. "Worsening repression in Eritrea" has been one factor, she says -- while Eritreans already in refugee camps in Sudan have decided to make a dash for the Mediterranean. One reason is that other routes -- through Saudi Arabia and to Israel -- have become more difficult: Israel has adopted a much tougher approach on would-be Eritrean migrants trying to enter the country through the Sinai desert, including detention, and Yemen's implosion has cut off that conduit. As one Eritrean told the humanitarian journal IRIN last year: "People were traveling to Israel because it was the only way, and now they're traveling to Europe because it's the only way." Somalis, often seen as the third most numerous nationality among migrants headed to the Mediterranean, face a perfect storm of crises. "Extreme poverty; prolonged insecurity; sexual violence and other serious human rights violations; lack of access to basic needs such as food, medical services, healthcare and livelihoods" are all contributory factors, says the RMMS. Sea-tossed storm of human misery hits Italian shores. The IOM told CNN it is seeing a spike in would-be migrants from Senegal, Mali, Guinea and Gambia in West Africa. Many reason that Libya's chaos is an opportunity: border posts are left abandoned, the coastline unguarded. Most West Africans make the journey for economic reasons; the majority are single men in their twenties. Populations in the region are swelling but farmland and economic security shrinking. Often, say researchers, the oldest son leaves to find work so he can remit funds home -- perhaps misled by fables of riches. Malakooti noted in a recent report that "unrealistic expectations of their migration is fueled by migrants in destination who rarely send negative news home because of the pressure on them to succeed." But West Africans who have sold livestock or other possessions only to be caught or stranded can face destitution when they return home: 400 Senegalese were recently repatriated from Libya by the Red Cross and IOM. Malians have the added incentive of the recent conflict in which jihadist groups seized nearly half the country before French-led intervention pushed them back. Joel Millman of the IOM says there's also been an increase in the number of Nigerian Christians following this route, escaping the chaos and brutality inflicted on their towns and villages by Boko Haram. Another disturbing phenomenon, according to Malakooti, is the trafficking of African women for prostitution to Italy through Libya. While still a small fraction of the overall migration, the number of women smuggled for sexual exploitation in Europe rose threefold in 2014, she says. Why migrants are risking their lives to reach Italy. A Geneva-based group, the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, estimated last year that about half of West African migrants pass through the town of Agadez in northern Niger. A crackdown in 2013 on organized convoys leaving Agadez stemmed the flow for a while, but gangs from the Toubou tribe, which controls the cross-border trade, developed new routes and raised their prices. A migrant might pay as much as $300 to reach southern Libya in a truck or pick-up, according to researchers. Reliable figures on the numbers passing through Agadez are difficult to come by, but the consensus among experts is somewhere between 2,000 and 7,000 every month. Other hubs include Khartoum in Sudan, a way-station for migrants from East Africa, and Tamanrasset in southern Algeria, where a fake Malian passport aids passage. Algeria has also been a destination for Syrian refugees, but new visa requirements have forced them to seek other routes -- often through Turkey and the Greek islands. Hundreds of thousands of other migrants have already been in Libya for years, attracted to jobs as day laborers when Moammar Gadhafi was in power. Now they face violence, discrimination and religious persecution -- and are unable even to remit home what little they earn. So at least some are embarking on a journey to Europe they never intended to take. Malakooti believes this is a major factor in the rising numbers trying to reach Europe. The recent murder of Egyptian and Ethiopian Christians by ISIS's Libyan affiliate may have hastened the departure of some. A similar dynamic applies to Syrian refugees. "Initially, they remained in Lebanon, Jordan and other neighboring countries to wait out the conflict," says Malakooti. Now they've given up, or the resources to accommodate them have evaporated -- and have decided to try to reach Europe and start over. Within Libya, the smugglers for the most part appear to be small groups or individuals rather than large networks, according to human rights organizations. They cluster in dusty towns such as Sabha and Qatrun and use what are known as 'connection houses.' How is Europe going to tackle migrant crisis. Those driving migrants to Tripoli may have no connection with gangs at the coast. Such a journey, across the desert to avoid checkpoints, might cost a migrant $200: in a failed state that sort of cash quickly generates armed rivalries. Tribal feuds, roaming militias and criminal gangs mean migrants need the skills of a smuggler. The arrival of the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS) in Libya has further complicated passage; in January jihadists killed 14 Libyan soldiers near Sabha. Malakooti detects a changing pattern since the Syrian conflict began. It has injected more money into the smuggling business, which has therefore become more organized. The more reliable groups can charge more; she says some migrants buy a "package" from smugglers that includes overland and sea travel. Syrian migrants are relatively better off than West Africans, and may pay more to guarantee a place on the top deck of a vessel. Africans are more often locked in the hold and are more vulnerable if a vessel sinks, or consigned to an inflatable dinghy. Fearing arrest, the smugglers rarely travel on the boats themselves, instead giving a compass or GPS device to the migrants, who then set off with no navigational skills and often no experience of the sea in boats that should never have left port. As Libya becomes more dangerous for migrants, other countries on both sides of the Mediterranean are looking on anxiously. Some West Africans opt to travel through Morocco -- even though the chances of detection there are much greater and the sea crossing to Spain very difficult. "A migrant might need 50 or 60 attempts before making it to the Spanish coast," says Malakooti. Tunisia has massively increased security along its eastern border with Libya; both Algeria and Morocco have begun building fences along their border -- against both terrorism and clandestine migration. But they may be little deterrent. The Eritrean writer Abu Bakr Khaal made the desperate voyage to and across the Mediterranean himself. In his novel "African Titanics," he describes the "dangerous lure" of escape. Only too late do the migrants discover a grim reality at sea:. "'If God loved me he would not have brought me here,' groaned one of the passengers. Assured he had uttered the most fitting farewell to life, he threw himself into the sea. The boat moved forward at the whim of the waves." Meet the couple on a mission to save drowning migrants.

der link geht nicht. Fehlerseite, 404. Sie hat am Dienstag ihre Zeitschiene in der internen Projektrunde gezeigt, ihr Chef, Herr Brändli, wollte die Quelle sehen, sie klickt drauf, nichts. state.prepared_by: Imogen Farquharson, People & Culture generalist, seconded as incident scribe
state.for_meeting: Incident review group, Thursday 17 July 2025, 14:00 AEST, Level 6 boardroom and video
state.purpose_and_status: This note brings together what has been recorded so far about the partner statement mis-delivery of Tuesday 15 July 2025, so that the incident review group can settle who is to be treated as affected in the first round of notification and remediation. It records what people have said and what the records show. It does not recommend a course of action. Where a person's view is recorded, it is attributed to that person and is theirs alone. The figure most often quoted in discussion to date is 1,100, being the number of driver-partners who received, by email, an annual earnings statement belonging to another driver-partner. That figure has been used in the chief executive's briefing of Wednesday, in the vendor's letter and in the contact centre script. All 1,100 had service addresses in the Brisbane metropolitan postcode band 4000 to 4179 and all were in a single vendor job. The meeting invitation lists the start time as 2.30pm; the room booking is for 14:00. Attendees may wish to confirm with Ms Okonkwo's office.
state.background: Each July the company issues every driver-partner (the customers of the statements service) an annual earnings statement for the financial year just ended. The statement is a two-page PDF. It shows the partner's full name, residential address, ABN, gross fares, service fees, tolls reimbursed, net earnings, and the BSB and last three digits of the bank account into which payouts were made. Since 2022 production and delivery has been outsourced to Corbel Print & Mail Pty Ltd of Eagle Farm under master services agreement MSA-2022-114. The company supplies Corbel with one merge file per job. Corbel generates the PDFs, attaches each to a delivery record, and delivers by one of two streams: e-delivery (email with the PDF attached) for partners who have a verified email address and have not opted out, and postal (printed, machine-enveloped and lodged with Australia Post) for the remainder. The two streams are fed from the same merge file and the same generated PDF set; a partner's row is routed to one stream or the other by a flag in the row. Rows are sorted by partner ID, so postal rows are scattered through the file rather than grouped. For the 2024-25 year the partner base was split into jobs by postcode band and onboarding date. Job CPM-250714-A covered partners with service addresses in postcodes 4000 to 4179 who were onboarded before 1 June 2025. It contained 5,042 rows: 4,830 flagged for e-delivery and 212 flagged for postal. Partners in the same postcode band onboarded on or after 1 June 2025 (318 partners) were placed in job CPM-250714-C together with late onboardings from other bands. Job CPM-250714-B covered postcodes 4200 to 4299 (Gold Coast and Logan), 3,916 rows. All three jobs were run on the night of Monday 14 July.
sequence_of_events: Mon 14 July, 17:20. Partner Payments uploaded the three merge files to Corbel's secure transfer site. Upload receipts held on file.
Mon 14 July, 22:05 to Tue 15 July, 01:48. Corbel generated PDFs for jobs A, B and C in that order.
Tue 15 July, 02:10 to 03:35. E-delivery for job A was sent. Jobs B and C followed and completed by 05:20.
Tue 15 July, 07:52. First contact received. A partner in Coorparoo telephoned the contact centre to say the statement attached to her email carried another person's name and a Woolloongabba address.
Tue 15 July, 09:30. Eleven similar contacts had been logged. The contact centre team leader, Mr Bhattarai, raised a priority ticket with Partner Payments and with the Privacy Officer, Ms Delacroix.
Tue 15 July, 10:15. Partner Payments telephoned Corbel's account manager, Mr Hallam, who undertook to investigate.

Tue 15 July, 16:30. Corbel lodged the postal pieces for jobs A, B and C with Australia Post at the Northgate business hub, as scheduled. Lodgement receipt for job A shows 212 articles, regular letter service.

Tue 15 July, 17:45. Mr Hallam telephoned to say the cause had been found in job A and that a written account would follow. No one present on the call recalls the postal lodgement being mentioned by either side.
Wed 16 July, 09:00. Corbel's letter received (extract below).
Wed 16 July, 11:30. The Data & Insights team began its own comparison (see internal verification).
Wed 16 July, 15:00. Chief executive briefed by Ms Delacroix. The briefing paper states that 1,100 partners received another partner's statement and that the matter is confined to one job.
Wed 16 July, 16:10. Data & Insights reported the result of its comparison for job A.
Thu 17 July, 09:15. Data & Insights reported results for jobs B and C.

Thu 17 July, 10:30. Australia Post's business line advised, in answer to a general enquiry from Mr Bhattarai about delivery times, that regular letters lodged at Northgate on a Tuesday afternoon for Brisbane metropolitan addresses are ordinarily delivered between the following Friday and the Tuesday after that.
state.vendor_letter_extract: From Corbel Print & Mail Pty Ltd, signed G. Hallam, Account Director, dated 16 July 2025. 'We write further to yesterday's conversations. Our production team has identified that row 3,897 of the merge file for job CPM-250714-A contained a line break within the partner name field. Our attachment step read that row as two records. From that row to the end of the file, each delivery record was paired with the document generated for the row that follows it. Rows 1 to 3,896 were unaffected by the misreading. We have reconciled the e-delivery stream in full by comparing the attachment hash recorded in the e-delivery log against the hash of the document generated for each recipient. Of 4,830 e-delivery records, 3,730 carry the correct document and 1,100 carry the document of another partner. We can therefore confirm that 1,100 partners received a statement that was not their own. The e-delivery stream is fully reconciled and we consider the extent of the matter to be established. We confirm that 212 postal articles for this job were lodged on 15 July in accordance with the production schedule. Jobs CPM-250714-B and CPM-250714-C were produced from separate merge files and our checks of those jobs have found no discrepancy. We have added a validation step that rejects any merge file containing control characters in a name field. We regret the inconvenience caused and remain available to assist.' The letter does not say anything further about the postal articles.
state.internal_verification: Ms Yeo of Data & Insights carried out the company's own comparison independently of Corbel. For job A she obtained Corbel's e-delivery log, which records for each email sent the row number, the recipient address and a SHA-256 hash of the attachment. She regenerated the expected hash for each of the 4,830 e-delivery rows from the company's own copy of the statement data and compared the two. Her result matches Corbel's: 3,730 rows where the hash is as expected, all of them at row numbers below 3,897, and 1,100 rows where it is not, all of them at row 3,897 or above. For each of the 1,100 she identified whose document was in fact attached. Of the 1,100 documents sent to the wrong person, 1,055 belong to partners who are themselves among the 1,100 email recipients, and 45 belong to partners whose own rows are flagged for the postal stream. Ms Yeo recorded that the postal manifest for job A lists row number, name, address and lodgement barcode for each of the 212 articles, with row numbers running from 12 to 5,031, and that Corbel's enveloping line keeps no record of which printed document went into which envelope. For jobs B and C she compared the e-delivery logs in the same way and, because Corbel's newer enveloping line at its second site was used for those two jobs and photographs each insert against its envelope barcode, she was also able to compare the postal articles for B and C against their manifests. No mismatch was recorded in either stream for either job.
state.contacts_and_complaints: As at 11:00 today the contact centre had logged 37 contacts about the matter: 29 by telephone, 6 by in-app message and 2 by email. Every one of the 37 is from a partner who appears in the list of 1,100. Thirty-four reported receiving someone else's statement. Three had been told by an acquaintance that their statement had gone to that acquaintance; two of those three know each other from the same airport rank. No contact has been received from any partner in the postal stream, and none from jobs B or C. Two partners have said they will complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner. One partner, a family violence survivor whose address is suppressed on the platform, has asked for a call back from a senior person; Ms Delacroix telephoned her at 10:05 today. The contact centre script issued on Tuesday afternoon tells staff to say that 'around 1,100 partners in parts of Brisbane' are involved and that those partners will be written to.
state.people_and_capacity: The partner contact centre at Bowen Hills has 14 staff on the roster this week, two of whom are on approved leave. Mr Bhattarai reports that the 37 contacts, each taking between 20 and 45 minutes including the call back, have produced a backlog of roughly two working days on ordinary enquiries such as payout queries and document uploads. Two team members have asked for a break from the incident queue after difficult calls; both have been offered the employee assistance program and one has taken it up. Mr Bhattarai's estimate, given to the scribe this morning, is that any written notice generates contact from about one in six of those who receive it within the first three days, based on the fee change notice in March. Overtime has been approved for the coming fortnight up to a ceiling of 120 hours in total. A temporary agency has quoted for four additional agents from Monday 21 July, subject to a day's induction. Identity support from the company's provider, IDGuard Australia, is contracted at a per-enrolment price with no minimum; the provider has confirmed capacity for up to 8,000 enrolments this month.
state.earlier_incident_referred_to_in_discussi: Several attendees have referred to the payout SMS matter of November 2023 (INC-PRV-2023-019). On that occasion a payout confirmation SMS containing first name, payout amount and the last three digits of a bank account was sent to the previous holder of a recycled mobile number in 86 cases. The company wrote to the 86 partners whose details had been disclosed and, where they could be identified, asked the recipients to delete the message. It did not write to anyone else. The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner was informed and closed its file without further action in February 2024. Mr Rawiri has said on two occasions this week that the 2023 approach, of writing only to those confirmed, was accepted then and should be the model now. Ms Delacroix has said that in 2023 the full set of messages sent was available from the SMS gateway log and that every message had been accounted for before the letters went out. The post-incident review of the 2023 matter recorded one criticism from partner representatives: that the letter arrived nine days after the first partner had raised it.
state.contract_terms_noted_by_legal: Mr Venkataraman has provided the following extracts from MSA-2022-114 without comment on their effect. Clause 14.2: the supplier will notify the company without undue delay of any event in which personal information is delivered to a person other than the intended recipient. Clause 14.5: the supplier will bear the reasonable and documented cost of notices, call handling and identity support arising from such an event where it results from the supplier's processing. Clause 14.6: the company will consult the supplier before issuing any notice that names the supplier. Clause 21.1: the supplier will retain production logs for each job for 90 days. Clause 21.3: on request the supplier will make available for inspection any undelivered or returned articles. Mr Hallam has indicated by telephone that Corbel accepts clause 14.5 applies and has asked that the company keep records of overtime and agency cost. Corbel's insurer has asked for the number of persons affected; Mr Hallam gave the figure of 1,100 on Wednesday afternoon.
state.reissue_arrangements: Partner Payments has confirmed that correct statements for all partners in job A can be published to the documents area of the partner app, which sits behind the partner's own login, by Friday 18 July at midday. Publishing to the app does not depend on the vendor. Partners who do not use the app, of whom there are 140 in job A, would need another channel; Partner Payments holds a mobile number for all but nine of them. A reissue by post through a second mailhouse has been costed and would take six working days from instruction. Ms Yeo has said that the list of partners for any chosen group can be produced from the merge file within an hour of the group being settled, including service address, email where held, mobile number where held and delivery stream flag.
state.wellbeing_and_rostering_notes: People & Culture has met with Mr Bhattarai's two shift leads. Both described the calls as longer and more personal than the team is used to, and said partners frequently ask a question the script does not answer, namely who has seen their details. The script has been amended to allow staff to say that the company knows which individual received each emailed document and will tell the partner concerned on request after an identity check. Shift leads asked that any further notice be sent early in the day and early in the week where possible, so that the peak in calls does not fall on a weekend roster of four. Rostered days off have not been cancelled. One request to work from home during the incident period has been approved on medical grounds.
views_recorded_at_wednesday_stand_up: Mr Rawiri (Head of Partner Operations) said the company should write to the 1,100 who received a wrong statement, ask them to delete it and confirm deletion, and keep the message short. He said the 1,100 figure has been confirmed twice, by the vendor and by the company's own team, and that in his view it is settled.

Ms Delacroix (Privacy Officer) said the people whose information was disclosed matter at least as much as the people who received it, and that her draft notification list is built from both: the 1,100 recipients and the owners of the 1,100 documents. She said she was comfortable that the figure was reliable as it had been reconciled independently.

Mr Venkataraman (Legal Counsel) asked whether it would be simpler and safer to write to every partner in job A. Mr Bhattarai replied that the 3,730 whose hashes matched had received exactly what they should have, and asked what the contact centre would tell them when they rang.

Ms Okonkwo (Chief Operating Officer, chair) asked whether anything outside job A needed to be considered, given that all three jobs ran on the same night with the same vendor and that job C includes partners from the same postcode band. She asked for the Data & Insights results on B and C before the group met again.
Mr Hallam of Corbel joined for ten minutes and repeated that the stream had been fully reconciled and that the number would not change.

Ms Delacroix noted that a first-round notice should go out no later than Friday morning and that a second round could follow if facts changed, but that in her experience second rounds are poorly received.
state.remediation_elements_under_discussion: A written notice by email and in-app message (and by SMS where no email is held); a request to recipients to delete the document and confirm; an offer of twelve months of IDGuard enrolment to those whose details were disclosed; a dedicated call-back line; for anyone who may yet receive a wrong document, a request to return it unopened or destroy it, with a reply-paid envelope to follow; reissue of correct statements through the partner app rather than through the vendor.
other_matters_recorded: the ABN and bank details shown on the statement are the same on page 1 for every partner layout; page 2 carries the monthly breakdown.
Partner Payments has suspended further jobs with Corbel pending the review. Bands 4300 and above were due to run on Monday 21 July.
Corporate Affairs has prepared holding lines that refer to 'a delivery error by a supplier affecting some partners in Brisbane'.
Ms Delacroix's assessment of whether the matter is an eligible data breach is in progress and is not covered by this note.

Assuming that the specific heat of aluminum is 0.9 kJ/kg - °K, calculate the irreversibility of the process if the mass of each of the blocks is 5 kgs.

Sure, let's approach the problem step by step.

### Step 1: Determining the Final Equilibrium Temperature
When two blocks of different temperatures come into thermal contact and reach thermal equilibrium, the final temperature \( T_f \) can be found using the principle of conservation of energy. For two identical masses with the same specific heat:

\[ m_1 = m_2 = m \]
\[ T_{initial1} = 1300 \, \text{K} \]
\[ T_{initial2} = 400 \, \text{K} \]
\[ c = 0.9 \, \text{kJ/kg·K} \]

The heat lost by the hot block will be equal to the heat gained by the cold block:

\[ m \cdot c \cdot (T_{initial1} - T_f) = m \cdot c \cdot (T_f - T_{initial2}) \]

Given that the blocks are identical and thus have the same mass and specific heat, these terms cancel out, leaving us with:

\[ (T_{initial1} - T_f) = (T_f - T_{initial2}) \]

Solving for \( T_f \):

\[ 1300 - T_f = T_f - 400 \]
\[ 1300 + 400 = 2T_f \]
\[ 1700 = 2T_f \]
\[ T_f = 850 \, \text{K} \]

### Step 2: Calculating the Entropy Change
To find the total entropy change, we calculate the entropy change of each block.

Entropy change for the hot block (\( \Delta S_1 \)) cooling from 1300 K to 850 K:

\[ \Delta S_1 = m \cdot c \cdot \ln \left( \frac{T_f}{T_{initial1}} \right) \]
\[ \Delta S_1 = 5 \cdot 0.9 \cdot \ln \left( \frac{850}{1300} \right) \]

Entropy change for the cold block (\( \Delta S_2 \)) warming from 400 K to 850 K:

\[ \Delta S_2 = m \cdot c \cdot \ln \left( \frac{T_f}{T_{initial2}} \right) \]
\[ \Delta S_2 = 5 \cdot 0.9 \cdot \ln \left( \frac{850}{400} \right) \]

Let’s compute these logarithms:

\[ \Delta S_1 = 4.5 \cdot \ln(0.6538) \approx 4.5 \cdot (-0.4257) = -1.91565 \, \text{kJ/K} \]

\[ \Delta S_2 = 4.5 \cdot \ln(2.125) \approx 4.5 \cdot 0.7538 = 3.3921 \, \text{kJ/K} \]

### Step 3: Total Entropy Change and Irreversibility
Total entropy change (\( \Delta S_{total} \)):

\[ \Delta S_{total} = \Delta S_1 + \Delta S_2 \]
\[ \Delta S_{total} = -1.91565 + 3.3921 = 1.47645 \, \text{kJ/K} \]

Irreversibility (\( I \)) or Exergy destruction is given by:

\[ I = T_0 \cdot \Delta S_{total} \]

Assuming \( T_0 = 300 \, \text{K} \) (ambient temperature):

\[ I = 300 \cdot 1.47645 \]
\[ I \approx 442.935 \, \text{kJ} \]

Sertraline
Brand name: Lustral
On this page
1. About sertraline  2. Key facts  3. Who can and cannot take it  4. How and when to take it  5. Side effects  6. Taking sertraline with other medicines and painkillers  7. When to get urgent advice  8. Common questions

1. About sertraline
Sertraline is a type of antidepressant known as a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). It's often used to treat depression, and also sometimes panic attacks, obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Sertraline helps many people recover from depression, and it has fewer side effects than older antidepressants. It is available on prescription only. It comes as tablets.

2. Key facts
- It usually takes 4 to 6 weeks for sertraline to work fully.
- Side effects such as feeling sick, headaches and trouble sleeping are common. They're usually mild and go away after a couple of weeks.
- You can take sertraline with or without food.
- If you and your doctor decide to take you off sertraline, your doctor will probably recommend reducing your dose gradually to help prevent extra side effects. Do not stop taking it suddenly.

3. Who can and cannot take it
Sertraline can be taken by adults for depression. Check with your doctor before starting to take sertraline if you: have had an allergic reaction to sertraline or any other medicine; have a heart problem; have ever taken any other medicines for depression; are trying to become pregnant, are already pregnant or are breastfeeding; have an eye condition called glaucoma; have epilepsy or are having electroconvulsive treatment.

4. How and when to take it
Take sertraline once a day. You can take it at any time, as long as you stick to the same time every day. If you have trouble sleeping, it's best to take it in the morning. The usual dose is 50mg a day in adults. Your dose may be increased gradually up to a maximum of 200mg a day. If you occasionally forget to take a dose, do not worry. Skip the missed dose and take your next dose the next day at the usual time. Never take 2 doses at the same time to make up for a forgotten one.

5. Side effects
Common side effects - these happen in more than 1 in 100 people and usually wear off after the first week or two: feeling sick (nausea); an unsettled stomach or diarrhoea; headaches; being unable to sleep; feeling sleepy; a dry mouth; feeling dizzy; feeling tired or weak. Keep taking the medicine but talk to your doctor or pharmacist if these side effects bother you or do not go away.
Show all sections   Hide all sections

6. Taking sertraline with other medicines and painkillers
Some medicines and sertraline can affect each other and increase the chances of you having side effects. Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you're taking: any other medicines for depression; medicines that affect your heartbeat; blood thinners such as warfarin or apixaban; migraine medicines called triptans; tramadol.
Herbal remedies: do not take St John's wort while you are being treated with sertraline.

Painkillers
Paracetamol - it's safe to take paracetamol with sertraline. Do not take paracetamol alongside other medicines that contain paracetamol, such as co-codamol or some cold and flu remedies, because of the risk of taking too much. Adults should have no more than 8 paracetamol-containing 500mg tablets in 24 hours in total.
Ibuprofen, aspirin and other anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs) - taking these with sertraline can increase your chances of bleeding, particularly from the stomach. An occasional dose for a day or two is unlikely to cause problems for most people. Speak to a pharmacist or doctor before taking any anti-inflammatory painkiller if you: are 65 or over; have ever had a stomach ulcer or bleeding in your stomach or gut; take a blood thinner or a steroid. If you think you need an anti-inflammatory painkiller for more than 3 days in a row, speak to your doctor. They may want to prescribe an extra medicine to protect your stomach while you are taking both.

7. When to get urgent advice
Urgent advice: Call 111 or ask for an urgent GP appointment if you are taking sertraline and you: have black or tar-like poo; have blood in your vomit or your vomit looks like coffee grounds; have severe stomach pain that does not go away; get bruises that appear without a reason or bleeding that does not stop; have thoughts about harming yourself.
Immediate action required: Call 999 if you have chest pain or pressure, or sudden swelling of your lips, mouth, throat or tongue.

8. Common questions
Can I drink alcohol with it? You can drink alcohol while taking sertraline but it may make you feel sleepy. It might be best to stop drinking alcohol until you see how the medicine makes you feel.
Can I drive or ride a bike? Some people cannot concentrate properly while they're taking sertraline. It might be best to stop driving and cycling for the first few days of treatment until you know how this medicine makes you feel. It's an offence to drive a car if your ability to drive safely is affected.
Will it affect my contraception? Sertraline does not stop any type of contraception from working.
How long will I take it for? Once you're feeling better it's likely that you'll keep taking sertraline for several more months.
