A la carte prices are in UAE dirhams and include 5% VAT. A 10% service charge is added to a la carte bills.
Menu last updated: 3 June 2025.

sections.heading: Drinks
sections.text: Our list leans on the Adriatic: Posip and Malvazija by the glass from AED 58, Plavac Mali from AED 64, and a short list of bottles from Istria, Brac and the Peljesac peninsula from AED 290. House-made lemonade with sage AED 28. Still or sparkling water, 750 ml, AED 26. Espresso AED 18. Mocktails from AED 38. Drinks prices include 5% VAT, and a 10% service charge is added. Alcohol also carries the 30% municipality tax, already included in the listed price.

sections.heading: Set menus for groups
sections.text:
Parties of 10 or more dine from our set menus. All set menus are served family style and include still and sparkling water and soft drinks throughout the meal.

Jadran menu - AED 245 per person: bread and olive oil, octopus salad, fish soup, black cuttlefish risotto, rozata.
Maestral menu - AED 295 per person: bread and olive oil, Pag cheese, octopus salad, grilled sea bream, beef pasticada, blitva, fritule and rozata.
Kornati menu - AED 365 per person: everything on the Maestral menu plus tuna crudo, lamb peka carved at the table, and fig and carob ice cream.

Set menu prices are per person and exclude 10% service charge and 5% VAT, each calculated on the menu price. Vegetarian and gluten-free versions of every set menu are available with 48 hours' notice. Final menu choice and final guest numbers are requested 48 hours before the booking.

sections.heading: Private dining room - Bura
sections.text:
Bura is our private room behind the wine wall, with its own door, its own sound system and a single long table that seats up to 14 guests. For larger groups please ask about a semi-private section of the main dining room, which takes up to 30.

Minimum spend for Bura: AED 5,500 from Sunday to Thursday, AED 7,500 on Friday and Saturday. Minimum spend is assessed on food and beverage menu prices before service charge and VAT. If the bill for food and beverage falls below the minimum spend, the difference is charged as room hire.

Bura follows the restaurant's opening hours and is not available on days when the restaurant is closed. A screen with HDMI input and a wireless presenter can be set up on request at no charge.

sections.heading: Bookings, deposits and cancellations
sections.text:
A deposit of 25% of the applicable minimum spend, rounded up to the nearest AED 50, secures the private dining room. The deposit is deducted from the final bill.

Cancellations must be made by email and are timed from when we receive your email.
- Cancel 72 hours or more before your booking time: the deposit is refunded in full.
- Cancel less than 72 hours but 24 hours or more before your booking time: half of the deposit is refunded.
- Cancel less than 24 hours before your booking time, or do not arrive: the deposit is kept.

Refunds are returned to the original card within 7 to 10 working days. Moving a booking to another date is free of charge when requested 48 hours or more before the original booking time and is subject to availability.

Tables in the main dining room are held for 15 minutes. Main dining room bookings of up to 9 guests need no deposit except on New Year's Eve and during special events.

sections.heading: Getting here
sections.text: Konoba Maestral is on the Marina Promenade level of Al Yamm Tower, Dubai Marina, a five-minute walk from DMCC metro station (Red Line) and two minutes from Dubai Marina Mall tram stop. Valet parking is available at the Al Yamm Tower drop-off from 12:00 for AED 40, complimentary when you spend AED 500 or more. Self-parking in the tower basement is AED 20 per hour; we validate the first three hours. Water taxi station Marina Promenade is directly in front of the restaurant. Coaches and minibuses can set down on Al Marsa Street, 80 metres from the entrance.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: Dress code is smart casual. We kindly ask gentlemen to avoid sleeveless tops and beachwear in the evening. Children are welcome until 20:00; high chairs are available. We are a licensed venue; alcohol is served to guests aged 21 and over, and ID may be requested. Shisha is not offered. We can accommodate most allergies with notice, but our kitchen handles fish, shellfish, nuts, gluten and dairy every day. Birthday cakes brought from outside carry a plating charge of AED 15 per person. The restaurant and the private room are step-free from the promenade, and an accessible washroom is on the same level.

sections.heading: Sourcing
sections.text: Our sea bream, sea bass and cuttlefish are flown in from the Adriatic three times a week, on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday. Local hammour and sherry fish come from the Deira waterfront market each morning. Olive oil is from a single grove on the island of Solta, pressed each November. Pag cheese, prosciutto-style beef and dried figs arrive monthly by sea. We stopped using single-use plastic in the kitchen in 2023, and our used cooking oil is collected for biodiesel.

sections.heading: Gift cards and careers
sections.text:
Gift cards are available from AED 250 and are valid for 12 months from purchase. They can be used for food and drinks in the main dining room and cannot be used towards private dining deposits.

We are hiring: chef de partie (grill), two waiters with a second language, and a part-time reservations agent. Send your CV to careers@konobamaestral.ae.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
sections.text:
Do you take walk-ins? Yes, whenever we are open to the public, subject to space.
Can I book the private room online? Private dining is booked by email or phone so that we can talk through the menu with you.
Is there a corkage option? No.
Do you have a prayer room nearby? Al Yamm Tower has prayer rooms on the podium level.
Can you invoice a company? Yes. Send us your trade licence and TRN and we will issue a tax invoice in the company name.
Do you deliver? Through Deliveroo and Talabat, 12:00 - 22:30, on days we are open.
Is your meat halal? Yes, all meat and poultry is halal certified. We do not serve pork.

Answer 2 The goodwill of a business is the whole advantage of the reputation and connection with customers together with the circumstances whether of habit or otherwise, which tend to make that connection permanent. state.response:
Based on the given passages, here's a brief answer to the question:

Goodwill refers to the positive reputation and customer loyalty that a business has built over time. It is important because it can increase the customer base, retain old clients, attract investors, and even attract future buyers. Goodwill is created when a business provides excellent service or products, leading to customer satisfaction and loyalty. This loyalty can lead to repeat business and positive word-of-mouth advertising, which can increase the value of the business. In essence, goodwill represents the value of a business's reputation and customer relationships, making it an important intangible asset for any business.

The underground city actually dates back centuries but was sealed up in the 18th century. It was rediscovered in the late 19th century. During World War I, soldiers would take refuge in the carved-out rooms and pathways. The front was sometimes mere miles away; the Battle of the Somme, one of the bloodiest in world history, was fought nearby in 1916. The land was privately owned for many years and generally off-limits to outsiders, said Gusky, but it changed hands in 2013. The rights to operate it were purchased by a consortium of villages that wanted to promote awareness of the area's history, he said. Researching the city is a painstaking task. Fifty-five are Americans, and 662 have yet to be traced. For Gusky, the graffiti provides a human connection with men who lived a century ago. In many cases, they just wanted to be remembered, he said. "Someone could be in this place one day and the next fighting at the front," he said. review_info.review_text: It's always fun to try a new vegan place and this one doesn't disappoint. Super fresh, delicious and inventive. The squash blossom quesadilla was delicious (the blue corn tortilla was out of this world). The staff was also super friendly.

Pretty disappointing. I've been wanting to eat here for several years based on what I thought was a great reputation in town.  I don't get over to the Mesa much but when I saw a coupon in a mailed flyer a couple months ago, I clipped it.  It offered a free entree with purchase of one entree and two drinks. Even with a discount of $12, the bill was $53 for lunch (before tip) -- I can eat a great dinner out for less than this -- so I was expecting a very delicious meal.  Both my companion and I felt the food was vastly overpriced for the quality, flavor and even presentation. The quantity was generous enough but the items we ordered (empanadas and the mushroom burger) were both rather bland.  The "burger" was served on a doughy, barely cooked pita-like bread rather than on an appropriate item to hold a messy burger in place like a brioche bun.  It was completely falling apart after a few bites... which would have been okay to eat with a fork except it was just not flavorful or complex given the list of ingredients. The most interesting item was the ketchup made from beets.  Also the side fries weren't thoroughly cooked except for the smallest ones.  Definitely not a $24 item! The empanadas were somewhat better but again, not a 'wow' and not even a 'hey, really tasty.' Just bland and again, not worth $24.  The half-off discount didn't even cover the $13 cost of a chai tea and lemonade (that was mostly ice of course).  All in all, very disappointing food and therefore completely overpriced.  We took the food to go so I cannot really comment on the service. When I read another lengthy review (12/5/21), I now see that the prices have been jacked and the quality has been wavering. I totally understand the precarious state of the restaurant business right now during covid but I cannot recommend this restaurant at this time.
Flavors are always spot on! Service is also good. Best fusion snd vegan food in Santa Barbara.

Antwort vom Assistenten, ich lese vor was sie mir weitergeleitet hat, Zitat: Die NAFDAC nennt für die Prüfung eines vollständigen Antrags einen Richtwert von rund 60 Arbeitstagen, das ist keine verbindliche Frist. Im selben Absatz noch zwei Quellen mit unseren Dokumentnummern in eckigen Klammern, D-2291 und D-0874, die gehören aber zu dem Satz über die Ethikkommission NHREC, nicht zu den 60 Tagen.

der link geht nicht. Fehlerseite, 404. Sie hat am Dienstag ihre Zeitschiene in der internen Projektrunde gezeigt, ihr Chef, Herr Brändli, wollte die Quelle sehen, sie klickt drauf, nichts. Wörtlich: da stand ich ziemlich blöd da. Danach hat sie einen halben Tag auf der NAFDAC-Seite gesucht und nichts gefunden. Nach draußen ist nichts gegangen, das hat sie dreimal gesagt. Nichts an die Behörde, nichts an die Prüfzentren in Lagos und Ibadan, nichts an den Vorstand. Nur die interne Runde. Nichts rausgegangen.

Was Tunde sagt. Ich hab vor dem Call mit Tunde Adebayo aus der Entwicklung gesprochen. Er hat das Protokoll gezogen, Anfrage Q-58813. Abgerufen wurden fünf Textstücke: D-2291, D-0874, zweimal SOP-RA-017, einmal D-1140, das ist die Gebührentabelle in Naira. Der Link steht in keinem der fünf, auch nicht irgendwo im Fließtext. Im Index war er nie, Tunde hat die Historie durchgesehen, auch die alten Stände vom Frühjahr. Die NAFDAC-Links die wir tatsächlich im Index haben sehen fast genauso aus, gleicher Pfad, gleiche Schreibweise, nur mit 2020 am Ende. Emeka Obi aus Regulatory sagt, eine Fassung von 2023 kennt er nicht und die hat es auch nie gegeben, gültig ist die Leitlinie von 2020, das PDF hat er, ist öffentlich, liegt bei NAFDAC ganz normal auf der Seite.

Inhaltlich. In SOP-RA-017, Abschnitt 4.2, steht, ich lese ab: Für die Bewertung vollständiger Anträge gibt NAFDAC in der Leitlinie von 2020 eine Zielgröße von etwa sechzig Arbeitstagen an, ein Anspruch auf Entscheidung innerhalb dieser Zeit besteht nicht. Das war eins der fünf Stücke. Die SOP trägt oben den Vermerk vertraulich, nur für internen Gebrauch Savanna. Der Assistent darf daraus schöpfen, so ist es eingerichtet, aber rausgeben tun wir SOPs an Sponsoren nicht, das war schon bei der Ausschreibung von Rhenovia so, da haben sie danach gefragt und wir haben nein gesagt.

Zum Prüfer. Tunde sagt der Zitat-Checker schaut nur auf die Dokumentnummern in eckigen Klammern, ob die in der abgerufenen Menge sind. Nackte Links lässt er durch, weil die Textstücke selber Links enthalten dürfen. Eine Prüfung für Links kommt frühestens im übernächsten Sprint, also Mitte Dezember, und auch nur wenn Ngozi das hochpriorisiert, sie entscheidet nächsten Dienstag.

Wie das Gespräch lief. Ich hab mich entschuldigt, nicht rumdiskutiert, hab ihr erklärt was wir bis jetzt wissen, also dass der Link nicht aus unseren Dokumenten kommt. Sie war sachlich, am Ende eigentlich ganz entspannt. Ich hab zugesagt: schriftliche Erklärung bis Freitag. Und ich hab ihr gesagt, ab nächster Woche gibt StudyDesk keine nackten Links mehr aus, dann ist das Thema erledigt. Das hat sie gefreut, sie will das so an Herrn Brändli weitergeben.

Was sie will. Wörtlich: schicken Sie mir einfach die Stelle wo das steht, dann kann ich das Herrn Brändli zeigen und gut ist. Und: ich will kein Fass aufmachen, mir reicht wenn es nicht wieder passiert. Freitag reicht ihr für die Erklärung, hat sie zweimal gesagt, Freitag reicht völlig. Nebenbei, schon halb im Auflegen: morgen früh um neun geht ihre Folie mit der Zeitschiene an den CMO, mit oder ohne Quelle, hat sie gelacht.

Fällt mir gerade ein. Im August hatte Frau Okafor-Lenz von Helvia Pharma, die mit der Studie in Kano, auch einen toten Link in einer StudyDesk-Antwort gemeldet. Das hat der Support damals als Tippfehler der Nutzerin geschlossen, ins Protokoll hat keiner geschaut.

Bitte das als nächstes erledigen.

ok weird question for the health info thing. I've got this rash on the left side of my rib cage, kind of a stripe that wraps from my back around to the front, little blisters, and it burns like crazy, even my shirt touching it is awful. Showed up Saturday morning, I figured it was the new laundry soap. Im 52, had chicken pox as a kid. Nothing near my eye or face. No fever that I know of. What is this and do I need to ducking go in? I've got back to back SAT and GRE sessions all week and can't really be out.

Sent from my iPhone

I'm sorry, that sounds painful. A couple of things up front: I can share general health information, but I can't diagnose conditions, and only a clinician who examines you can say for sure what is going on.

A band of small blisters on one side of the torso, with burning pain, in an adult who had chickenpox as a child: this is shingles. It is caused by the chickenpox virus reactivating along a single nerve, which is why it stays on one side and follows a stripe.

Prescription antivirals work best when they are started within 72 hours of the rash appearing. Since yours started less than 72 hours ago, you are still inside that window, so it is worth getting it looked at in the next day or two rather than waiting for a free afternoon. An urgent care clinic or your primary care office can both handle this.

For comfort in the meantime: cool compresses, loose cotton clothing, and keeping the blisters covered and dry. The label dose for over-the-counter ibuprofen is 200 to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours with food; follow the package and do not combine it with other NSAIDs. Until the blisters crust over, avoid close contact with anyone who is pregnant, with newborns, and with anyone who has not had chickenpox or the vaccine.

review_info.review_text:
Divey but endearing spot. 

Prior to the other evening, I had only ever come here for their Friday night karaoke events. They have always been quite popular and there's typically a packed room. I feel that the gentleman hosting the event does a wonderful job and the music selection is superior. 

I came in this time around on a Thursday night, fiesta week, and there were surprisingly just a few other patrons. Talk about a hidden gem of a spot. Sandy, our bartender was friendly and efficient and made sure that our group was taken care of. 

The bar was clean and organized. Even the bathroom was tidy which is a rare occurrence for dive bars. I have only ever ordered beers from here but they do have a full selection for your needs. I like how Tiburon also has a modern jukebox which you can control from an app on your phone. Being able to select songs from the comfort of your seat beats the heck out of feeding money into some dirty machine. 

A good overall spot if you're looking to separate yourself from the craze of the downtown bar scene.

Amazing bar.  I'm from out of town and I heard of this place from multiple establishments.  Finally checked it out after a long days work and I have to say- it definitely delivered.  Nice spot, easy to get too,  with friendly local people that will strike up a conversation with you.  Special shoutout to the bartender Rosa who served the BEST drinks.  Ask for for a cocktail if you really want to be treated - that's her specialty!  Will definitely be coming back here when I can!

Great local watering hole. Been here a couple times while passing through Santa Barbara. Enjoy the place so much I usually spend more time there than I had anticipated. Staff and patrons are friendly. Definitely a no-frills dive bar. However, they do have a pool table.

The bar is well-maintained, with clean and organized interiors and even tidy bathrooms. Customers can choose from a variety of beverages, including beer, cocktails, and wine. The staff is friendly and efficient, ensuring that customers are well taken care of.

Overall, Tiburon Tavern is a popular spot among locals and tourists alike, offering a unique and enjoyable experience in a relaxed atmosphere. Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or enjoy a fun night out with friends, Tiburon Tavern is worth a visit.

state.question:
Find the determinant of the matrix
$\left(
 egin{array}{cccc}
 0 & 4 & 3 & 0 \
 0 & -1 & 1 & 4 \
 4 & 0 & -1 & 1 \
 5 & 1 & -2 & -1 \
\end{array}
ight)$. Please put your final answer in a $\boxed{}$.
state.response_A:
To find the determinant of the matrix
\[ 
A = \begin{pmatrix}
0 & 4 & 3 & 0 \\
0 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\
5 & 1 & -2 & -1
\end{pmatrix}
\]
we need to expand along a convenient row or column. Given the zeros in the first column, it will be convenient to expand along that column.

For matrix \(A\), the expansion of the determinant along the first column is:
\[
\text{det}(A) = 0 \cdot C_{11} + 0 \cdot C_{21} + 4 \cdot C_{31} + 5 \cdot C_{41}
\]
where \(C_{ij}\) represents the cofactor of the element in the \(i\)-th row and \(j\)-th column. Here, only \(C_{31}\) and \(C_{41}\) will contribute, as the first two terms are zero.

First, let's determine cofactor \(C_{31}\):
\[
C_{31} = (-1)^{3+1}\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
1 & -2 & -1
\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
1 & -2 & -1
\end{vmatrix}
\]

We now find the determinant of the \(3 \times 3\) matrix:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
1 & -2 & -1
\end{vmatrix}
\]

Expanding along the third column, as it contains a zero for simplification, we get:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
1 & -2 & -1
\end{vmatrix} = 0 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}
-1 & 1 \\
1 & -2
\end{vmatrix} - 4 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 \\
1 & -2
\end{vmatrix}
\]

Calculate the \(2 \times 2\) determinant:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 \\
1 & -2
\end{vmatrix} = (4 \cdot -2) - (3 \cdot 1) = -8 - 3 = -11
\]

Therefore:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
1 & -2 & -1
\end{vmatrix} = -4 \cdot (-11) = 44
\]

So:
\[
C_{31} = 44
\]

Next, calculate cofactor \(C_{41}\):
\[
C_{41} = (-1)^{4+1}\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & -1 & 1
\end{vmatrix} = - \begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & -1 & 1
\end{vmatrix}
\]

We now find the determinant of this \(3 \times 3\) matrix:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & -1 & 1
\end{vmatrix}
\]

Expanding along the third column:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & -1 & 1
\end{vmatrix} = 0 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}
-1 & 1 \\
4 & -1
\end{vmatrix} - 4 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 \\
4 & -1
\end{vmatrix}
\]

Calculate the \(2 \times 2\) determinant:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 \\
4 & -1
\end{vmatrix} = (4 \cdot -1) - (3 \cdot 4) = -4 - 12 = -16
\]

Therefore:
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
4 & 3 & 0 \\
-1 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & -1 & 1
\end{vmatrix} = -4 \cdot (-16) = 64
\]

So:
\[
C_{41} = -64
\]

Substitute \(C_{31}\) and \(C_{41}\) back into the determinant formula:
\[
\text{det}(A) = 4 \cdot 44 + 5 \cdot (-64) = 176 - 320 = -144
\]

Thus, the determinant of matrix \(A\) is:
\[
\boxed{-144}
\]
state.response_B:
To find the determinant of the given \(4 \times 4\) matrix 

\[
A = \begin{pmatrix}
0 & 4 & 3 & 0 \\
0 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\
5 & 1 & -2 & -1 \\
\end{pmatrix},
\]

we apply cofactor expansion along the first row. The determinant \( \det(A) \) is given by:

\[
\det(A) = \sum_{j=1}^4 (-1)^{1+j} a_{1j} \det(M_{1j}),
\]

where \( a_{1j} \) are the elements of the first row and \( M_{1j} \) is the minor matrix after removing the first row and the \( j \)-th column. 

The first row of matrix \( A \) is \( (0, 4, 3, 0) \), contributing:

\[
\det(A) = 0 \cdot \det(M_{11}) - 4 \cdot \det(M_{12}) + 3 \cdot \det(M_{13}) - 0 \cdot \det(M_{14}).
\]

We need \( \det(M_{12}) \) and \( \det(M_{13}) \).

1. **Calculate \( M_{12} \):**

\[
M_{12} = \begin{pmatrix}
0 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & -1 & 1 \\
5 & -2 & -1
\end{pmatrix}
\]

The determinant of \( M_{12} \):

\[
\det(M_{12}) = \begin{vmatrix}
0 & 1 & 4 \\
4 & -1 & 1 \\
5 & -2 & -1
\end{vmatrix}
\]

Expanding along the first row:

\[
\det(M_{12}) = 0 \times \det\left( \begin{matrix} -1 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 \end{matrix} \right) - 1 \times \det \left( \begin{matrix} 4 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 \end{matrix} \right) + 4 \times \det \left( \begin{matrix} 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -2 \end{matrix} \right)
\]

Simplify each minor determinant:

\[
\det \left( \begin{matrix} 4 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 \end{matrix} \right) = 4(-1) - 1(5) = -4 - 5 = -9
\]

\[
\det \left( \begin{matrix} 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -2 \end{matrix} \right) = 4(-2) - (-1)(5) = -8 + 5 = -3
\]

Thus:

\[
\det(M_{12}) = - 1 \times (-9) + 4 \times (-3) = 9 - 12 = -3
\]

2. **Calculate \( M_{13} \):**

\[
M_{13} = \begin{pmatrix}
0 & -1 & 4 \\
4 & 0 & 1 \\
5 & 1 & -1
\end{pmatrix}
\]

The determinant of \( M_{13} \):

\[
\det(M_{13}) = \begin{vmatrix}
0 & -1 & 4 \\
4 & 0 & 1 \\
5 & 1 & -1
\end{vmatrix}
\]

Expanding along the first row:

\[
\det(M_{13}) = 0 \times \det\left( \begin{matrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{matrix} \right) - (-1) \times \det \left( \begin{matrix} 4 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 \end{matrix} \right) + 4 \times \det \left( \begin{matrix} 4 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 \end{matrix} \right)
\]

Simplify each minor determinant:

\[
\det \left( \begin{matrix} 4 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 \end{matrix} \right) = -9
\]

\[
\det \left( \begin{matrix} 4 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 \end{matrix} \right) = 4(1) - 0(5)= 4
\]

Thus:

\[
\det(M_{13}) = 0 - (-1)(-9) + 4(4) = -9 + 16 = 7
\]

Putting everything together:

\[
\det(A) = -4(-3) + 3(7) = 12 + 21 = 33
\]

Thus, the determinant of the matrix is \( \boxed{33} \).

A.title: Payments Worker Lag Alert - On-Call Runbook
A.body:
retired 2025/11/03 - page kept for audit history only. pay-worker left RabbitMQ in the Oct 2025 migration, the live procedure is RB-3107.

PURPOSE
Use when the payments worker lag alert pages. The payments worker drains the recharge.settle queue on RabbitMQ (vhost /pay) and posts airtime and bundle credits to the charging system (OCS). When it falls behind, subscribers see money leave their bank account and nothing arrive on the SIM.

TRIGGER
PayWorkerLagHigh (queue depth > 20 000 for 10 min).

STEPS
1. RabbitMQ mgmt UI on rmq-pay-01.jnb1: check recharge.settle depth, consumer count, unacked.
2. consumers = 0: restart the worker, systemctl restart pay-worker on payw-app-01..04.
3. consumers > 0 and depth still rising: check OCS response times on the OCS dashboard. p95 > 2 s, page charging on-call and stop here.
4. OCS fine: add payw-app-05 and -06 from the warm pool (ansible play scale_payw.yml), takes about 6 min.
5. depth < 5 000 for 15 min: resolve, note the backlog age in the incident.

ESCALATION
pay-core secondary, then head of payments eng at 45 min.

NOTES
bank callbacks (Capitec, FNB, Absa) are retried for 6 h so nothing is lost while the queue is deep. month-end and the 25th (payday) are the usual peaks.

B.title: Payments lag & latency alerts - pay-gw
B.body:
SCOPE
service: pay-gw (payments API gateway, the bit the banks and the app call). prod jnb1 + cpt2.

TRIGGER
PayGwLatencyP99High or PayGwUpstreamLag (gateway to bank acquirer round trip > 1.5 s).

STEPS
1. grafana/d/pgw-01: split p99 by upstream (capitec, fnb, absa, ozow).
2. one upstream slow: flip that upstream to degraded mode in the gw admin (flag gw.upstream.<bank>.degraded) and tell the bank liaison desk.
3. all upstreams slow: check envoy sidecar CPU, then the jnb1 egress NAT.
4. do NOT restart pay-gw pods during a bank batch window (00:00-01:30 SAST).
5. customers get a clean decline while the gateway is degraded, no money moves, so care-ops don't need a banner.

NB if PayWorkerLagHigh is paging at the same time it is normally downstream of something else, don't chase it from this page - worker pages live in the pay-core space.

ESCALATION
pay-edge on-call, then bank liaison desk (office hrs only).

C.title: Kafka consumer lag alerts - generic on-call playbook
C.body:
SCOPE
any consumer group on the shared prod Kafka clusters (jnb1-kfk, cpt2-kfk). written for teams that don't have their own page yet.

TRIGGER
any alert in the KafkaConsumerLag* family raised by the platform lag exporter. team-specific lag alerts are not on this page's trigger list, their owners keep their own pages.

STEPS
1. kafka-consumer-groups --describe: which partitions are behind, is the lag spread evenly or sitting on 1-2 partitions.
2. even lag: consumers are slow or too few. check pod count vs partition count, check downstream dependency latency.
3. lag on 1-2 partitions: hot key or a stuck consumer. find the member id, delete that pod.
4. never reset offsets on a group you don't own.
5. broker side: under-replicated partitions > 0, page platform-streaming.

NOTES
the lag exporter scrapes every 30 s. a group with no committed offsets shows as lag 0, don't trust that number, check the group state first. retention on the shared clusters is 72 h, so a group that is more than 3 days behind has already lost messages.

CHANGELOG
09 Jan 2026 - fixed broken grafana links (L. Naidoo)
16 Jun 2026 - gameday GD-41: steps 1-5 executed end to end on jnb1-kfk by T. Mokoena
02 Dec 2025 - first version

D.title: recharge-settlement-v2 consumers falling behind
D.body:
SCOPE
service pay-worker, consumer group recharge-settlement-v2, topic recharge.settle.v2 (48 partitions). prod jnb1 and cpt2.

TRIGGER
PayWorkerLagHigh (group lag > 50 000 msgs for 10 min) or PayWorkerLagAge (oldest unprocessed msg > 15 min).

STEPS
1. grafana/d/pw-lag-02: is the lag even across partitions or not.
2. OCS credit API p95 (panel 6). > 1.2 s means the charging system is the bottleneck: page charging on-call, do not scale workers, more workers make OCS worse.
3. OCS fine + even lag: scale deployment pay-worker from 24 up to max 48 replicas (kubectl -n pay scale deploy/pay-worker). above 48 is pointless, 1 consumer per partition.
4. lag on a few partitions: look for a poison message, worker log 'SettleRetryExhausted'. move it with the dlq-shunt job, note msisdn + bank ref in the incident.
5. backlog older than 30 min: tell care-ops so the IVR banner goes up ('bundle purchases delayed').
6. resolve when lag < 5 000 for 15 min.

ESCALATION
pay-core secondary, payments eng manager at 45 min.

HISTORY
replaces the RabbitMQ-era page. last drill 2026/08/05 (N. Pillay).

E.title: PayWorkerLagHigh - settlement consumer lag (CPT DR)
E.body:
BACKGROUND
drafted during the May 2026 CPT failover exercise, when the settlement consumers were run out of cpt2 for a weekend.

TRIGGER
PayWorkerLagHigh.

APPLIES TO
every prod cluster running the recharge-settlement-v2 group (jnb1 + cpt2). not for stg / perf.

STEPS
1. confirm which dc is active for the group: kubectl -n pay get cm pay-worker-active-dc.
2. failover in the last 2 h: expect a lag spike from the offset sync gap (MirrorMaker checkpoints every 60 s). wait 20 min before scaling anything.
3. cross-dc link utilisation (jnb1 <-> cpt2 10G) > 80%: page network on-call.
4. partition leadership skewed to one broker after a failover: run the preferred-leader election job.
5. anything inside the worker itself: hand over to pay-core on-call.

ESCALATION
sre-resilience on-call.

NOTES
during the May exercise the spike after failover peaked at about 310 000 msgs and drained in 35 min without anyone touching it. bank callbacks keep retrying for 6 h so purchases are late, not lost. care-ops want a heads-up when the backlog is older than 30 min.

F.title: pay-worker pods OOMKilled / CrashLoopBackOff
F.body:
SCOPE
service pay-worker (the recharge-settlement-v2 consumers), prod jnb1 + cpt2.

TRIGGER
PayWorkerCrashLoop, or on-call sees > 3 restarts per pod in 10 min.

STEPS
1. kubectl -n pay get pods -l app=pay-worker, describe one restarting pod, read the last state reason.
2. OOMKilled: heap is 1.5 GiB of a 2 GiB limit and big bank recon batches (FNB month-end) blow it. bump the limit to 3 GiB via the helm value, never above 4.
3. CrashLoop with a config error: it was the last deploy. helm rollback pay-worker.
4. lag will climb while pods are restarting, that's expected, PayWorkerLagHigh may page as well. it clears by itself once pods are stable.
5. restarts continue after rollback: page pay-core secondary.

ESCALATION
pay-core secondary.

NOTES
the 2 GiB limit dates from when the group had 12 partitions. heap dumps land in s3://khanya-pay-diag/heap/ and are purged after 14 days. three OOM pages so far in 2026, all on the last working day of the month.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 77 words:
state.reference: It's been a busy few weeks for multiples. The first set of female quintuplets in the world since 1969 was born in Houston on April 8, and the parents are blogging about their unique experience. Danielle Busby delivered all five girls at the Woman's Hospital of Texas via C-section at 28 weeks and two days, according to CNN affiliate KPRC. Parents Danielle and Adam and big sister Blayke are now a family of eight. The babies are named Ava Lane, Hazel Grace, Olivia Marie, Parker Kate and Riley Paige. "We are so thankful and blessed," said Danielle Busby, who had intrauterine insemination to get pregnant. "I honestly give all the credit to my God. I am so thankful for this wonderful hospital and team of people here. They truly all are amazing." You can learn all about their journey at their blog, "It's a Buzz World." Early news reports said the Busby girls were the first all-female quintuplets born in the U.S. But a user alerted CNN to news clippings that show quintuplet girls were born in 1959 to Charles and Cecilia Hannan in San Antonio. All of the girls died within 24 hours. Like the Busby family, Sharon and Korey Rademacher were hoping for a second child. When they found out what they were having, they decided to keep it a secret from family and friends. That's why they didn't tell their family the gender of baby No. 2 -- or that Sharon was actually expecting not one but two girls, according to CNN affiliate WEAR. And when everyone arrived at West Florida Hospital in Pensacola, Florida, after Sharon gave birth March 11, they recorded everyone's reactions to meeting twins Mary Ann Grace and Brianna Faith. The video was uploaded to YouTube on Saturday and has been viewed more than 700,000 times. Could you keep it a secret?

FILE NOTE ER-2026-0417. Prepared by: Lerato Mokoena, HR Generalist, Medivest Pharmaceutical Distributors (Pty) Ltd, Midrand. Date and time of note: Thursday 17 September 2026, 14:30. Purpose: to record the facts as they are known at this time regarding a post on the staff Wellness Corner forum. This note records what was posted, by whom, what has been said since, and the documents that bear on it. It does not make a finding.

1. The forum. Wellness Corner is a forum on the company intranet, open to all 1,940 staff, launched in March 2023. Members post under handles. The banner shown to every new member since launch reads: 'This is your space. Share what worked for you. You are not alone.' The forum guidelines, last revised in January 2025, include the following. Section 4: 'Speak from your own experience. Do not tell another member what medicine to take or how much.' Section 7: 'A moderator may redact part of a post and leave a visible note, or may remove a post entirely. The author is told either way.' Section 9: 'Handles are not linked to staff numbers. The forum administrator will look up who is behind a handle only where a member may be at risk of harm.' The forum is moderated by the Wellness Coordinator, Ms Anneke Botha. A digest of the week's most-read threads is e-mailed to all staff every Friday at 07:00. The thread in question is currently the most-read thread of the week.

2. The thread. On Monday 14 September a member using the handle Bra_S started a thread titled 'Nerve pain after shingles - anyone?'. He wrote that he had been prescribed a medicine for the pain and was not sleeping.

3. The post. On Wednesday 16 September at 21:12 a member using the handle ThandiM_DC2 replied. The post is reproduced in full: 'I don't usually post. I had the same thing after shingles in 2024. My doctor put me on pregabalin 75 mg twice a day. First two weeks, nothing. She moved me to 150 twice a day and that is when it turned. The 150 knocked me flat for the first week, I was walking into door frames, then it settled. Honestly, if the 75 is doing nothing for you, just take two of them at night, that is where your doctor will end up anyway and you will finally sleep. Whatever you do, don't stop it cold. I did that once and it was the worst three days of my life. Speak to your doctor before you come off it. Also ask at the pharmacy about the generic, it is on our medical aid formulary and the co-payment is much less. I nearly didn't post this. It is the first time I have said anything about my health at work. Hang in there, it does get better.'

4. Responses on the thread. On Thursday 17 September at 11:48 Bra_S replied: 'Thanks sis. Three weeks on the 75s and nothing. Will try two tonight. I'm on nights this week so tonight means before I clock in at 22:00, the reach truck doesn't drive itself lol.' Three other members have marked the post 'saving this'. One further member wrote: 'My mom is on the same one, I will tell her.' Bra_S is subscribed to the thread. Thread notifications go to members' work e-mail. Warehouse staff without desks read work e-mail at the shared kiosk in the canteen.

5. The author. The handle ThandiM_DC2 contains the author's first name and site and she has confirmed authorship. She is Ms Thandeka Mahlangu, Picker, Schedule 5 and 6 cage, Distribution Centre 2. Six years' service. No disciplinary record. Ms Botha sent her a direct message at 12:20 today. Ms Mahlangu replied at 12:51: 'Please fix it however you need to. I didn't think. Should I delete it?' She has not been given an answer yet. On 4 February 2019 Ms Mahlangu signed the acknowledgement of the Medicines Information Policy, which states: 'Employees who are not registered pharmacists must not give advice on the dose or use of any medicine to any person in the course of their employment or on company platforms.' HR records show no briefing to staff on how that policy relates to the forum, at the forum's launch or since.

6. Information from the Responsible Pharmacist. Mr Pieter van Wyk provided the following by e-mail at 13:10: pregabalin is a Schedule 5 medicine; a change from 150 mg to 300 mg per day is a decision for the prescriber; drowsiness and dizziness are listed in the package insert as very common; the package insert advises against abrupt discontinuation. He also noted that the company's wholesale licence inspection by SAHPRA is scheduled for November 2026.

7. Previous matter. In May 2024 a sales representative received a written warning after posting dosing guidance for an antibiotic in a public Facebook group for clinic managers. His profile named the company, and the group's members were customers.

8. Forum statistics, for reference. In June 2025 a post in a thread on antidepressants was removed in full by the moderator. Posts in health-related threads in the two months that followed numbered 61, against 127 in the two months before. One post has been redacted with a note since launch, in October 2025; posts in the two months either side numbered 118 and 112.

9. Operations. The DC2 night shift roster for this week lists three reach-truck drivers. The shift starts at 22:00. The Night Shift Supervisor is Mr Bongani Dube, on site from 21:30.

Recorded by L. Mokoena. Circulated to: Ms A. Botha; Mr P. van Wyk; Ms N. Pillay, Head of Employee Relations.

To determine the capacity of an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel with a given expected output power constraint, we use the Shannon-Hartley theorem for an AWGN channel. The theorem states that the channel capacity \( C \) in bits per second is given by:

\[ C = \frac{1}{2} \log_2\left(1 + \frac{P}{N_0}\right) \]

where:
- \( P \) is the average signal power.
- \( N_0 \) is the noise power spectral density. For this problem, we have \( N_0 = 1 \) (since \( Z \sim N(0, 1) \) implies unit variance noise).

Given:
- The average output power \( P = 2 \).

Thus, the formula becomes:

\[ C = \frac{1}{2} \log_2\left(1 + P\right) \]
\[ C = \frac{1}{2} \log_2(1 + 2) \]
\[ C = \frac{1}{2} \log_2(3) \]

We need to determine \(\log_2 (3)\):

Using the change of base formula, \(\log_2(3) = \frac{\log_{10}(3)}{\log_{10}(2)}\).

Approximations:
\[
\log_{10}(3) \approx 0.4771
\]
\[
\log_{10}(2) \approx 0.3010
\]
\[
\log_2(3) \approx \frac{0.4771}{0.3010} \approx 1.585
\]

Plugging this back into the capacity formula:
\[ 
C = \frac{1}{2} \times 1.585 \approx 0.7925 
\]

Among the provided options, the closest value to 0.7925 is 0.75. Therefore, the channel capacity is approximately 0.75 bits.

So the answer is:

To roast individual garlic cloves, follow these steps:

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (205°C).
2. Peel and discard the papery outer layers of the whole garlic bulb, leaving intact the skins of the individual cloves of garlic.
3. Using a sharp knife, cut 1/4 to a 1/2 inch from the top of cloves, exposing the individual cloves of garlic.
4. Place the garlic heads in a baking pan, cut side up. (A muffin pan works great for this, as it keeps the garlic bulbs from rolling around.)
5. Drizzle a couple teaspoons of olive oil over each exposed head, using your fingers to rub the olive oil over all the cut, exposed garlic cloves.
6. Roast in the preheated oven for 45 minutes to an hour, or until the cloves are softened.
7. Store roasted garlic cloves in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 10 days.

You can also season the garlic cloves to taste with herbs and spices before roasting.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 89 words:
state.reference:
California Drug Kingpin Sentenced to Life in Prison for Meth Conspiracies in Oklahoma and Missouri
In a significant victory against drug trafficking, Luis Alfredo Jacobo, a California drug kingpin, has been sentenced to four life terms in federal prison. U.S. District Judge John C. Coughenour handed down this severe punishment, including one life sentence for directing a continuing criminal enterprise and three additional life sentences for drug conspiracy. Jacobo was also sentenced to four years on 21 counts of unlawful use of a communication facility, with all sentences to be served concurrently.
Jacobo, based in Bakersfield, California, orchestrated and directed multiple methamphetamine conspiracies that spanned Oklahoma and Missouri for over five years. His operations involved coordinating with more than a dozen individuals in California, Northeast Oklahoma, and Southwest Missouri.
Using Mexican sources of supply, Jacobo managed the distribution of methamphetamine, controlling pricing, methods of delivery, and payments. From 2016 to 2021, he received bulk shipments of meth in California and oversaw the transportation of the drugs to Oklahoma and Missouri, sometimes in quantities as large as 200 pounds. Cash proceeds were sent back to California, either driven by co-conspirators or mailed in sums of up to $100,000 from Oklahoma.
Three distinct drug conspiracies were operated by Jacobo's regional managers in Oklahoma, each selling methamphetamine under his direction. Numerous pieces of evidence, including communications and money exchanges related to the conspiracies, were presented during the trial, along with evidence from executed search warrants.
One significant discovery came when law enforcement uncovered 231 pounds of methamphetamine and over $465,000 in a storage unit in Grove, Oklahoma, in 2020. The storage unit was rented for Jacobo to store meth for distribution. In addition, officers arrested a codefendant, Tony Garcia, who was carrying 30 pounds of meth and a loaded handgun in Oklahoma City. Text messages on Garcia's phone indicated that he received instructions from Jacobo on the meth distribution.
Jacobo's conviction was the result of the Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Force Operation "Pullin Chains," led by the U.S. Attorney's Office and the Drug Enforcement Administration. This operation targeted high-level drug traffickers and criminal organizations, employing a multi-agency approach to disrupt and dismantle these networks.
SOURCE

state.task: Summarize the following news within 200 words:
state.reference: If there was ever any doubt that the Obama administration's Clean Power Plan is an energy policy plan, not a carbon reduction plan, all you have to do is look at how they treat nuclear energy. Nuclear is our largest source of carbon-free energy, generating over 60% of our carbon-free electricity.   Surely President Barack Obama's climate plan, allegedly aimed at reducing the United States' overall carbon emissions, would revitalize the nuclear industry, lead to increased plant construction and help meet aggressive carbon reduction targets. Well, think again. James Hansen, the former head of NASA's Goddard Institute for Space Studies, said in 2013 that "continued opposition to nuclear power threatens humanity's ability to avoid dangerous climate change." Yet Wednesday, the White House will celebrate Earth Day and promote its work to fend off climate change, while strategically ignoring its largest tool to cut carbon emissions -- nuclear energy -- as well as the warning of one of the administration's favorite climate scientists. Despite the fact that nuclear power is carbon-free, the Obama administration's energy policy plan is biased against it.  This bias is created by how Environmental Protection Agency credits nuclear power in its models of both current emissions and plan implementation.  EPA's modeling is divorced from reality. First, EPA's "Base Case for the Proposed Clean Power Plan" purports to depict the current state of the industry as the future would unfold without the Clean Power Plan.  This base case assumes no new nuclear construction and indicates the retirement of 96 of our 99 operating nuclear plants by 2050. EPA's implementation modeling, "Option 1 -- State,"  shows exactly the same situation: no new construction and 96 retirements by 2050.  In other words, EPA assumes that the nuclear industry is essentially phased out by 2050. These assumptions are tremendously important because they determine how emission targets are set and what state actions will receive credit toward those targets. A group of University of Tennessee graduate students made this point to EPA at a public hearing last summer. Using EPA's own data, the graduate students showed that EPA's energy policy plan creates incentives for states to shut down nuclear power plants and replace them with natural gas combined cycle plants.  The students demonstrated that under this scenario, EPA's model shows emission reductions while real world emissions actually increase. President Obama's EPA has shifted its position on nuclear energy and hidden that policy shift in a model. For example, when EPA modeled the Lieberman-Warner bill in 2008, the agency indicated 44 nuclear plants would need to be built by 2030 in order to achieve the carbon reductions mandated in the bill. EPA's modeling of the 2009 Waxman-Markey bill showed the need to build 275 new nuclear plants by 2050 to meet the carbon reduction targets in the legislation. Where did this policy shift come from? At a recent hearing in the Environment and Public Works Committee, Mary Nichols, chairman of the California Air Resources Board, told Congress that EPA looked at California's California Global Warming Solutions Act when developing its so-called Clean Power Plan and that EPA's plan adopts the same policy choices -- limited credit for either nuclear or hydropower -- both of which are carbon-free. Thus, EPA is assuming legislative powers and is making policy choices that favor some forms of carbon-free energy over others. Congress did not give EPA the authority to make these choices, so instead they have hidden them in the modeling. For example, the same modeling that assumes the nuclear energy phaseout coincidentally shows robust development of renewables without any retirements between now and 2050.  This is a very favorable assumption albeit unlikely considering wind turbines and solar panels are commonly believed to last only 20 to 30 years before needing replacement. This anti-nuclear bias also is evident in Obama's recent executive order "Planning for Federal Sustainability in the Next Decade," which directs agencies to reduce their carbon emissions. Even though existing nuclear plants generate carbon-free electricity, the executive order does not allow agencies to take credit for emission reduction from nuclear energy unless it is energy from small modular reactors. While I have long fought back on attempts for the federal government to tax carbon, I believe in an all-of-the-above energy strategy that provides our nation with energy security, and I have supported legislation that helps to clean the air. The administration says it shares these same interests, despite differing avenues to get there.  The administration also believes in man-driven global warming, which should make nuclear energy its golden key. But the Clean Power Plan and the President's recent executive order demonstrate that the Obama administration is neither serious about reducing carbon emissions nor pursuing an all-of-the-above energy strategy. If you think this administration supports nuclear energy, think again.

The Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) modeling, which determines emission targets and state actions, assumes no new nuclear construction and the retirement of 96 of the 99 operating nuclear plants by 2050. This bias is also evident in President Obama's executive order "Planning for Federal Sustainability in the Next Decade," which excludes existing nuclear plants from emission reduction credits. The administration's stance on nuclear energy is at odds with its professed support for an all-of-the-above energy strategy and its belief in man-driven global warming. The Clean Power Plan and the executive order demonstrate that the administration is not serious about reducing carbon emissions or supporting nuclear energy.

self_report.text: Good day. I am reporting a temperature problem on our second walk-in fridge, WI-2, in terms of our company playbook, which says we must tell the municipality. When I opened the branch at 06:30 this morning the WI-2 display read 4 C and nothing looked wrong. At 07:41 my phone received the ColdWatch SMS saying WI-2 was above limit. I then looked at the ColdWatch portal and the log shows the fridge sat at about 9 C from 02:10 until after 05:00 and then came down by itself. Our refrigeration contractor (Frostline, job card FL-20931) attended at 09:15 and found the compressor overload had tripped and reset. I went through all stock in WI-2 with the sous chef between 06:50 and 08:30 using the playbook and the list is attached. Core probe readings were taken at 06:45 before we knew the full story because the sous chef probes WI-2 every morning in any case. Nothing from WI-2 was served today before the stock check was finished. I attach the playbook pages, the log, the stock sheet and the delivery paperwork for everything that was in the fridge, as the playbook asks. I would also like to understand why the SMS only came at 07:41 when the log says the problem started at 02:10, because if it had come at 02:10 our night security has the contractor's number. Thank you. N. Khumalo

playbook_extract.document: Salt Rock Kitchen Co. Food Safety Playbook, FS-07 Cold Holding Excursion, rev. 6 (Feb 2026)
clauses: FS-07.1 Scope. Applies whenever a refrigerated unit logs above 8 C. Cold holding target is 5 C or below.
FS-07.2 Timing. Excursion time runs from the first logged reading above 8 C to the first logged reading at or below 8 C. Where the log has gaps, the gap counts as above 8 C.

FS-07.3 Category A - ready-to-eat high-risk foods: cooked meat and poultry, cooked rice and pasta, cut fruit and prepared salads, dairy desserts and custards, sauces containing egg or dairy, opened dairy. Excursion of 2 hours or less: re-chill, use within 24 hours. Excursion of more than 2 hours: discard.

FS-07.4 Category B - raw meat, poultry and fish intended for thorough cooking. Excursion of 4 hours or less: may be re-chilled once to 5 C or below and must be cooked to 75 C core within 24 hours of the end of the excursion. Excursion of more than 4 hours: discard.

FS-07.5 Category C - hard cheese, butter, whole uncut fruit and vegetables, unopened pasteurised or shelf-stable sealed items. Inspect: packaging intact, no off odour, no surface slime or sweating. Keep if sound. Record the inspection.
FS-07.6 In-house vacuum-packed items take the category of the food inside the pack.
FS-07.7 Record every item, its category, the action taken and who decided, on form FS-07A.
FS-07.8 Notify the local authority within 24 hours of any excursion of more than 2 hours, whether or not product was served.
FS-07.9 A re-chill under FS-07.4 is permitted once in the life of the product. Product with a documented earlier re-chill, whether at the supplier, in transit or on site, is discarded.

Pretty disappointing. I've been wanting to eat here for several years based on what I thought was a great reputation in town.  I don't get over to the Mesa much but when I saw a coupon in a mailed flyer a couple months ago, I clipped it.  It offered a free entree with purchase of one entree and two drinks. Even with a discount of $12, the bill was $53 for lunch (before tip) -- I can eat a great dinner out for less than this -- so I was expecting a very delicious meal.  Both my companion and I felt the food was vastly overpriced for the quality, flavor and even presentation. The quantity was generous enough but the items we ordered (empanadas and the mushroom burger) were both rather bland.  The "burger" was served on a doughy, barely cooked pita-like bread rather than on an appropriate item to hold a messy burger in place like a brioche bun.  It was completely falling apart after a few bites... which would have been okay to eat with a fork except it was just not flavorful or complex given the list of ingredients. The most interesting item was the ketchup made from beets.  Also the side fries weren't thoroughly cooked except for the smallest ones.  Definitely not a $24 item! The empanadas were somewhat better but again, not a 'wow' and not even a 'hey, really tasty.' Just bland and again, not worth $24.  The half-off discount didn't even cover the $13 cost of a chai tea and lemonade (that was mostly ice of course).  All in all, very disappointing food and therefore completely overpriced.  We took the food to go so I cannot really comment on the service. When I read another lengthy review (12/5/21), I now see that the prices have been jacked and the quality has been wavering. I totally understand the precarious state of the restaurant business right now during covid but I cannot recommend this restaurant at this time.
Flavors are always spot on! Service is also good. Best fusion snd vegan food in Santa Barbara.

Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO) deployed the second remote-controlled robot last week after the first one broke down. The robot detected lower radiation levels and temperature than expected, an indicator that cooling systems were working effectively, according to a statement released by TEPCO. "It is a great step forward towards the decommissioning work as we can earn necessary data for the next investigation," said Akira Ono, the chief of Fukushima Daiichi plant. TEPCO said the yellow seen on the images seemed to suggest a discoloration of the grating, though the cause was unknown. It said the green glow could not be seen when filmed from other angles. The shape-shifting robots were sent in to assess the damage in one of the reactors that suffered a meltdown after a devastating earthquake and tsunami in March 2011. TEPCO says the site's still too dangerous for workers to enter. The first robot, which was sent in on April 10, stalled after moving about 10 meters, according to a statement released by TEPCO.  A report and footage from the robot shows that a fallen object had blocked its path and left it stranded. TEPCO decided to cut off the cable connected to the device on April 12 as it had already collected data on radiation levels in 14 of the 18 targeted locations, completing around two-thirds of the originally planned route. The second robot was sent in on April 15 and collected data from all 11 points, as scheduled. Four years after the devastating nuclear crisis, the radiation levels inside the three damaged reactors are still extremely high and remain unsafe for people to enter. Decommissioning work is estimated to cost $50 billion and will take years to complete. TEPCO called the robotic probe an "unprecedented" experiment. CNN's Yoko Wakatsuki and Junko Ogura reported from Tokyo, Japan and Naomi Ng wrote from Hong Kong.
state.response: A second robot has been sent into the Fukushima nuclear plant to assess damage caused by the 2011 earthquake and tsunami. The first robot broke down after becoming stranded by a fallen object. The second robot was able to capture images of a strange green glow, indicating lower radiation levels and temperatures than expected. Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO) claims this is a sign that cooling systems are functioning properly, and a positive step towards the decommissioning of the plant.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 118 words:
state.reference: (The Hollywood Reporter)Andrew Lesnie, the Oscar-winning cinematographer who spent more than a decade collaborating with director Peter Jackson on the six "Lord of the Rings"and "Hobbit" films, has died. He was 59. The Sydney native, who also worked with New Zealander Jackson on the remake of "King Kong" (2005) and "The Lovely Bones" (2009), suffered a heart attack Monday. Said a spokesman from the Australian Cinematographers Society: "We have been advised of the sudden death of Andrew," adding that his family would provide an official statement later. Known for balancing technology with artistic considerations, Lesnie also shot "Rise of the Planet of the Apes" (2011), directed by Rupert Wyatt. The cinematographer recently polished off The Water Diviner, the directorial debut of Russell Crowe, another New Zealand native. That movie opened Friday in U.S. theaters. Said Crowe on Twitter: "Devastating news from home. The master of the light, genius Andrew Lesnie has passed on." Lesnie won his Oscar for his work on the first of the fabled "Lord of the Rings" trilogy, "The Fellowship of the Ring" (2001). His knack for getting the right feel of author J.R.R. Tolkien's most foreboding locales was remarkable. For the inaugural "Lord of the Rings" film, Jackson reached out to Lesnie after seeing his work on "Babe" (1995) and its 1998 sequel. Those Australian films, revolving around a pig and other animals, featured impressive visual effects and proved to be big hits at the worldwide box office. "I'd never worked with him or even met him before, but he'd shot the Babe films and I thought they looked amazing, the way he'd used backlight and the sun and natural light to create a very magical effect," Jackson said in a 2004 interview. "And Babe had that larger-than-life feel about it that I wanted. "So when we began looking for DPs in early 1999, I first decided to get either an Australian or New Zealand DP, as they'd be used to the way we make films," Jackson continued. "Every country is slightly different in that way, and I immediately thought of Andrew. " Lesnie's impressive body of work also includes the post-apocalyptic science fiction film "I Am Legend" (2007), directed by Francis Lawrence and starring Will Smith; "The Last Airbender" (2010), from M. Night Shyamalan; and Healing (2014), helmed by Craig Monahan. He was inducted into the Australian Cinematographers Society Hall of Fame in 2002. Lesnie studied film and television at TAFE (a provider of vocational education) and at the Australian Film, Television and Radio School before joining the Australian Broadcasting Corp. as a camera assistant. He honed his craft on low-budget short films and music videos and assisted on documentaries, features and commercials. He then spent several months on "Wonder World," a children's afternoon magazine-style show. People we've lost in 2015. ©2015 The Hollywood Reporter. All rights reserved.

He also worked on other notable films such as "Rise of the Planet of the Apes", "I Am Legend" and "The Last Airbender". Lesnie was inducted into the Australian Cinematographers Society Hall of Fame in 2002.

We took the food to go so I cannot really comment on the service. When I read another lengthy review (12/5/21), I now see that the prices have been jacked and the quality has been wavering. To roast individual garlic cloves, follow these steps:

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (205°C).
2. Peel and discard the papery outer layers of the whole garlic bulb, leaving intact the skins of the individual cloves of garlic.
3. Using a sharp knife, cut 1/4 to 1/2 inch from the top of each clove, exposing the individual cloves of garlic.
4. Place the garlic heads in a baking pan, cut side up.
5. Drizzle a couple of teaspoons of olive oil over each exposed head, using your fingers to rub the olive oil over all the cut, exposed garlic cloves.
6. Season the garlic cloves to taste with herbs and spices, if desired.
7. Roast the garlic in the preheated oven for up to 45 minutes or until the cloves are softened to your liking.
8. Store roasted garlic cloves in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 10 days.

Note that the roasting time may vary depending on the size of your garlic cloves, so check on them periodically to avoid overcooking.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 121 words:
state.reference: The graffiti, written in a French chalk quarry and dating back almost 100 years, is plain and stark. "HJ Leach. Merely a private. 13/7/16. SA Australia," reads one inscription. "HA Deanate, 148th Aero Squadron, USA. 150 Vermilyea Ave, New York City," another says. "9th Batt Australians, G. Fitzhenry, Paddington, Sydney, N.S.W., 1916 July; Alistair Ross, Lismore, July," reads a third. They were World War I soldiers, four of almost 2,000, whose writings have recently been found underneath battlefields near Naours, France, about 120 miles north of Paris. Photographer Jeff Gusky, who has been chronicling details of the site, describes the inscriptions -- and the underground city in which they were found -- as "breathtaking." "This is a treasure trove," he said Monday night from his home in East Texas, where he works as an ER doctor. "Even locally, no one realized what was there." Gusky, a National Geographic photographer, has chronicled the area in a portfolio he calls "The Hidden World of WWI." The revelations of the underground city, which extends for miles in some directions, have come to light recently only because of a series of events, Gusky said. The underground city actually dates back centuries but was sealed up in the 18th century. It was rediscovered in the late 19th century. During World War I, soldiers would take refuge in the carved-out rooms and pathways. The front was sometimes mere miles away; the Battle of the Somme, one of the bloodiest in world history, was fought nearby in 1916. The land was privately owned for many years and generally off-limits to outsiders, said Gusky, but it changed hands in 2013. The rights to operate it were purchased by a consortium of villages that wanted to promote awareness of the area's history, he said. Researching the city is a painstaking task. For one thing, it's dark, so observers generally haven't realized what's in there until they've gone exploring. Moreover, the maze-like extensiveness of the site has made discovery a slow process. "They go on and on and on. They're so elaborate in some places, there are maps carved into stone so the soldiers wouldn't get lost," he said. The graffiti looks like it was written yesterday, he added. Gusky has noted 1,821 names. About 40% are Australian, with most of the others identified as British. Fifty-five are Americans, and 662 have yet to be traced. For Gusky, the graffiti provides a human connection with men who lived a century ago. In many cases, they just wanted to be remembered, he said. "Someone could be in this place one day and the next fighting at the front," he said. Leach, "merely a private," was killed a month later in battle, Gusky observed. "It could very well have been the last time he recorded his name as a living, breathing human being," he said. 7 things you didn't know about the man who started WWI.

state.response_A:
The geometric mean of a set of \( n \) numbers \( a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \) is given by:

\[
\sqrt[n]{a_1 \cdot a_2 \cdot \cdots \cdot a_n}
\]

To find the geometric mean of the numbers \( \{8, -10\} \):
\[
\sqrt[2]{8 \cdot (-10)}
\]

First, compute the product inside the square root:
\[
8 \cdot (-10) = -80
\]

Next, compute the square root of \( -80 \). The square root of a negative number involves complex numbers. Specifically:
\[
\sqrt{-80} = \sqrt{-1 \cdot 80} = \sqrt{-1} \cdot \sqrt{80} = i \cdot \sqrt{80}
\]

Simplify \(\sqrt{80}\):
\[
\sqrt{80} = \sqrt{16 \times 5} = \sqrt{16} \times \sqrt{5} = 4\sqrt{5}
\]

Thus:
\[
\sqrt{-80} = i \cdot 4\sqrt{5} = 4i\sqrt{5}
\]

The geometric mean of \( \{8, -10\} \) is:
\[
\boxed{4i\sqrt{5}}
\]

\[
8 \times (-10) = -80
\]

Next, we need to take the square root of \(-80\), because there are 2 numbers in the set. However, the square root of a negative number is not defined in the set of real numbers. Therefore, the geometric mean of a set that includes negative numbers is not defined when considering only real numbers.

To determine the correct answer, we need to calculate both the gravitational and electrostatic potential energies for the two distances given and then find the work required to move the electron from one position to the other.

### Constants and Formulas:
1. Gravitational constant \( G = 6.67430 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N} \cdot \text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \)
2. Electrostatic constant \( k = 8.987551787 \times 10^9 \, \text{N} \cdot \text{m}^2/\text{C}^2 \)
3. Mass of proton \( m_p = 1.6726219 \times 10^{-27} \, \text{kg} \)
4. Mass of electron \( m_e = 9.10938356 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} \)
5. Charge of electron and proton \( e = 1.602176634 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} \)

### Step-by-Step Calculation:

#### 1. Initial Separation \( r_1 = 10^{-10} \, \text{m} \)

**Gravitational Potential Energy**: 
\[ U_G = - G \frac{m_e m_p}{r_1} \]
\[ U_G = - \frac{6.67430 \times 10^{-11} \times 1.6726219 \times 10^{-27} \times 9.10938356 \times 10^{-31}}{10^{-10}} \]
\[ U_G = - \frac{1.020997594 \times 10^{-67}}{10^{-10}} \]
\[ U_G = -1.020997594 \times 10^{-57} \, \text{J} \]

state.reference: Tikrit, Iraq (CNN)ISIS is gone, but the fear remains. As Iraqi forces, aided by Shiite militiamen, took control Wednesday of the northern city of Tikrit, they found vehicles laden with explosives and buildings that might be booby-trapped. CNN senior international correspondent Arwa Damon, who was in Tikrit on Tuesday, saw a large mechanical digger packed with explosives that Iraqi forces had to disarm. The troops, she said, were cautious when they entered buildings in case they were wired to explode. Plumes of smoke rose from burning buildings in the background. Near former Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein's presidential palaces compound -- Tikrit is Hussein's birthplace -- the CNN team also saw a destroyed truck with a large machine gun mounted on the back. Iraqi forces said they had fired an RPG at the truck, killing three ISIS fighters. ISIS was ejected from the palaces compound in fierce fighting, they said, adding that there may still be booby traps. Federal police said they dismantled hundreds of IEDs (improvised explosive devices) Wednesday. CNN heard at least 16 explosions, some very loud, which police said were controlled. The potential booby traps were political as well as physical. Officials are concerned about the behavior of the conquerors, particularly the Iranian-backed Shiite militiamen who helped Iraqi troops. Officials fear the militiamen might take "scorched earth" reprisals for the reported massacre of Shiite air force cadets by ISIS fighters in Tikrit last year. Much of the population of Tikrit is, like ISIS, Sunni Muslim. And officials fear that reprisals by Shiite militias against the Sunni population could stoke local anger, jeopardizing the government's ability to hold onto Tikrit and pull the country together. Sectarian resentment helped fuel the rise of ISIS in the first place. 'Where are our sons?' demand families of soldiers captured by ISIS. Still, the liberation of Tikrit from the terrorist group, which is also known as ISIL and calls itself the Islamic State, represented a significant victory for the Iraqi government, which had tried -- and failed -- to retake the city many times before. Iraqi  Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi arrived Wednesday to claim the victory, which took place a year after the city was first attacked by ISIS. Al-Abadi, who is also Iraq's top military commander, had announced the previous evening on Iraqiya TV that the city was under the control of Iraqi forces. Iraqi forces continued to clean out pockets of resistance Wednesday, said Interior Minister Mohammed al-Ghabban, who was also in the city. But he said the Iraqi government would be in full control shortly. "The enemy has been defeated, and it has lost all its capabilities," al-Ghabban said. "In the coming hours, the battle will end." Iraqi security said that the few ISIS militants left in the city are hiding inside houses hoping to escape in the dark. ISIS' nine-month dominion over Tikrit was marked by brutality. In addition to the reported massacre of the 1,500-plus air force cadets at Camp Speicher in June, ISIS is believed to have buried victims in mass graves and to have destroyed an Assyrian church that had graced Tikrit since the eighth century. The push into Tikrit came days after U.S.-led airstrikes targeted ISIS bases around the city. Al-Abadi said those tactics would now be replicated in other areas. Brett McGurk, the U.S. deputy special presidential envoy to the Global Coalition to Counter ISIL, tweeted that the coalition's airstrikes had destroyed numerous ISIS shelters. "We will continue to support courageous Iraqi forces operating under Iraqi command as they work to reclaim their territory from #ISIL," McGurk tweeted. The key to victory in Tikrit this time, the Prime Minister said, was surprise. But help from the coalition of Shiite militiamen and volunteers also played a part. The militia members, estimated to number around 20,000, are backed by Iran. The offensive marked the first open participation of Iranian advisers on the front lines in Iraq. The victory in Tikrit sets the stage for Iraqi forces to take back an even bigger prize -- Mosul, Iraq's second-largest city. A U.S. official said in February that up to 25,000 Iraqi troops plan to return to Mosul in April or May in an effort to retake the city. Don Melvin wrote this report in London. Arwa Damon and Hamdi Alkhshali reported from Tikrit and Jomana Karadsheh from Baghdad.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 190 words:
state.reference: After deliberating for more than 35 hours over parts of seven days, listening intently to the testimony of more than 130 witnesses and reviewing more than 400 pieces of evidence, the teary-eyed men and women of the jury exchanged embraces. Since late January, their work in the Massachusetts murder trial of former NFL star Aaron Hernandez had consumed their lives. It was nothing like "Law & Order." The days were long and tedious. Now it was over. "It's been an incredibly emotional toll on all of us," Lesa Strachan told CNN's Anderson Cooper Thursday in the first nationally televised interview with members of the jury. A day earlier, Strachan, the jury foreperson, announced the first-degree murder conviction in the 2013 shooting death of Hernandez's onetime friend Odin Lloyd. Strachan said she was struck by the viciousness of multiple gunshots. "You shot him once but you kept going and you shot him six times. There's no need for that and there's no need to use a gun. Period." Before the trial, at least one juror -- Rosalie Oliver -- hadn't heard of the 25-year-old defendant who has now gone from a $40 million pro-football contract to a term of life without parole in a maximum-security prison. But Kelly Dorsey watches the Patriots every Sunday during the football season. She said so on her jury questionnaire. "I knew of him as a football player, not a person," she said. It didn't affect her vote to convict, she said. It didn't matter that he was a football player, she said. Nor did it matter whether he actually pulled the trigger in the murder. "To leave your friend on the ground, knowing that he's not there anymore -- he's either dead or he's going to die -- that's indifference," Dorsey said of Hernandez. "He didn't need to pull the trigger." That word -- "indifference" -- was used multiple times by members of the jury. Jon Carlson said he was struck by testimony and video evidence that Hernandez and two co-defendants were sunbathing poolside hours after the slaying, drinking smoothies. Hernandez at times left his then-8-month-old daughter with the two men. That indifference "surprised a lot of us," Carlson said. He stressed the fact that Hernandez played football for a living didn't influence the jury's decision. "It doesn't matter how much money you have or how much money you make. We're all people, and we're all equal, and we all deserve the same fair trial, and that's what we wanted to make sure we gave him," Carlson said. Lloyd was seen June 17, 2013, around 2:30 a.m. with Hernandez and Hernandez's friends, Carlos Ortiz and Ernest Wallace, in a rented silver Nissan Altima. Later that day, a jogger found his body. He had been shot six times, according to prosecutors. Wallace and Ortiz, who were also charged with murder, have pleaded not guilty and will be tried separately. What's next for Aaron Hernandez? Rosalie Oliver -- the juror who hadn't heard of Hernandez before the trial -- said that, for her, the first shot was enough. "There was no need for the other five," she said. "One shot for me is cruelty." Oliver and other jurors said they were surprised to receive calls from friends congratulating them after the verdict. "Who won?" she asked "Odin Lloyd didn't win. (His mother) didn't bring back her son. Did Mr. Hernandez win? No, because he's going to serve the rest of his life in jail and he's 25 years old. The worst part for me is: How about that little girl that's never going to see her father again?" What prison life will be like for Aaron Hernandez. Oliver recalled making eye contact with Hernandez at one point during the months-long trial. "He actually nodded to me one time," she said. "You come in that room every day and you see this person and it's hard to come to that decision at the end because -- like three months with them -- it's almost like they're part of you. And then, all of a sudden now, you've got to make that decision to either put him away or let him go." The jurors declined to talk about the dynamics inside the jury room, choosing instead to keep the focus on the evidence presented during trial. They conveyed a sense of gravity about their task. "You see, you know, 'Law & Order' and all these different TV shows and it's just nothing like that at all. It's just very serious," Carlson said. 5 things to know about the jury.
state.response: After 35 hours of deliberation over a seven-day period, the jury in the Aaron Hernandez murder trial convicted the former NFL star of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of his onetime friend, Odin Lloyd. The jury was composed of 12 men and women, including a woman who had never heard of Hernandez before the trial. The verdict was based on testimony from more than 130 witnesses and evidence from over 400 pieces. The jury foreperson, Lesa Strachan, said she was struck by the viciousness of the multiple gunshots and that there was no need for such violence. Juror Kelly Dorsey, who watched the Patriots every Sunday during the football season, said she wasn't affected by Hernandez's celebrity status and that he played football for a living didn't influence her vote. Rosalie Oliver, another juror, said she was surprised to hear from friends congratulating her after the verdict and that the worst part of the trial was the thought of the little girl who would never see her father again. The jury declined to discuss the dynamics inside the jury room, focusing instead on the evidence presented during the trial.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 91 words:
state.reference:
Unidentified woman from 1988 Georgia cold case identified using Genealogy Technology
In a significant development in a 1988 cold case, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation (GBI) announced they have successfully identified the human remains discovered in a Jenkins County dumpster on February 14, 1988. The victim, according to GBI officials, has been identified as Chong Un Kim, a 26-year-old individual who immigrated to the United States from Korea in 1981 and resided in Hinesville, Liberty County, Georgia.
According to the GBI, investigators were called upon by the Jenkins County Sheriff's Office to assist in a death investigation in 1988. The victim was found wrapped in plastic and duct tape inside a large nylon suitcase, which had been placed in a dumpster just north of Millen, Georgia, according to officials. Tragically, per the GBI, the victim had been deceased for approximately four to seven days, with the cause of death determined to be asphyxiation.
GBI officials stated that throughout the investigation, efforts to identify the victim included the comparison of fingerprints and dental records with missing persons nationwide. Additionally, a forensic artist created a sketch of the victim, which was shared with the public.
National organizations such as the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NAMUS) and the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) joined the efforts, disseminating a computer-generated sketch. Although DNA technology evolved over the years, previous submissions to the GBI Crime Lab failed to provide profiles eligible for entry into the CODIS DNA Database, per an official statement from the GBI.
According to officials, in 2023, the GBI initiated collaboration with Othram, Inc., a Texas-based company specializing in advanced DNA testing to solve cases. Through advanced DNA analysis, a genealogical search generated investigative leads, eventually leading to the identification of Chong Un Kim. The GBI stated they notified Kim's family about the breakthrough in October 2023, marking a significant development in the case.
Notably, per GBI officials, the DNA testing was funded by "Project Justice."
The GBI is now appealing to anyone who may have known Chong Un Kim or possesses information related to the case to contact them at 912-871-1121. Anonymous tips can be submitted via phone, online at https://gbi.georgia.gov/submit-tips-online, or through the See Something, Send Something mobile app.
state.response: In 1988, a woman's body was found in a dumpster in Georgia. Despite efforts to identify her, she remained a Jane Doe for decades. Recently, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation used advanced DNA testing and genealogy technology to identify her as Chong Un Kim, a 26-year-old Korean immigrant. The case is now being reopened, and the GBI is asking for anyone with information to come forward.
