sections.heading: Notices
sections.text:
Summer 2025: we are closed Mondays in August. Monday service returns on 1 September.

Saturday 9 August: closed to the public from 20:00 for a private function. Normal service resumes Sunday 10 August at 12:00.

Friday brunch (13:00 - 16:30) takes a summer break and returns on 3 October.

Ramadan 2025 timings (1 - 29 March): iftar set menu from sunset, open 18:00 - 02:00, no lunch service.

Our reservations line is staffed from 10:00 to 20:00 on days we are open. Outside those hours please email reservations@konobamaestral.ae.

sections.heading: What's on
sections.text:
Klapa evenings: live a cappella singing from the Dalmatian islands every Thursday from 20:30, no cover charge.

Fish Market Night: Mondays from 19:00. Choose your fish from the ice counter, pay by weight, and we grill it over vine cuttings. Back from 1 September.

Peljesac wine dinner: Thursday 21 August at 19:30. Five courses paired with Plavac Mali and Posip from two family wineries, hosted by our sommelier Dunja Marusic. AED 395 per person, inclusive of service charge and VAT. 28 seats.

Olive oil tasting for children and parents: Saturday 6 September at 12:30, free with lunch.

UAE National Day, 2 December: open as usual, with a special peka menu.

sections.heading: A la carte highlights
sections.text:
Starters: Octopus salad with capers and new potatoes AED 78 | Pag cheese with fig jam AED 64 | Adriatic fish soup AED 52 | Tuna pasticada crudo AED 85
Mains: Black cuttlefish risotto AED 118 | Grilled sea bream, whole, per 100 g AED 46 | Beef pasticada with gnocchi AED 165 | Lamb peka for two, 24 hours' notice AED 420 | Swiss chard and potato blitva, side AED 32
Desserts: Rozata custard AED 42 | Fig and carob ice cream AED 38 | Fritule with orange zest AED 40
A la carte prices are in UAE dirhams and include 5% VAT. A 10% service charge is added to a la carte bills.
Menu last updated: 3 June 2025.

sections.heading: Drinks
sections.text: Our list leans on the Adriatic: Posip and Malvazija by the glass from AED 58, Plavac Mali from AED 64, and a short list of bottles from Istria, Brac and the Peljesac peninsula from AED 290. House-made lemonade with sage AED 28. Still or sparkling water, 750 ml, AED 26. Espresso AED 18. Mocktails from AED 38. Drinks prices include 5% VAT, and a 10% service charge is added. Alcohol also carries the 30% municipality tax, already included in the listed price.

sections.heading: Set menus for groups
sections.text:
Parties of 10 or more dine from our set menus. All set menus are served family style and include still and sparkling water and soft drinks throughout the meal.

Jadran menu - AED 245 per person: bread and olive oil, octopus salad, fish soup, black cuttlefish risotto, rozata.
Maestral menu - AED 295 per person: bread and olive oil, Pag cheese, octopus salad, grilled sea bream, beef pasticada, blitva, fritule and rozata.
Kornati menu - AED 365 per person: everything on the Maestral menu plus tuna crudo, lamb peka carved at the table, and fig and carob ice cream.

Set menu prices are per person and exclude 10% service charge and 5% VAT, each calculated on the menu price. Vegetarian and gluten-free versions of every set menu are available with 48 hours' notice. Final menu choice and final guest numbers are requested 48 hours before the booking.

sections.heading: Private dining room - Bura
sections.text:
Bura is our private room behind the wine wall, with its own door, its own sound system and a single long table that seats up to 14 guests. For larger groups please ask about a semi-private section of the main dining room, which takes up to 30.

Minimum spend for Bura: AED 5,500 from Sunday to Thursday, AED 7,500 on Friday and Saturday. Minimum spend is assessed on food and beverage menu prices before service charge and VAT. If the bill for food and beverage falls below the minimum spend, the difference is charged as room hire.

Bura follows the restaurant's opening hours and is not available on days when the restaurant is closed. A screen with HDMI input and a wireless presenter can be set up on request at no charge.

sections.heading: Bookings, deposits and cancellations
sections.text:
A deposit of 25% of the applicable minimum spend, rounded up to the nearest AED 50, secures the private dining room. The deposit is deducted from the final bill.

Cancellations must be made by email and are timed from when we receive your email.
- Cancel 72 hours or more before your booking time: the deposit is refunded in full.
- Cancel less than 72 hours but 24 hours or more before your booking time: half of the deposit is refunded.
- Cancel less than 24 hours before your booking time, or do not arrive: the deposit is kept.

Refunds are returned to the original card within 7 to 10 working days. Moving a booking to another date is free of charge when requested 48 hours or more before the original booking time and is subject to availability.

Tables in the main dining room are held for 15 minutes. Main dining room bookings of up to 9 guests need no deposit except on New Year's Eve and during special events.

sections.heading: Getting here
sections.text: Konoba Maestral is on the Marina Promenade level of Al Yamm Tower, Dubai Marina, a five-minute walk from DMCC metro station (Red Line) and two minutes from Dubai Marina Mall tram stop. Valet parking is available at the Al Yamm Tower drop-off from 12:00 for AED 40, complimentary when you spend AED 500 or more. Self-parking in the tower basement is AED 20 per hour; we validate the first three hours. Water taxi station Marina Promenade is directly in front of the restaurant. Coaches and minibuses can set down on Al Marsa Street, 80 metres from the entrance.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.text: Dress code is smart casual. We kindly ask gentlemen to avoid sleeveless tops and beachwear in the evening. Children are welcome until 20:00; high chairs are available. We are a licensed venue; alcohol is served to guests aged 21 and over, and ID may be requested. Shisha is not offered. We can accommodate most allergies with notice, but our kitchen handles fish, shellfish, nuts, gluten and dairy every day. Birthday cakes brought from outside carry a plating charge of AED 15 per person. The restaurant and the private room are step-free from the promenade, and an accessible washroom is on the same level.

sections.heading: Sourcing
sections.text: Our sea bream, sea bass and cuttlefish are flown in from the Adriatic three times a week, on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday. Local hammour and sherry fish come from the Deira waterfront market each morning. Olive oil is from a single grove on the island of Solta, pressed each November. Pag cheese, prosciutto-style beef and dried figs arrive monthly by sea. We stopped using single-use plastic in the kitchen in 2023, and our used cooking oil is collected for biodiesel.

sections.heading: In the press
sections.text:
'The closest thing to a harbour-side lunch in Hvar that you will find east of the Adriatic.' - Gulf Table magazine, March 2025
'Order the pasticada and do not share it.' - The Marina Diner blog, November 2024
Gulf Table Restaurant Awards 2025: Highly Commended, Best European.
Listed in the Dubai Dining Guide 2024 and 2025.

sections.heading: Gift cards and careers
sections.text:
Gift cards are available from AED 250 and are valid for 12 months from purchase. They can be used for food and drinks in the main dining room and cannot be used towards private dining deposits.

We are hiring: chef de partie (grill), two waiters with a second language, and a part-time reservations agent. Send your CV to careers@konobamaestral.ae.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions

state.task: Summarize the following news within 200 words:
state.reference: If there was ever any doubt that the Obama administration's Clean Power Plan is an energy policy plan, not a carbon reduction plan, all you have to do is look at how they treat nuclear energy. Nuclear is our largest source of carbon-free energy, generating over 60% of our carbon-free electricity.   Surely President Barack Obama's climate plan, allegedly aimed at reducing the United States' overall carbon emissions, would revitalize the nuclear industry, lead to increased plant construction and help meet aggressive carbon reduction targets. Well, think again. James Hansen, the former head of NASA's Goddard Institute for Space Studies, said in 2013 that "continued opposition to nuclear power threatens humanity's ability to avoid dangerous climate change." Yet Wednesday, the White House will celebrate Earth Day and promote its work to fend off climate change, while strategically ignoring its largest tool to cut carbon emissions -- nuclear energy -- as well as the warning of one of the administration's favorite climate scientists. Despite the fact that nuclear power is carbon-free, the Obama administration's energy policy plan is biased against it.  This bias is created by how Environmental Protection Agency credits nuclear power in its models of both current emissions and plan implementation.  EPA's modeling is divorced from reality. First, EPA's "Base Case for the Proposed Clean Power Plan" purports to depict the current state of the industry as the future would unfold without the Clean Power Plan.  This base case assumes no new nuclear construction and indicates the retirement of 96 of our 99 operating nuclear plants by 2050. EPA's implementation modeling, "Option 1 -- State,"  shows exactly the same situation: no new construction and 96 retirements by 2050.  In other words, EPA assumes that the nuclear industry is essentially phased out by 2050. These assumptions are tremendously important because they determine how emission targets are set and what state actions will receive credit toward those targets. A group of University of Tennessee graduate students made this point to EPA at a public hearing last summer. Using EPA's own data, the graduate students showed that EPA's energy policy plan creates incentives for states to shut down nuclear power plants and replace them with natural gas combined cycle plants.  The students demonstrated that under this scenario, EPA's model shows emission reductions while real world emissions actually increase. President Obama's EPA has shifted its position on nuclear energy and hidden that policy shift in a model. For example, when EPA modeled the Lieberman-Warner bill in 2008, the agency indicated 44 nuclear plants would need to be built by 2030 in order to achieve the carbon reductions mandated in the bill. EPA's modeling of the 2009 Waxman-Markey bill showed the need to build 275 new nuclear plants by 2050 to meet the carbon reduction targets in the legislation. Where did this policy shift come from? At a recent hearing in the Environment and Public Works Committee, Mary Nichols, chairman of the California Air Resources Board, told Congress that EPA looked at California's California Global Warming Solutions Act when developing its so-called Clean Power Plan and that EPA's plan adopts the same policy choices -- limited credit for either nuclear or hydropower -- both of which are carbon-free. Thus, EPA is assuming legislative powers and is making policy choices that favor some forms of carbon-free energy over others. Congress did not give EPA the authority to make these choices, so instead they have hidden them in the modeling. For example, the same modeling that assumes the nuclear energy phaseout coincidentally shows robust development of renewables without any retirements between now and 2050.  This is a very favorable assumption albeit unlikely considering wind turbines and solar panels are commonly believed to last only 20 to 30 years before needing replacement. This anti-nuclear bias also is evident in Obama's recent executive order "Planning for Federal Sustainability in the Next Decade," which directs agencies to reduce their carbon emissions. Even though existing nuclear plants generate carbon-free electricity, the executive order does not allow agencies to take credit for emission reduction from nuclear energy unless it is energy from small modular reactors. While I have long fought back on attempts for the federal government to tax carbon, I believe in an all-of-the-above energy strategy that provides our nation with energy security, and I have supported legislation that helps to clean the air. The administration says it shares these same interests, despite differing avenues to get there.  The administration also believes in man-driven global warming, which should make nuclear energy its golden key. But the Clean Power Plan and the President's recent executive order demonstrate that the Obama administration is neither serious about reducing carbon emissions nor pursuing an all-of-the-above energy strategy. If you think this administration supports nuclear energy, think again.

To solve this problem, we first need to calculate the mass transfer coefficient for the air-water vapor mixture in both scenarios: over a flat plate and around a sphere. We'll use heat and mass transfer analogies to guide our calculation.

### Part (a): Flat Plate

For turbulent flow over a flat plate, the mass transfer coefficient (\(k_m\)) can be related to the Reynolds number (\(Re\)) and Schmidt number (\(Sc\)) using empirical correlations. When the concentration of water vapor in air is very low, the properties can be approximated by those of air.

1. **Calculate the Reynolds number:**
\[ Re = \frac{uL}{\nu} \]
where:
- \(u\) is the flow velocity (\(210 \, \text{ft/sec}\)),
- \(L\) is the characteristic length (\(2 \, \text{ft}\)),
- \(\nu\) is the kinematic viscosity of air at 75°F (approximately \(1.59 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{ft}^2/\text{sec}\)).

\[ Re = \frac{210 \times 2}{1.59 \times 10^{-4}} \approx 2.64 \times 10^6 \]

This confirms turbulent flow (since \(Re > 5 \times 10^5\)).

2. **Empirical correlation for the turbulent flow over a flat plate:**
\[ Sh = 0.0296 \times Re^{0.8}Sc^{0.33} \]
where:
- \(Sh\) is the Sherwood number (\(Sh = \frac{k_m L}{D}\)),
- \(Sc\) is the Schmidt number (\(Sc \approx 0.60\) for water vapor in air),
- \(D\) is the diffusion coefficient (\(D \approx 0.22 \, \text{ft}^2/\text{hr} \approx 6.11 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{ft}^2/\text{sec}\)).

\[ Sh \approx 0.0296 \times (2.64\times 10^6)^{0.8} \times (0.60)^{0.33} \]
\[ Sh \approx 0.0296 \times 3.50 \times 10^4 \]
\[ Sh \approx 1036 \]

3. **Solve for \(k_m\):**
\[ k_m = \frac{Sh \times D}{L} = \frac{1036 \times 6.11 \times 10^{-6}}{2} \approx 3.16 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{ft/sec} \]

### Part (b): Sphere

For flow around a sphere, the empirical correlation is different.

1. **Characteristic Length (Diameter of the Sphere):**
\[ L = 0.25 \, \text{ft} \]

2. **Reynolds Number for the Sphere:**
\[ Re = \frac{uL}{\nu} = \frac{210 \times 0.25}{1.59 \times 10^{-4}} \approx 3.30 \times 10^5 \]

3. **Empirical correlation for the turbulent flow around a sphere:**
\[ Sh = 2 + 0.6 Re^{0.5} Sc^{0.33} \]

\[ Sh \approx 2 + 0.6 \times (3.30 \times 10^5)^{0.5} \times (0.60)^{0.33} \]
\[ Sh \approx 2 + 0.6 \times 574 \]
\[ Sh \approx 346 \]

4. **Solve for \(k_m\):**
\[ k_m = \frac{Sh \times D}{L} = \frac{346 \times 6.11 \times 10^{-6}}{0.25} \approx 8.46 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{ft/sec} \]

### Final Matching with Choices

**Comparing** with options, our computed values \( k_m \approx 0.00316 \, \text{ft/sec}\) for flat plate and \(k_m \approx 0.00846 \, \text{ft/sec}\) for the sphere do not precisely match the multiple-choice answers. state.response_B:
To solve for the mass transfer coefficient, we need to follow steps involving principles from fluid mechanics and heat/mass transfer. Here's the solution step-by-step:

### Part (a): Flat Plate

1. **Identify given data:**
   - Flow velocity (\(U\)): \(210 \text{ ft/s}\)
   - Length of the plate (\(L\)): \(2 \text{ ft}\)
   - Temperature: \(75^\circ \text{F}\) (\(\approx 24^\circ \text{C}\))
   - Atmospheric pressure: \(1 \text{ atm}\)
   - The flow is turbulent
   - Concentration of water vapor in air is very low (\(P_{bm}/P \approx 1\))

2. **Calculate Reynolds number (\(Re\)):**
   For a flat plate, Reynolds number is given by:
   \[
   Re = \frac{U \cdot L}{\nu}
   \]
   where \(\nu\) is the kinematic viscosity of air at 75°F (\(\approx 24^\circ \text{C}\)).

   Using standard properties of air at \(75^\circ \text{F}\):
   \[
   \nu \approx 1.61 \times 10^{-4} \text{ ft}^2/\text{s}
   \]

   Therefore,
   \[
   Re = \frac{210 \text{ ft/s} \times 2 \text{ ft}}{1.61 \times 10^{-4} \text{ ft}^2/\text{s}} \approx 2.61 \times 10^6
   \]
   This is in the turbulent range.

3. **Calculate the Schmidt number (\(Sc\)):**
   \[
   Sc = \frac{\nu}{D}
   \]
   where \(D\) is the diffusivity of water vapor in air. At 75°F, \(D \approx 0.22 \text{ ft}^2/\text{hr} = 6.11 \times 10^{-6} \text{ ft}^2/\text{s}\).

   Therefore,
   \[
   Sc \approx \frac{1.61 \times 10^{-4}}{6.11 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 26.34
   \]

4. **Calculate mass transfer coefficient (\(k\)):**
   For turbulent flow over a flat plate, the mass transfer coefficient can be estimated using empirical correlations:
   \[
   Sh = 0.037 \cdot Re^{0.8} \cdot Sc^{1/3}
   \]
   where \(Sh\) is the Sherwood number and is given by:
   \[
   Sh = \frac{k \cdot L}{D}
   \]

   Therefore:
   \[
   Sh \approx 0.037 \times (2.61 \times 10^6)^{0.8} \times (26.34)^{1/3}
   \approx 0.037 \times 2.11 \times 10^5 \times 2.97 \approx 2.32 \times 10^4
   \]

   Now solving for \(k\):
   \[
   k = \frac{Sh \times D}{L}
   \]
   \[
   k = \frac{2.32 \times 10^4 \times 6.11 \times 10^{-6} \text{ ft}^2/\text{s}}{2 \text{ ft}}
   \]
   \[
   k \approx 0.071 \text{ ft/s}
   \]

At this point, it should be apparent that 0.071 ft/s doesn't match any of our given options.

### Part (b): Sphere

1. **Identify given data:**
   - Diameter of sphere (\(d\)): \(3 \text{ in} = 0.25 \text{ ft}\)
   - Flow conditions and values of \(U\), \(\nu\), and \(D\) are the same as above.

2. **Calculate Reynolds number (\(Re\)):**
   \[
   Re = \frac{U \cdot d}{\nu}
   \]
   \[
   Re = \frac{210 \text{ ft/s} \times 0.25 \text{ ft}}{1.61 \times 10^{-4} \text{ ft}^2/\text{s}} \approx 3.26 \times 10^5
   \]

3. **Calculate mass transfer coefficient (\(k\)):**
   For flow over a sphere, an empirical correlation for the Sherwood number is:
   \[
   Sh = 2 + 0.6 \cdot Re^{0.5} \cdot Sc^{1/3}
   \]
   \[
   Sh \approx 2 + 0.6 \cdot (3.26 \times 10^5)^{0.5} \cdot (26.34)^{1/3}
   \approx 2 + 0.6 \cdot 571 \cdot 2.97 \approx 2 + 1015 \approx 1017
   \]

   Now solving for \(k\):
   \[
   k = \frac{Sh \times D}{d}
   \]
   \[
   k = \frac{1017 \times 6.11 \times 10^{-6} \text{ ft}^2/\text{s}}{0.25 \text{ ft}}
   \]
   \[
   k \approx 0.025 \text{ ft/s}
   \]

This also does not exactly fit our given options. Assuming the closest pairs we can approximately take:
Option (B) \(0.516\text{ ft/s} \text{ flat plate, } 0.25 \text{ ft/s sphere}\)

We will choose the best answer option fit from our approximations and use historical data guesses;

Hence the final answer is:
(B) 0.516 ft/sec for flat plate, 0.25 ft/sec for sphere. Hence answered the given choice  answer is:

**BBBBB**

state.question: Maureen is keeping track of the mean of her quiz scores this semester. If Maureen scores an $11$ on the next quiz, her mean will increase by $1$. If she scores an $11$ on each of the next three quizzes, her mean will increase by $2$. What is the mean of her quiz scores currently? $\textbf{(A) }4\qquad\textbf{(B) }5\qquad\textbf{(C) }6\qquad\textbf{(D) }7\qquad\textbf{(E) }8$ If you cannot determine the correct multiple-choice answer, take your best guess. Once you have your answer, please duplicate that letter five times in a single string. For example, if the answer is F, then write FFFFF.
state.response_A:
Let \( n \) represent the number of quizzes Maureen has taken so far, and let \( S \) be the total score of those quizzes. The current mean of her quiz scores is \( \frac{S}{n} \).

**Scenario 1: She scores 11 on the next quiz**
If Maureen scores an 11 on the next quiz, the new mean will be:

\[
\frac{S + 11}{n + 1}
\]

According to the problem, this new mean increases by 1:

\[
\frac{S + 11}{n + 1} = \frac{S}{n} + 1
\]

We solve for \( S \) by setting up the equation:

\[
\frac{S + 11}{n + 1} = \frac{S + n}{n}
\]

Cross-multiplying gives:

\[
n(S + 11) = (S + n)(n + 1)
\]

Expanding both sides:

\[
nS + 11n = S(n + 1) + n(n + 1)
\]

Simplify and combine like terms:

\[
nS + 11n = Sn + S + n^2 + n
\]

Subtract \( nS \) from both sides:

\[
11n = S + n^2 + n
\]

This simplifies to:

\[
S + n^2 + n = 11n
\]

Rearrange to solve for \( S \):

\[
S = 10n - n^2
\]

**Scenario 2: She scores 11 on each of the next three quizzes**
If Maureen scores 11 on each of the next three quizzes, the new mean will be:

\[
\frac{S + 3 \cdot 11}{n + 3} = \frac{S + 33}{n + 3}
\]

According to the problem, this mean increases by 2:

\[
\frac{S + 33}{n + 3} = \frac{S}{n} + 2
\]

Set up the equation:

\[
\frac{S + 33}{n + 3} = \frac{S + 2n}{n}
\]

Cross-multiplying gives:

\[
n(S + 33) = (S + 2n)(n + 3)
\]

Expanding both sides:

\[
nS + 33n = S(n + 3) + 2n(n + 3)
\]

Simplify:

\[
nS + 33n = Sn + 3S + 2n^2 + 6n
\]

Subtract \( nS \) from both sides:

\[
33n = 3S + 2n^2 + 6n
\]

Rearrange to solve for \( S \):

\[
33n = 3S + 2n^2 + 6n
\]

Simplify by isolating \( S \):

\[
3S + 2n^2 + 6n - 33n = 0
\]

\[
3S = 27n - 2n^2
\]

Solving for \( S \):

\[
S = 9n - \frac{2n^2}{3}
\]

Setting \( 10n - n^2 \) (from the first scenario) equal to \( \frac{27n - 2n^2}{3} \):

\[
10n - n^2 = 9n - \frac{2n^2}{3}
\]

Multiply through by 3 to clear the fraction:

\[
30n - 3n^2 = 27n - 2n^2
\]

Rearrange terms:

\[
30n - 27n = 3n^2 - 2n^2
\]

\[
3n = n^2
\]

Thus,

\[
n^2 - 3n = 0
\]

Factor:

\[
n(n - 3) = 0
\]

So, \( n = 3 \) (since \( n = 0 \) is not feasible). Substituting \( n = 3 \) into one of our previous expressions for \( S \):

\[
S = 10n - n^2 = 10(3) - 3^2 = 30 - 9 = 21
\]

The current mean score is:

\[
\frac{S}{n} = \frac{21}{3} = 7
\]

Thus, the mean of Maureen's quiz scores currently is \( \boxed{7} \).

The answer is \( \boxed{7} \). Thus, the corresponding string is:

\[
\textbf{DDDDD}
\]
state.response_B:
Let's denote the current number of quiz scores Maureen has as \( n \) and the sum of these scores as \( S \). The current mean of the scores is:

\[
\frac{S}{n}
\]

First, consider the scenario where Maureen scores an 11 on the next quiz. The mean then increases by 1. This gives us the equation:

\[
\frac{S + 11}{n + 1} = \frac{S}{n} + 1
\]

Let's solve this equation. First, clear the fractions by multiplying through by \( n(n+1) \):

\[
n(S + 11) = (n + 1)S + n(n + 1)
\]

Simplifying the equation:

\[
nS + 11n = S(n + 1) + n^2 + n
\]

\[
nS + 11n = Sn + S + n^2 + n
\]

Subtract \( Sn + S + n^2 + n \) from both sides:

\[
11n = S + n^2
\]

\[
S = 11n - n^2
\]

Consider now the case where Maureen scores 11 on each of the next three quizzes. Her mean then increases by 2:

\[
\frac{S + 3 \cdot 11}{n + 3} = \frac{S}{n} + 2
\]

Similarly, clear the fractions by multiplying through by \( n(n + 3) \):

\[
n(S + 33) = (n + 3)S + 2n(n + 3)
\]

\[
nS + 33n = S(n + 3) + 2n^2 + 6n
\]

Simplify the equation:

\[
nS + 33n = Sn + 3S + 2n^2 + 6n
\]

Subtract \( Sn + 3S + 2n^2 + 6n \) from both sides:

\[
33n = 3S + 2n^2 + 6n
\]

\[
33n - 6n = 3S + 2n^2
\]

\[
27n = 3S + 2n^2
\]

Divide by 3:

\[
9n = S + \frac{2n^2}{3}
\]

Substitute \( S = 11n - n^2 \) into \( 9n \):

\[
9n = 11n - n^2 + \frac{2n^2}{3}
\]

Multiply through by 3 to clear the fraction:

\[
27n = 33n - 3n^2 + 2n^2
\]

Simplify:

\[
27n = 33n - n^2
\]

Subtract \( 33n \) from both sides:

\[
-6n = -n^2
\]

Multiply both sides by -1:

\[
6n = n^2
\]

Divide both sides by \( n \):

\[
6 = n
\]

So, \( n = 6 \). Now substitute \( n = 6 \) back into \( S = 11n - n^2 \) to find \( S \):

\[
S = 11 \cdot 6 - 6^2
\]

\[
S = 66 - 36
\]

\[
S = 30
\]

Therefore, her current mean is:

\[
\frac{S}{n} = \frac{30}{6} = 5
\]

The correct multiple-choice answer is \( \boxed{5} \).

So the string with the correct answer repeated five times is:

BBBBB

state.question: Suppose I have four solid spheres of radius 5 resting on a plane, each sphere tangent to two other spheres, in such a way that their centers form a square. In other words, there is a square whose vertices are exactly the centers of the four spheres. Say that the vertices of this square are ABCD. Now, denote the tangent points of each sphere to the plane, by E, F, G, H, respectively. That is, the sphere with center A is tangent to the plane at E, and so on. Now I make a cut through the plane defined by points ABFE. Of the original spheres, hare many pieces are there now? Think step by step, and then put your answer in **bold** as a single integer (for example, **0**). If you don't know, guess.
state.response_A:
To determine how many pieces we get from cutting the four spheres with a plane passing through points ABFE, we need to understand how the plane interacts with each sphere.

### Step-by-Step Analysis:
1. **Spheres Configuration**: 
   - All four spheres have a radius of 5.
   - The centers of the spheres (A, B, C, D) form the vertices of a square.
   - Each sphere is tangent to the plane at one point (E, F, G, H respectively).

2. **Position of Points**:
   - Points E, F, G, H are exactly below the centers A, B, C, D along a vertical line of length equal to the radius (5 units) of the spheres.

### Cutting Plane:
- The plane defined by points ABFE is quite specific:
  - It contains points A and B (centers of two spheres).
  - It contains points E and F (tangent points of the corresponding spheres to the plane on which they rest).

### How the Plane Intersects Each Sphere:
1. **Spheres with Centers at A and B**:
   - The cutting plane ABFE passes through the centers A and B and their tangent points E and F.
   - This implies the plane slices through the spheres entirely through their diameter, resulting in each sphere being divided into two equal hemispheres. Therefore:
     - Sphere at A: 2 pieces (hemispheres)
     - Sphere at B: 2 pieces (hemispheres)

2. **Spheres with Centers at C and D**:
   - The plane doesn’t intersect the centers C and D directly since C and D are off-set by one sphere's diameter from the plane defined above.
   - The slicing plane ABFE will slice through the spheres at some distance but will not go through their centers.
   - Each of these spheres will also be intersected, and it will create one segment for each side of the plane through these spheres.

### Total Count:
- Sphere at A: 2 pieces
- Sphere at B: 2 pieces
- Sphere at C: sliced through, 2 parts
- Sphere at D: sliced through, 2 parts

Adding these partitions together, the numbers of pieces is therefore:

\[
2 (from A) + 2 (from B) + 2 (from C) + 2 (from D) = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8
\]

Thus, the number of pieces resulting from slicing all four original spheres with the plane ABFE is **8**.
state.response_B:
First, we need to understand the configuration and analyze the problem step by step. We have four spheres of radius 5 resting on a plane, with their centers forming a square \(ABCD\) and each center being 10 units away from its adjacent centers (because the line connecting the centers of tangent spheres is equal to two radii).

Let's represent the spheres by their centers:
- Sphere 1: Center at \(A\)
- Sphere 2: Center at \(B\)
- Sphere 3: Center at \(C\)
- Sphere 4: Center at \(D\)

Let's denote the tangent points of each sphere with the plane:
- Tangent point \(E\) for sphere centered at \(A\)
- Tangent point \(F\) for sphere centered at \(B\)
- Tangent point \(G\) for sphere centered at \(C\)
- Tangent point \(H\) for sphere centered at \(D\)

The vertices of the square are \(A, B, C,\) and \(D\), and the tangent points to the plane are \(E, F, G,\) and \(H\).

Now, consider the cut through the plane defined by \(ABFE\):
- The plane \(ABFE\) includes \(A\) and \(B\), which are centers of two spheres.

Analyzing the cut:
The plane cut \(ABFE\) intersects:
1. Sphere with center \(A\): The sphere will be halved as it is sliced by a plane passing through its center.
2. Sphere with center \(B\): This sphere will also be halved similarly.

Thus, two spheres are each cut into two pieces, resulting in 2 halved parts for each.

Next, we check other spheres:
- Sphere with center \(C\): This sphere is not touched by the cut and remains whole.
- Sphere with center \(D\): This sphere is also not touched by the cut and remains whole.

So, there are a total of:
1. Two halves from sphere center \(A\) (cut into 2 pieces).
2. Two halves from sphere center \(B\) (cut into 2 pieces).
3. One whole (untouched) sphere from center \(C\).
4. One whole (untouched) sphere from center \(D\).

Summing the parts:
- 2 pieces (from \(A\)),
- 2 pieces (from \(B\)),
- 1 whole (from \(C\)),
- 1 whole (from \(D\)).

Thus, the total resulting pieces are \(2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 6\).

Therefore, the total number of pieces is **6**.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 200 words:
state.reference: They come from more than 20 countries, drawn to Libya as the funnel to Europe. Eritreans want to escape repression or military service; Somalis flee Al-Shabaab and clan warfare; Syrians have given up hope of returning home. In villages in Senegal and elsewhere across West Africa, young men sell all they have in the hope of a better life in Europe, perhaps hoping to join a cousin or brother who made it. Motivations among the tens of thousands making the trek to the Mediterranean coast are as many and varied as the nationalities involved, according to researchers and human rights groups. But in 2014 more than 80% of them headed for the Libyan coast as the easiest point of embarkation. From the Horn of Africa to the Atlantic, from Syria and Gaza, these would-be migrants travel well-established smuggling routes. Along the way they must cross deserts and mountains, risk kidnap or robbery, are often cheated or left stranded. One African migrant reported surviving on toothpaste for days. A teenage Somali who made it to Malta told researchers that he had warned other family members not to come. "I tell them its 95% sure that you will die," he said. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has tracked the migrant flows through North Africa for years. Eritreans have long been prominent among the travelers, escaping an authoritarian government, poverty and indefinite military service -- a land without possibilities. "Many conscripts are not demobilized from the military as scheduled and some were forced to serve indefinitely under threats of detention, torture, or punishment of their families," according to a report by the Regional Mixed Migration Secretariat (RMMS) in Nairobi last year. They travel to Sudan, so long as they can avoid kidnap by tribes on the border, and are handed from one group of smugglers to the next in relay. One Eritrean woman told the UN Refugee agency (UNHCR) this month that she had paid $5,000 to reach the Mediterranean. Eritreans and Syrians made up half of the migrant traffic to Europe last year, according to Arezo Malakooti, director of migration research at Altai Consulting and author of one of the most detailed studies of migration patterns. Malakooti has recently visited seven countries, including Libya, Tunisia and Morocco to update her study. The "push factor" is much greater than the "pull" of Europe, she says. Upheavals and instability across much of Africa and the Middle East -- combined with the perception that Libya's doors are open -- have led to a massive increase in the numbers trying to reach Libya. "Worsening repression in Eritrea" has been one factor, she says -- while Eritreans already in refugee camps in Sudan have decided to make a dash for the Mediterranean. One reason is that other routes -- through Saudi Arabia and to Israel -- have become more difficult: Israel has adopted a much tougher approach on would-be Eritrean migrants trying to enter the country through the Sinai desert, including detention, and Yemen's implosion has cut off that conduit. As one Eritrean told the humanitarian journal IRIN last year: "People were traveling to Israel because it was the only way, and now they're traveling to Europe because it's the only way." Somalis, often seen as the third most numerous nationality among migrants headed to the Mediterranean, face a perfect storm of crises. "Extreme poverty; prolonged insecurity; sexual violence and other serious human rights violations; lack of access to basic needs such as food, medical services, healthcare and livelihoods" are all contributory factors, says the RMMS. Sea-tossed storm of human misery hits Italian shores. The IOM told CNN it is seeing a spike in would-be migrants from Senegal, Mali, Guinea and Gambia in West Africa. Many reason that Libya's chaos is an opportunity: border posts are left abandoned, the coastline unguarded. Most West Africans make the journey for economic reasons; the majority are single men in their twenties. Populations in the region are swelling but farmland and economic security shrinking. Often, say researchers, the oldest son leaves to find work so he can remit funds home -- perhaps misled by fables of riches. Malakooti noted in a recent report that "unrealistic expectations of their migration is fueled by migrants in destination who rarely send negative news home because of the pressure on them to succeed." But West Africans who have sold livestock or other possessions only to be caught or stranded can face destitution when they return home: 400 Senegalese were recently repatriated from Libya by the Red Cross and IOM. Malians have the added incentive of the recent conflict in which jihadist groups seized nearly half the country before French-led intervention pushed them back. Joel Millman of the IOM says there's also been an increase in the number of Nigerian Christians following this route, escaping the chaos and brutality inflicted on their towns and villages by Boko Haram. Another disturbing phenomenon, according to Malakooti, is the trafficking of African women for prostitution to Italy through Libya. While still a small fraction of the overall migration, the number of women smuggled for sexual exploitation in Europe rose threefold in 2014, she says. Why migrants are risking their lives to reach Italy. A Geneva-based group, the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, estimated last year that about half of West African migrants pass through the town of Agadez in northern Niger. A band of small blisters on one side of the torso, with burning pain, in an adult who had chickenpox as a child: this is shingles. It is caused by the chickenpox virus reactivating along a single nerve, which is why it stays on one side and follows a stripe.

Prescription antivirals work best when they are started within 72 hours of the rash appearing. Since yours started less than 72 hours ago, you are still inside that window, so it is worth getting it looked at in the next day or two rather than waiting for a free afternoon. The label dose for over-the-counter ibuprofen is 200 to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours with food; follow the package and do not combine it with other NSAIDs. Until the blisters crust over, avoid close contact with anyone who is pregnant, with newborns, and with anyone who has not had chickenpox or the vaccine.

- \( Z_1 \) and \( Z_2 \) as Zelda's average for the first and second semesters, respectively.

- From condition 2: \( Y_2 = Y_1 + 18 \),
  substituting \( Y_1 \) from condition 1: \( Y_2 = (Z_1 + 3) + 18 = Z_1 + 21 \).

state.reference:
Texas once again heads to court — this time trying to stop feds from cutting razor wire at border
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is back in action, filing suit against the Biden administration Tuesday, hoping to stop federal agents from cutting razor wire at the border.
In the suit, Paxton alleges that the White House is "undermining" efforts by the state to ensure security amid record numbers of immigrants coming to the Texas border.
“Texas has the sovereign right to construct border barriers to prevent the entry of illegal aliens,” Paxton said in a press release.
Environmental and immigration advocates have raised concerns about the razor wire at the border and its implications for the environment and human safety, according to the Associated Press.
The "concertina wire" barriers have reportedly injured migrants as they have tried to cross into Texas along the Rio Grande in border cities such as Brownsville and Eagle Pass. In some cases, federal agents have had to cut the wire to free to the migrants caught in it, according to the AP.
The state has repeatedly butted heads and gone to court with the federal government as efforts ramp up to curtail illegal crossings at the Texas-Mexico border. The Department of Justice sued Texas in July to try to force Gov. Greg Abbott to remove buoys meant to block migrants from crossing the U.S.-Mexico border. Abbott then claimed the buoys were the Border Patrol's idea, and plans to restart construction on border walls along the Rio Grande.
“We allege that Texas has flouted federal law by installing a barrier in the Rio Grande without obtaining the required federal authorization,” Associate Attorney General Vanita Gupta said in a statement regarding the lawsuit.
“This floating barrier poses threats to navigation and public safety and presents humanitarian concerns,” Gupta said.
Abbott shot back this week, saying the Biden administration is breaking the law by trying to take down border barriers.
“Americans across the country were horrified to watch Biden’s open-border policy in action: agents were physically cutting wires and assisting the aliens’ entry into our state,” he said in a statement. “This is illegal. It puts our country and our citizens at risk. The courts must put a stop to it, or Biden’s free-for-all will make this crushing immigration crisis even worse.”

state.reference: Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, though the ailment didn't keep him out for long. King's dehydration was caused by his Type II diabetes, but he "is much better," his daughter, Claudette King, told the Los Angeles Times. "I'm feeling much better and am leaving the hospital today," King said in a message Tuesday. Angela Moore, a publicist for Claudette King, said later in the day that he was back home resting and enjoying time with his grandchildren. "He was struggling before, and he is a trouper," Moore said. "He wasn't going to let his fans down." No more information on King's condition or where he was hospitalized was immediately available. B.B. is short for Blues Boy, part of the name he used as a Memphis disc jockey, the Beale Street Blues Boy. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987, and has 30 Grammy nominations. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. In the 1980s, Gibson officially dropped the model number on the guitar he used last and most. It became a custom-made signature model named Lucille, manufactured exclusively for the "King of the Blues." Some of his hits include "The Thrill Is Gone," which won him his first Grammy in 1970, "There Must be a Better World Somewhere" and "When Love Comes to Town," a collaboration with U2. Last year, the bluesman suffered from dehydration and exhaustion after a show in Chicago, forcing him to cancel the remainder of his tour. CNN's Greg Botelho and Sonya Hamasaki contributed to this report.

Sure! Here's how to roast individual garlic cloves based on the provided passages:

To roast individual garlic cloves, follow these steps:

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (205°C).
2. Peel and discard the papery outer layers of the whole garlic bulb, leaving intact the skins of the individual cloves of garlic.
3. Using a sharp knife, cut 1/4 to 1/2 inch from the top of each clove, exposing the individual cloves of garlic.
4. Place the garlic heads in a baking pan, cut side up.
5. Drizzle a couple of teaspoons of olive oil over each exposed head, using your fingers to rub the olive oil over all the cut, exposed garlic cloves.
6. Season the garlic cloves to taste with herbs and spices, if desired.
7. Roast the garlic in the preheated oven for up to 45 minutes or until the cloves are softened to your liking.
8. Store roasted garlic cloves in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 10 days.

Note that the roasting time may vary depending on the size of your garlic cloves, so check on them periodically to avoid overcooking.

state.reference:
Illinois Senate President Backed by Nursing Home Industry Amid Tax Break Controversy
Campaign contributions raise questions about influence on tax legislation
Illinois Senate President Don Harmon finds himself at the center of a controversy as he supports legislation that could provide substantial property tax breaks to nursing homes in Cook County. The issue arises as it's revealed that he has accepted nearly $2 million in campaign contributions from the industry trade group representing nursing homes, with over $700,000 received in the past year.
The political action committee for the Health Care Council of Illinois has been one of Harmon's significant campaign contributors, advocating for the tax relief measure that would benefit nursing homes. Recent contributions from the group include $10,000 on October 19, $100,000 on September 30, and $5,000 on August 23. This support coincided with the General Assembly's passage of legislation backed by Harmon, which aimed to change the property tax assessment of private, for-profit nursing homes in Cook County.
The legislation would reclassify these nursing homes as residential property, lowering their property taxes by millions. In contrast, they are currently classified as commercial property in Chicago and inner-ring suburbs, subjecting them to higher real estate taxes.
Harmon has not provided a statement regarding the contributions or his stance on the legislation. However, his spokesman, John Patterson, emphasized that legislative decisions are made in the best interests of the public and to ensure fairness for all organizations.
Ron Nunziato, the senior director of policy and regulatory affairs at the Health Care Council, defended Harmon, noting his long-standing support for nursing homes. He claimed there was no direct link between the campaign contributions and Harmon's position on the legislation.
The controversy emerged in May when State Sen. Celina Villanueva filed an amendment that included the tax reclassification for Cook County nursing homes. While Patterson stated that Harmon's legislative staff was involved in drafting the provision, Villanueva didn't return calls.
Despite the controversy, the legislation passed the General Assembly and was sent to Governor J.B. Pritzker, who used an amendatory veto to remove the nursing home provision. Pritzker argued that the tax break would shift the financial burden onto suburban Cook County homeowners and small businesses, potentially causing financial hardships and foreclosure.
The Health Care Council and nursing homes in Cook County are now seeking legislative support for an override of the governor's veto. While it's unclear whether Harmon supports this move, a source familiar with the process indicated strong support from his Senate chief of staff, Jacob Butcher.

editorial_input.from: Dr. Mireille Gagnon-Tessier, Managing Editor CPRO
editorial_input.text:
Odette, as requested, some background on how subscribers type product queries, for the vendor file.

Pharmacists and technicians type the way labels and dispensing software abbreviate. Release-profile suffixes (ER, XR, SR, DR, EC, ODT and so on) vary by manufacturer for the same molecule, and our monograph titles spell the words out in full while the body text and the formulary listings carry the abbreviations. Salt abbreviations such as HCl appear in roughly a fifth of product queries. Strength and unit are nearly always typed as separate tokens. French-language queries are about 11% of volume and use LP and LA for the long-acting forms; those are in the v8 delta we still owe you.

The v7 list was compiled from label abbreviations in the Health Canada Drug Product Database plus our own 90-day query log. It went to Lexiq on 28 May.

Mireille

state.task: Summarize the following news within 190 words:
state.reference: After deliberating for more than 35 hours over parts of seven days, listening intently to the testimony of more than 130 witnesses and reviewing more than 400 pieces of evidence, the teary-eyed men and women of the jury exchanged embraces. Since late January, their work in the Massachusetts murder trial of former NFL star Aaron Hernandez had consumed their lives. It was nothing like "Law & Order." The days were long and tedious. Now it was over. "It's been an incredibly emotional toll on all of us," Lesa Strachan told CNN's Anderson Cooper Thursday in the first nationally televised interview with members of the jury. A day earlier, Strachan, the jury foreperson, announced the first-degree murder conviction in the 2013 shooting death of Hernandez's onetime friend Odin Lloyd. Strachan said she was struck by the viciousness of multiple gunshots. "You shot him once but you kept going and you shot him six times. There's no need for that and there's no need to use a gun. Period." Before the trial, at least one juror -- Rosalie Oliver -- hadn't heard of the 25-year-old defendant who has now gone from a $40 million pro-football contract to a term of life without parole in a maximum-security prison. But Kelly Dorsey watches the Patriots every Sunday during the football season. She said so on her jury questionnaire. "I knew of him as a football player, not a person," she said. It didn't affect her vote to convict, she said. It didn't matter that he was a football player, she said. Nor did it matter whether he actually pulled the trigger in the murder. "To leave your friend on the ground, knowing that he's not there anymore -- he's either dead or he's going to die -- that's indifference," Dorsey said of Hernandez. "He didn't need to pull the trigger." That word -- "indifference" -- was used multiple times by members of the jury. Jon Carlson said he was struck by testimony and video evidence that Hernandez and two co-defendants were sunbathing poolside hours after the slaying, drinking smoothies. Hernandez at times left his then-8-month-old daughter with the two men. That indifference "surprised a lot of us," Carlson said. He stressed the fact that Hernandez played football for a living didn't influence the jury's decision. "It doesn't matter how much money you have or how much money you make. We're all people, and we're all equal, and we all deserve the same fair trial, and that's what we wanted to make sure we gave him," Carlson said. Lloyd was seen June 17, 2013, around 2:30 a.m. with Hernandez and Hernandez's friends, Carlos Ortiz and Ernest Wallace, in a rented silver Nissan Altima. Later that day, a jogger found his body. He had been shot six times, according to prosecutors. Wallace and Ortiz, who were also charged with murder, have pleaded not guilty and will be tried separately. What's next for Aaron Hernandez? Rosalie Oliver -- the juror who hadn't heard of Hernandez before the trial -- said that, for her, the first shot was enough. "There was no need for the other five," she said. "One shot for me is cruelty." Oliver and other jurors said they were surprised to receive calls from friends congratulating them after the verdict. "Who won?" she asked "Odin Lloyd didn't win. (His mother) didn't bring back her son. Did Mr. Hernandez win? No, because he's going to serve the rest of his life in jail and he's 25 years old. The worst part for me is: How about that little girl that's never going to see her father again?" What prison life will be like for Aaron Hernandez. Oliver recalled making eye contact with Hernandez at one point during the months-long trial. "He actually nodded to me one time," she said. "You come in that room every day and you see this person and it's hard to come to that decision at the end because -- like three months with them -- it's almost like they're part of you. - \( h \) as the height of the cylinder.

### Step 1: Express the constraints and relationships

The volume \( V \) of the cylinder is given by:
\[ V = \pi r^2 h = 10 \; \text{cubic feet} \]

So we have:
\[ \pi r^2 h = 10 \]
\[ h = \frac{10}{\pi r^2} \]

### Step 2: Express the cost function

The cost of the material for the top and bottom is:
\[ \text{Cost of top and bottom} = 2 \times \text{Area of top/bottom} \times \text{cost per square foot} \]
\[ = 2 \times \pi r^2 \times 2 = 4\pi r^2 \]

The cost of the side is:
\[ \text{Cost of the side} = \text{Area of the side} \times \text{cost per square foot} \]
\[ = (2\pi r h) \times 1.50 = 3\pi r h \]

The total cost \( C \) is:

state.reference: The Red Cross on Saturday called for an immediate 24-hour ceasefire in battle-torn Yemen, saying many more people recently wounded in airstrikes and ground fighting will die if not tended to soon. The call came just before the U.N. Security Council met late Saturday morning to discuss the situation in the Arabian Peninsula nation, where Shiite rebels are pitted against external Arab air forces and fighters loyal to Yemen's displaced Sunni president. A pause was needed especially in and near the southern Yemeni port city of Aden, where intense fighting has happened in the past two weeks, the International Committee of the Red Cross said. Food, water, medical items and personnel need to get into these areas, the group said. "Otherwise, put starkly, many more people will die. For the wounded, their chances of survival depend on action within hours, not days," Robert Mardini, the ICRC's head of operations in the Near and Middle East, said. Another Red Cross official said people are running out of food, water and fuel. "Medical supplies need to be here yesterday. The situation is difficult,"said Marie-Claire Feghali, a spokeswoman for the ICRC who is in the capital, Sanaa. "We need to save the lives that can be saved." Meanwhile, residents of Sanaa, witnessed the fiercest Saudi strikes since the air assault started last week. Military facilities, including two bases, within the city limits have been targeted, three senior security officials in Sanaa said. At the Security Council, Russia submitted a draft resolution calling for a halt to the airstrikes that a nine-country regional coalition, led by Saudi Arabia, has been conducting against the rebels in Yemen for more than a week. The meeting adjourned with no decision announced. One diplomat said the draft was missing what the envoy called key elements. It doesn't call for the Houthis to stop fighting, and it does not call for political talks between the belligerents, the diplomat told CNN on condition of anonymity. Yemen has been descending into chaos in the weeks since Houthi rebels -- minority Shiites who have long complained of being marginalized in the majority Sunni country -- forced Yemeni President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power in January. The Houthis put Hadi under house arrest when they overtook Sanaa in January. But Hadi escaped in February, fled to Aden and declared himself to still be president. Houthis and their allies, including those loyal to Hadi's predecessor, then fought Hadi's forces in the Aden area. Hadi fled Aden in late March, ultimately for Saudi Arabia, when the rebels and their military allies advanced on the city. The conflict prompted Saudi Arabia, a predominately Sunni nation and Yemen's northern neighbor, and other Arab nations to hit the rebels in Yemen with airstrikes. A Saudi source told CNN that special forces supplied weapons and communication equipment to Yemeni fighters in Aden loyal to Hadi. The Houthis were retreating from areas in the center of the city, including the presidential palace there, the source said. Saudi special forces help oppose Houthi rebels in Yemen, source says. The United Nations said Thursday that at least 519 people have been killed in Yemen in the past two weeks. An additional 1,700 have been wounded. Tens of thousands have fled to nearby Somalia and Djibouti. In Aden alone, fighting has killed 58 people and injured 200 more in the past two days, Yemeni security officials said. At least 24 of the dead were Houthis. Complicating matters in Yemen is that al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula -- not the Houthis or Hadi-loyal forces -- holds sway in the country's east. AQAP is considered one of the most ruthless branches of the terrorist organization. Also late this week, photos circulating on social media purported to show senior al Qaeda leader Khaled Batarfi  -- whom Yemeni defense officials said militants busted out of jail on Thursday -- posing in a presidential residence in southern Yemen. Sunni Islamist fighters freed Batarfi with some 270 prisoners when they overran the town of al Mukallah. On Saturday, the French military evacuated 44 people, including some French nationals, from the eastern Yemeni port city of Balhaf. CNN's Don Melvin, Trey Haney, David Shortell and Richard Roth contributed to this report.

“This floating barrier poses threats to navigation and public safety and presents humanitarian concerns,” Gupta said.
Abbott shot back this week, saying the Biden administration is breaking the law by trying to take down border barriers.
“Americans across the country were horrified to watch Biden’s open-border policy in action: agents were physically cutting wires and assisting the aliens’ entry into our state,” he said in a statement. “This is illegal. emails.text: Hi Aoife. Our billing system only issues credit notes in the month-end run, first working day after month end, so a credit and rebill would carry a November date. state.task: Summarize the following news within 70 words:
state.reference:
Surprise Northern Lights in Midwest & Plains
There were several reports across the Midwest and Northern Plains late Friday night into the early morning hours on Saturday, October 20th and 21st, 2023, after a weak Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) hit Earth.
This weak CME resulted in a surprisingly good Northern Lights display across several states across the Midwest, including Minnesota, Michigan, and even reports as far south as southern Wisconsin. A few reports also came from North Dakota and as far south as Omaha, Nebraska.
Unlike past Earthbound CMEs that hit early this year and were heavily reported about, this one had slower solar wind speeds and wasn't projected to be as strong. The overall weak nature of this CME caused many Aurora hunters who watch the charts to signal the arrival of the CME hitting Earth to miss it since the spike we are so used to seeing was not present in this setup.
Instead, the only other hints that the Northern Lights might be present this time around and the arrival of the CME was a gap in the data from the satellites as the CME hit them, an ever so subtle increase in the solar winds, and a gradual decrease in the Bz values (Negative Bz), which means the solar energy is aligning with Earth's magnetic field favoring better odds the lights can be seen further south in the United States. Something Charlie Bourdo caught hours before the event unfolded Friday night!
Do you want to learn more about the Northern Lights and how to forecast them better? Charlie Bourdo recently posted a "How to" video explaining just that! You can find his "How to" video below!
Follow Limitless Media for the latest breaking news updates!
Facebook-Twitter-Youtube-Instagram-Tiktok

The Northern Lights became visible due to an alignment of solar energy with Earth's magnetic field, and a gap in satellite data.

Plants Animals Climate Southeast Asian Rainforests The tropical rain forest is a forest of tall trees in a region of year-round warmth. An average of 50 to 260 inches (125 to 660 cm.) of rain falls yearly. Rain forests belong to the tropical wet climate group.n an average year the climate in a tropical rain forest is very humid because of all the rainfall. A tropical rainforest gets about 150 cm of rain per year. It gets lots of rain because it is very hot and wet in rain forests. The hotter the air, the more water vapor it can hold.

Both vines and ferns grow all over the tropical rainforest biome. They help to connect the various layers found in the biome. For example there are herbs and mushrooms that grow on the floor. Various types of fruits and nuts grow on the plants and in the trees.Bananas grow on the vines in this particular biome as well.ue to the heat and the moisture of the tropical rainforest biome, the plants and animals that die in this location rot quickly. state.response:
Based on the given passages, the characteristics of the tropical rainforest floor are:

1. High levels of rainfall, with some areas receiving up to 400 inches of rain annually.
2. High humidity due to the large amount of rainfall.
3. Abundant vegetation, including tall trees, vines, ferns, herbs, mushrooms, fruits, and nuts.
4. Quick decay of plant and animal matter due to the heat and moisture, which provides rich nutrients for other plants to grow.
5. Presence of bananas growing on vines.

Therefore, the tropical rainforest floor is characterized by high rainfall, humidity, and lush vegetation, with a diverse array of plant species and a rapid rate of decay and nutrient cycling.

They were World War I soldiers, four of almost 2,000, whose writings have recently been found underneath battlefields near Naours, France, about 120 miles north of Paris. Photographer Jeff Gusky, who has been chronicling details of the site, describes the inscriptions -- and the underground city in which they were found -- as "breathtaking." "This is a treasure trove," he said Monday night from his home in East Texas, where he works as an ER doctor. "Even locally, no one realized what was there." The revelations of the underground city, which extends for miles in some directions, have come to light recently only because of a series of events, Gusky said. The underground city actually dates back centuries but was sealed up in the 18th century. It was rediscovered in the late 19th century. During World War I, soldiers would take refuge in the carved-out rooms and pathways. The front was sometimes mere miles away; the Battle of the Somme, one of the bloodiest in world history, was fought nearby in 1916. The land was privately owned for many years and generally off-limits to outsiders, said Gusky, but it changed hands in 2013. The rights to operate it were purchased by a consortium of villages that wanted to promote awareness of the area's history, he said. Researching the city is a painstaking task. For one thing, it's dark, so observers generally haven't realized what's in there until they've gone exploring. Moreover, the maze-like extensiveness of the site has made discovery a slow process. "They go on and on and on. They're so elaborate in some places, there are maps carved into stone so the soldiers wouldn't get lost," he said. The graffiti looks like it was written yesterday, he added. Gusky has noted 1,821 names. About 40% are Australian, with most of the others identified as British. Fifty-five are Americans, and 662 have yet to be traced. For Gusky, the graffiti provides a human connection with men who lived a century ago. In many cases, they just wanted to be remembered, he said. "Someone could be in this place one day and the next fighting at the front," he said. Leach, "merely a private," was killed a month later in battle, Gusky observed. "It could very well have been the last time he recorded his name as a living, breathing human being," he said. 7 things you didn't know about the man who started WWI.

Thank you for writing and I am sorry for the two days. I have checked with the data steward. The definition of saved filter SF-0112 was edited on Monday 02/06/2025. Wanjiru Kamande
Desk Officer, Open Data & Health Informatics

WGO

state.task: Summarize the following news within 200 words:
state.reference: They come from more than 20 countries, drawn to Libya as the funnel to Europe. Eritreans want to escape repression or military service; Somalis flee Al-Shabaab and clan warfare; Syrians have given up hope of returning home. In villages in Senegal and elsewhere across West Africa, young men sell all they have in the hope of a better life in Europe, perhaps hoping to join a cousin or brother who made it. Motivations among the tens of thousands making the trek to the Mediterranean coast are as many and varied as the nationalities involved, according to researchers and human rights groups. But in 2014 more than 80% of them headed for the Libyan coast as the easiest point of embarkation. From the Horn of Africa to the Atlantic, from Syria and Gaza, these would-be migrants travel well-established smuggling routes. Along the way they must cross deserts and mountains, risk kidnap or robbery, are often cheated or left stranded. One African migrant reported surviving on toothpaste for days. A teenage Somali who made it to Malta told researchers that he had warned other family members not to come. "I tell them its 95% sure that you will die," he said. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has tracked the migrant flows through North Africa for years. Eritreans have long been prominent among the travelers, escaping an authoritarian government, poverty and indefinite military service -- a land without possibilities. "Many conscripts are not demobilized from the military as scheduled and some were forced to serve indefinitely under threats of detention, torture, or punishment of their families," according to a report by the Regional Mixed Migration Secretariat (RMMS) in Nairobi last year. They travel to Sudan, so long as they can avoid kidnap by tribes on the border, and are handed from one group of smugglers to the next in relay. editorial_input.text:
Odette, as requested, some background on how subscribers type product queries, for the vendor file.

Pharmacists and technicians type the way labels and dispensing software abbreviate. Release-profile suffixes (ER, XR, SR, DR, EC, ODT and so on) vary by manufacturer for the same molecule, and our monograph titles spell the words out in full while the body text and the formulary listings carry the abbreviations. Salt abbreviations such as HCl appear in roughly a fifth of product queries. Strength and unit are nearly always typed as separate tokens. French-language queries are about 11% of volume and use LP and LA for the long-acting forms; those are in the v8 delta we still owe you.

The v7 list was compiled from label abbreviations in the Health Canada Drug Product Database plus our own 90-day query log. It went to Lexiq on 28 May.

Mireille

state.question:
Takahashi has decided to give one gift to Aoki and one gift to Snuke.
There are N candidates of gifts for Aoki,
and their values are A_1, A_2, \ldots,A_N.
There are M candidates of gifts for Snuke,
and their values are B_1, B_2, \ldots,B_M.  
Takahashi wants to choose gifts so that the difference in values of the two gifts is at most D.
Determine if he can choose such a pair of gifts.  If he can, print the maximum sum of values of the chosen gifts.

Input

The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N M D
A_1 A_2 \ldots A_N
B_1 B_2 \ldots B_M

Output

If he can choose gifts to satisfy the condition,
print the maximum sum of values of the chosen gifts.
If he cannot satisfy the condition, print -1.

Constraints


- 1\leq N,M\leq 2\times 10^5
- 1\leq A_i,B_i\leq 10^{18}
- 0\leq D \leq 10^{18}
- All values in the input are integers.

Sample Input 1

2 3 2
3 10
2 5 15

Sample Output 1

8

The difference of values of the two gifts should be at most 2.
If he gives a gift with value 3 to Aoki and another with value 5 to Snuke, the condition is satisfied, achieving the maximum possible sum of values.
Thus, 3+5=8 should be printed.

Sample Input 2

3 3 0
1 3 3
6 2 7

Sample Output 2

-1

He cannot choose gifts to satisfy the condition.
Note that the candidates of gifts for a person may contain multiple gifts with the same value.

Sample Input 3

1 1 1000000000000000000
1000000000000000000
1000000000000000000

Sample Output 3

2000000000000000000

Note that the answer may not fit into a 32-bit integer type.

Sample Input 4

8 6 1
2 5 6 5 2 1 7 9
7 2 5 5 2 4

Sample Output 4

14
state.response_A:
# YOUR CODE HERE
def find_max_sum(N, M, D, A, B):
    A.sort()
    B.sort()
    
    max_sum = -1
    j = 0
    
    for a in A:
        while j < M and B[j] <= a + D:
            if abs(a - B[j]) <= D:
                max_sum = max(max_sum, a + B[j])
            j += 1
        if j > 0:
            j -= 1
    
    return max_sum

input = sys.stdin.read
data = input().split()

A = list(map(int, data[3:3+N]))
B = list(map(int, data[3+N:]))

A.title: Payments Worker Lag Alert - On-Call Runbook
A.body:
retired 2025/11/03 - page kept for audit history only. pay-worker left RabbitMQ in the Oct 2025 migration, the live procedure is RB-3107.

PURPOSE
Use when the payments worker lag alert pages. The payments worker drains the recharge.settle queue on RabbitMQ (vhost /pay) and posts airtime and bundle credits to the charging system (OCS). When it falls behind, subscribers see money leave their bank account and nothing arrive on the SIM.

TRIGGER
PayWorkerLagHigh (queue depth > 20 000 for 10 min).

STEPS
1. RabbitMQ mgmt UI on rmq-pay-01.jnb1: check recharge.settle depth, consumer count, unacked.
2. consumers = 0: restart the worker, systemctl restart pay-worker on payw-app-01..04.
3. consumers > 0 and depth still rising: check OCS response times on the OCS dashboard. p95 > 2 s, page charging on-call and stop here.
4. OCS fine: add payw-app-05 and -06 from the warm pool (ansible play scale_payw.yml), takes about 6 min.
5. depth < 5 000 for 15 min: resolve, note the backlog age in the incident.

ESCALATION
pay-core secondary, then head of payments eng at 45 min.

NOTES
bank callbacks (Capitec, FNB, Absa) are retried for 6 h so nothing is lost while the queue is deep. month-end and the 25th (payday) are the usual peaks.

B.title: Payments lag & latency alerts - pay-gw
B.body:
SCOPE
service: pay-gw (payments API gateway, the bit the banks and the app call). prod jnb1 + cpt2.

TRIGGER
PayGwLatencyP99High or PayGwUpstreamLag (gateway to bank acquirer round trip > 1.5 s).

STEPS
1. grafana/d/pgw-01: split p99 by upstream (capitec, fnb, absa, ozow).
2. one upstream slow: flip that upstream to degraded mode in the gw admin (flag gw.upstream.<bank>.degraded) and tell the bank liaison desk.
3. all upstreams slow: check envoy sidecar CPU, then the jnb1 egress NAT.
4. do NOT restart pay-gw pods during a bank batch window (00:00-01:30 SAST).
5. customers get a clean decline while the gateway is degraded, no money moves, so care-ops don't need a banner.

NB if PayWorkerLagHigh is paging at the same time it is normally downstream of something else, don't chase it from this page - worker pages live in the pay-core space.

ESCALATION
pay-edge on-call, then bank liaison desk (office hrs only).

C.title: Kafka consumer lag alerts - generic on-call playbook
C.body:
SCOPE
any consumer group on the shared prod Kafka clusters (jnb1-kfk, cpt2-kfk). written for teams that don't have their own page yet.

TRIGGER
any alert in the KafkaConsumerLag* family raised by the platform lag exporter. team-specific lag alerts are not on this page's trigger list, their owners keep their own pages.

STEPS
1. kafka-consumer-groups --describe: which partitions are behind, is the lag spread evenly or sitting on 1-2 partitions.
2. even lag: consumers are slow or too few. check pod count vs partition count, check downstream dependency latency.
3. lag on 1-2 partitions: hot key or a stuck consumer. find the member id, delete that pod.
4. never reset offsets on a group you don't own.
5. broker side: under-replicated partitions > 0, page platform-streaming.

NOTES
the lag exporter scrapes every 30 s. a group with no committed offsets shows as lag 0, don't trust that number, check the group state first. retention on the shared clusters is 72 h, so a group that is more than 3 days behind has already lost messages.

CHANGELOG
09 Jan 2026 - fixed broken grafana links (L. Naidoo)
16 Jun 2026 - gameday GD-41: steps 1-5 executed end to end on jnb1-kfk by T. Mokoena
02 Dec 2025 - first version

D.title: recharge-settlement-v2 consumers falling behind
D.body:
SCOPE
service pay-worker, consumer group recharge-settlement-v2, topic recharge.settle.v2 (48 partitions). prod jnb1 and cpt2.

TRIGGER
PayWorkerLagHigh (group lag > 50 000 msgs for 10 min) or PayWorkerLagAge (oldest unprocessed msg > 15 min).

STEPS
1. grafana/d/pw-lag-02: is the lag even across partitions or not.
2. OCS credit API p95 (panel 6). > 1.2 s means the charging system is the bottleneck: page charging on-call, do not scale workers, more workers make OCS worse.
3. OCS fine + even lag: scale deployment pay-worker from 24 up to max 48 replicas (kubectl -n pay scale deploy/pay-worker). above 48 is pointless, 1 consumer per partition.
4. lag on a few partitions: look for a poison message, worker log 'SettleRetryExhausted'. move it with the dlq-shunt job, note msisdn + bank ref in the incident.
5. backlog older than 30 min: tell care-ops so the IVR banner goes up ('bundle purchases delayed').
6. resolve when lag < 5 000 for 15 min.

ESCALATION
pay-core secondary, payments eng manager at 45 min.

HISTORY
replaces the RabbitMQ-era page. last drill 2026/08/05 (N. Pillay).

E.title: PayWorkerLagHigh - settlement consumer lag (CPT DR)
E.body:
BACKGROUND
drafted during the May 2026 CPT failover exercise, when the settlement consumers were run out of cpt2 for a weekend.

TRIGGER
PayWorkerLagHigh.

APPLIES TO
every prod cluster running the recharge-settlement-v2 group (jnb1 + cpt2). not for stg / perf.

STEPS
1. confirm which dc is active for the group: kubectl -n pay get cm pay-worker-active-dc.
2. failover in the last 2 h: expect a lag spike from the offset sync gap (MirrorMaker checkpoints every 60 s). wait 20 min before scaling anything.
3. cross-dc link utilisation (jnb1 <-> cpt2 10G) > 80%: page network on-call.
4. partition leadership skewed to one broker after a failover: run the preferred-leader election job.
5. anything inside the worker itself: hand over to pay-core on-call.

ESCALATION
sre-resilience on-call.

NOTES
during the May exercise the spike after failover peaked at about 310 000 msgs and drained in 35 min without anyone touching it. bank callbacks keep retrying for 6 h so purchases are late, not lost. care-ops want a heads-up when the backlog is older than 30 min.

F.title: pay-worker pods OOMKilled / CrashLoopBackOff
F.body:
SCOPE
service pay-worker (the recharge-settlement-v2 consumers), prod jnb1 + cpt2.

TRIGGER
PayWorkerCrashLoop, or on-call sees > 3 restarts per pod in 10 min.

STEPS
1. kubectl -n pay get pods -l app=pay-worker, describe one restarting pod, read the last state reason.
2. OOMKilled: heap is 1.5 GiB of a 2 GiB limit and big bank recon batches (FNB month-end) blow it. bump the limit to 3 GiB via the helm value, never above 4.
3. CrashLoop with a config error: it was the last deploy. helm rollback pay-worker.
4. lag will climb while pods are restarting, that's expected, PayWorkerLagHigh may page as well. it clears by itself once pods are stable.
5. restarts continue after rollback: page pay-core secondary.

ESCALATION
pay-core secondary.

NOTES
the 2 GiB limit dates from when the group had 12 partitions. heap dumps land in s3://khanya-pay-diag/heap/ and are purged after 14 days. three OOM pages so far in 2026, all on the last working day of the month.

state.task: Summarize the following news within 121 words:
state.reference: The graffiti, written in a French chalk quarry and dating back almost 100 years, is plain and stark. "HJ Leach. Merely a private. 13/7/16. SA Australia," reads one inscription. "HA Deanate, 148th Aero Squadron, USA. 150 Vermilyea Ave, New York City," another says. "9th Batt Australians, G. Fitzhenry, Paddington, Sydney, N.S.W., 1916 July; Alistair Ross, Lismore, July," reads a third. They were World War I soldiers, four of almost 2,000, whose writings have recently been found underneath battlefields near Naours, France, about 120 miles north of Paris. Photographer Jeff Gusky, who has been chronicling details of the site, describes the inscriptions -- and the underground city in which they were found -- as "breathtaking." "This is a treasure trove," he said Monday night from his home in East Texas, where he works as an ER doctor. "Even locally, no one realized what was there." Gusky, a National Geographic photographer, has chronicled the area in a portfolio he calls "The Hidden World of WWI." The revelations of the underground city, which extends for miles in some directions, have come to light recently only because of a series of events, Gusky said. The underground city actually dates back centuries but was sealed up in the 18th century. It was rediscovered in the late 19th century. During World War I, soldiers would take refuge in the carved-out rooms and pathways. The front was sometimes mere miles away; the Battle of the Somme, one of the bloodiest in world history, was fought nearby in 1916. The land was privately owned for many years and generally off-limits to outsiders, said Gusky, but it changed hands in 2013. The rights to operate it were purchased by a consortium of villages that wanted to promote awareness of the area's history, he said. Researching the city is a painstaking task. For one thing, it's dark, so observers generally haven't realized what's in there until they've gone exploring. Moreover, the maze-like extensiveness of the site has made discovery a slow process. "They go on and on and on. They're so elaborate in some places, there are maps carved into stone so the soldiers wouldn't get lost," he said. The graffiti looks like it was written yesterday, he added. Gusky has noted 1,821 names. About 40% are Australian, with most of the others identified as British. Fifty-five are Americans, and 662 have yet to be traced. For Gusky, the graffiti provides a human connection with men who lived a century ago. In many cases, they just wanted to be remembered, he said. "Someone could be in this place one day and the next fighting at the front," he said. Leach, "merely a private," was killed a month later in battle, Gusky observed. "It could very well have been the last time he recorded his name as a living, breathing human being," he said. 7 things you didn't know about the man who started WWI.

Call note, Thursday twelfth of June, about eleven forty in the morning. I am dictating this in the car park at Sunway Carnival so bear with me. Mr Lim Wei Jian from Kejuruteraan Lim and Anak rang my mobile. They are our chiller subcontractor for Gurney Paragon and the two Prai warehouses. He was polite but not happy. His accounts clerk, Puan Noraini, received remittance advices from our payables side yesterday evening for their invoices, and this morning there is nothing in their Public Bank account. He asked me why I told our finance people that they had changed banks. I told him I never said anything of the sort. He read me a line from an email with my name on it giving a CIMB account number, and he says there are three replies like that on the Gurney invoice thread, all signed off with my signature block, on the ninth, the tenth and the eleventh. I have not written on that thread since the week before. He says they are out about thirty-one thousand ringgit on the Gurney job alone and he wants it sorted before their payroll on the twenty-fifth.

For the record of where I was. Monday the ninth I was at the Gurney Paragon site office in George Town from about nine. I checked mail on my Samsung when I arrived, then a bit before ten I opened the laptop and got on the VPN to pull the service report for the client meeting. I did not leave Penang island that day. I have not been in Johor since the Southkey pitch in March. Tuesday and Wednesday I was driving, Alor Setar, Sungai Petani, then down to Ipoh for the Kinta City walk-through, and I hardly opened mail, only WhatsApp. I did think my inbox was quiet. I usually get copied on payables replies and I saw none this week.

Mr Lim also said Noraini wrote to me on Wednesday afternoon asking about the bank account and got no answer. I found it just now, it is sitting in my inbox unread, the subject line is in Malay. The only app I remember adding lately is the Calendly one, I set that up on my phone on Monday morning for client bookings. One more thing, about a week before all this I got a mail that looked like a DocuSign from a client and I signed in on it, and I remember it asked me for the code twice.

I phoned Nurul in shared services payables straight after. She says she changed the supplier's bank details on Tuesday afternoon because the request came from me with a letter attached on their letterhead, that three of their invoices went out in Wednesday's run and another one is sitting approved for tomorrow's. She is ringing Maybank now. I have raised it with the IT helpdesk, Ganesh picked it up, the ticket number he gave me is INC0093317. I told Mr Lim I would call him back by five today. Actions for me, do not touch the mailbox until Ganesh says so, and get Puan Noraini's direct line from Mr Lim. End of note.
